title.en: Volume 30 Biographies 18: Lu Xuan, Lu Rou, Lu Guan, Lu Tong, Lu Dan
title.raw: 卷三十 列傳第十八: 盧玄 盧柔 盧觀 盧同 盧誕 Volume 30 Biographies 18: Lu Xuan, Lu Rou, Lu Guan, Lu Tong, Lu Dan

sentences.zh: 盧玄 盧柔 盧觀 盧同 盧誕

translations.literal: Lu Xuan, Lu Rou, Lu Guan, Lu Tong, Lu Dan
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan, Lu Rou, Lu Guan, Lu Tong, and Lu Dan

sentences.zh: 列傳第十八

translations.literal: Biographies 18
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 18

sentences.zh: 盧玄玄孫思道昌衡元明潛盧柔子愷盧觀弟仲宣彪從子文偉盧同子斐兄子景裕景裕弟辯光光子賁光從弟勇盧誕

translations.literal: Lu Xuan, great-grandson Sidao, Changheng, Yuanming, Qian; Lu Rou, son Kai; Lu Guan, younger brother Zhongxuan, Biao, nephew Wenwei; Lu Tong, son Fei, elder brother's son Jingyu; Jingyu's younger brothers Bian, Guang, son Ben; Guang's younger cousin Yong; Lu Dan
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan; his great-grandson Sidao, Changheng, Yuanming, and Qian; Lu Rou and son Kai; Lu Guan, brothers Zhongxuan and Biao, and nephew Wenwei; Lu Tong and son Fei, and brother's son Jingyu; Jingyu's brothers Bian and Guang, Guang's son Ben, and Guang's cousin Yong; and Lu Dan

sentences.zh: 盧玄，字子真，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Xuan, styled Zizhen, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan, styled Zizhen, came from Zhuo in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖諶，晉司空劉琨從事中郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chen was Attendant Gentleman to Jin Minister of Works Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chen had served Liu Kun, Jin's Minister of Works, as Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 祖偃，父邈，並仁慕容氏。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yan and father Miao both entered the service of the Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan and father Miao both took office under the Murong.

sentences.zh: 偃為營丘太守，邈為范陽太守，皆以儒雅稱。

translations.literal: Yan was Administrator of Yingqiu and Miao Administrator of Fanyang; both were famed for scholarly refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Yan governed Yingqiu and Miao Fanyang, each renowned for cultured learning.

sentences.zh: 神蒨四年，太武辟召天下儒俊，以玄為首。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shenqi, Emperor Taiwu summoned eminent scholars empire-wide, with Xuan at their head.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenqi year 4, Taiwu called up the empire's leading scholars and placed Xuan first among them.

sentences.zh: 授中書博士，遷侍郎，本州大中正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, promoted to Gentleman, and made Grand Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He received the post of Secretariat Doctor, rose to Gentleman, and became his province's Grand Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 使馮弘，稱臣請附。

translations.literal: Sent to Feng Hong; he declared submission and asked to be received.
translations.idiomatic: On embassy to Feng Hong he offered allegiance and asked to join the court.

sentences.zh: 外兄司徒崔浩每與言輒歎曰：「對子真，使我懷古之情更深。

translations.literal: His cousin by marriage, Minister of Works Cui Hao, would sigh whenever they spoke: "Facing Zizhen deepens my longing for antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's brother Cui Hao, Minister of Works, would sigh in conversation: "In Zizhen's company my nostalgia for the ancients grows keener.

sentences.zh: 」浩大欲齊整人倫，分明姓族。

translations.literal: " Hao greatly wished to regularize human relations and clarify clan lines.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao was bent on ordering society and sorting surnames and lineages.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「創制立事，各有其時，樂為此者，詎幾人也？

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Establishing institutions each has its season; how many would delight in this?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan replied: "Founding customs and offices has its proper hour—how many would truly relish such work?

sentences.zh: 宜三思。

translations.literal: You should think thrice."
translations.idiomatic: Think thrice."

sentences.zh: 」浩當時雖無以異之，竟於不納。

translations.literal: Hao had no answer at the time, yet in the end he did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao could not refute him then, yet never took his advice.

sentences.zh: 浩敗，頗亦由此。

translations.literal: Hao's fall owed something to this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's ruin owed something to that refusal too.

sentences.zh: 後賜爵固安子，散騎常侍，使宋。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gu'an, made Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, and sent on embassy to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Viscount of Gu'an and Regular Attendant, then sent as envoy to Song.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝與之言，嘉歎良久，曰：「中郎，卿曾祖也！

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song spoke with him and praised him at length, saying: "The Palace Attendant—he was your great-grandfather!
translations.idiomatic: Song's Emperor Wen talked with him, admired him long, and said: "The Palace Attendant was your great-grandfather!

sentences.zh: 」還，遇疾，歸鄉卒。

translations.idiomatic: (end of quotation)

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、幽州刺史、固安侯，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: On his return he fell ill, went home to his district, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he fell ill, went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 子度世，字子遷。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of You Province, and Marquis of Gu'an; posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of You, and Marquis of Gu'an, with the temple name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 幼聰達，有計數。

translations.literal: His son Dushi, styled Ziqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dushi, styled Ziqian.

sentences.zh: 為中書學生，應選東宮。

translations.literal: Clever and quick as a child, with a gift for calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was sharp and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，與從兄遐俱以學行為時流所重。

translations.literal: A student of the Secretariat, he was selected for the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Secretariat and was chosen for the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 遐特為崔浩所敬，位至尚書、光祿大夫、范陽子。

translations.literal: At twenty he and his elder cousin Xia were both esteemed by the age for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he and cousin Xia won the day's respect for scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 度世後以崔浩事，棄官逃于高陽鄭羆家，羆匿之。

translations.literal: Xia was especially honored by Cui Hao and rose to Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Viscount of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xia in particular won Cui Hao's regard and reached Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Viscount of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 使者囚羆長子，將加捶楚。

translations.literal: Later, because of the Cui Hao affair, Dushi abandoned office and fled to the home of Zheng Pi of Gaoyang; Pi hid him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cui Hao affair broke, Dushi quit his post and hid with Zheng Pi of Gaoyang, who sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 羆誡之曰：「君子殺身以成仁，汝雖死勿言。

translations.literal: Envoys seized Pi's eldest son and were about to flog him.
translations.idiomatic: Officers seized Pi's eldest son to beat him.

sentences.zh: 」子奉父言，遂被拷掠，乃至火爇其體，因以物故，卒無所言。

translations.literal: Pi admonished him: "A gentleman dies to fulfill humaneness; though you die, do not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Pi warned him: "A gentleman gives his life for humaneness—die if you must, but say nothing."

sentences.zh: 度世後令弟娶羆妹，以報其恩。

translations.literal: The son obeyed his father, was tortured, even had fire applied to his body, died thereby, and to the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The boy obeyed, was tortured and even burned, died, and never spoke.

sentences.zh: 太武臨江，宋文使其殿上將軍黃延年至。

translations.literal: Later Dushi had his younger brother marry Pi's sister to repay the kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi later had a younger brother marry Pi's sister in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「盧度世坐與崔浩親通，逃命江表，應已至彼。

translations.literal: When Taiwu reached the Yangzi, Emperor Wen of Song sent his Palace General Huang Yannian.
translations.idiomatic: As Taiwu camped on the Yangzi, Song's emperor sent Palace General Huang Yannian.

sentences.zh: 」延年對曰：「都下無聞，當必不至。

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Lu Dushi, implicated with Cui Hao, fled south; he should have reached them by now."
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu asked: "Lu Dushi, close to Cui Hao, fled south—he must be there by now."

sentences.zh: 」帝詔東宮赦度世宗族逃亡籍沒者，度世乃出。

translations.literal: Yannian replied: "Nothing is heard in the capital; he surely has not gone."
translations.idiomatic: Yannian said: "The capital hears nothing; he surely never went."

sentences.zh: 拜中書侍郎，襲爵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Eastern Palace to pardon Dushi's clan for flight and confiscation; Dushi then came forth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from the Eastern Palace pardoned Dushi's fleeing kin; he emerged from hiding.

sentences.zh: 興安初，兼太常卿，立保太后父遼西獻王廟，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Secretariat Gentleman and inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 後除散騎侍郎，使宋，應對宋侍中柳元景失衷。

translations.literal: At the start of Xing'an he also served as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, erected the temple to the Liaoxi King, father of the Dowager Protector, and was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xing'an he doubled as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, built the temple to the Dowager Protector's father the Liaoxi King, and was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 還，被禁劾，經年乃釋。

translations.literal: Later removed as Regular Attendant, sent to Song; in replying to Song's Palace Attendant Liu Yuanjing he missed the tone.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Regular Attendant on embassy to Song and answered Palace Attendant Liu Yuanjing awkwardly.

sentences.zh: 除濟州刺史。

translations.literal: On return he was detained and impeached; only after a year was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he was held and impeached; a year passed before release.

sentences.zh: 州接邊境，將士數相侵掠。

translations.literal: He was made Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 度世乃禁勒所統，還其俘虜，二境以寧。

translations.literal: The province bordered foreign territory; officers and men often raided one another.
translations.idiomatic: The province lay on the frontier; troops on both sides kept raiding.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免。

translations.literal: Dushi restrained his command, returned captives, and both borders grew quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi tightened discipline, returned prisoners, and both sides calmed.

sentences.zh: 尋除青州刺史，未拜，卒，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was removed for a fault.

sentences.zh: 四子，伯源、敏、昶、尚之。

translations.literal: Soon after he was named Inspector of Qing but died before taking up the post; posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Inspector of Qing but died before assuming it; his posthumous name was Hui.

sentences.zh: 初，玄有五子，唯度世嫡，餘皆別生。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Boyuan, Min, Chang, and Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons: Boyuan, Min, Chang, and Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 崔浩之難，其庶兄弟恆欲害之，度世常深忿恨。

translations.literal: At first Xuan had five sons; only Dushi was legitimate, the rest born of concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had five sons; only Dushi was legitimate—the rest were by concubines.

sentences.zh: 及度世有子，每誡絕妾孽，以防後患。

translations.literal: In the Cui Hao disaster his half-brothers often wished to harm him; Dushi bore deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Cui Hao affair his half-brothers repeatedly tried to destroy him; he never forgave it.

sentences.zh: 至伯源兄弟，婢妾生子，雖形貌相類，皆不舉接。

translations.literal: When Dushi had sons he always warned them to cut off concubine offspring to guard against later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had sons he warned them to reject sons by slave women, lest trouble follow.

sentences.zh: 為識者所非。

translations.literal: With Boyuan's generation, when slave women bore sons who even resembled them, they would not acknowledge them.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan's generation would not acknowledge sons by maids even when the boys looked like them.

sentences.zh: 伯源小名陽烏，性溫雅寡欲，有祖父風。

translations.literal: Men of judgment criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: The knowing faulted them for it.

sentences.zh: 敦尚學業，閨門和睦。

translations.literal: Boyuan's childhood name was Yangwu; his nature was mild, refined, and free of craving, with his grandfather's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan, childhood name Yangwu, was gentle, cultured, and sparing of desire—his grandfather's air.

sentences.zh: 襲侯爵，降為伯。

translations.literal: He honored learning and kept the household harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished scholarship and kept the family at peace.

sentences.zh: 累加秘書監、本州大中正。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate, which was reduced to a barony.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate, later reduced to a barony.

sentences.zh: 時孝文帝將立馮後，先問伯源。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Secretariat and Grand Rectifier of his province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Secretariat Director and provincial Grand Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 請更簡卜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was about to install Lady Feng as empress he first consulted Boyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen meant to make Lady Feng empress he asked Boyuan first.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「以先後之侄，朕意已定。

translations.literal: Boyuan asked that divination be performed anew.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan asked for fresh divination.

sentences.zh: 」伯源曰：「雖奉敕如此，然臣心實有未盡。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "As niece of the empress dowager, my mind is set."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "She is the empress dowager's niece—my choice stands."

sentences.zh: 」及朝臣集議，執意如前。

translations.literal: Boyuan said: "Though I have received such an order, in my heart I am not fully satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan said: "I obey, yet my heart is not wholly at ease."

sentences.zh: 馮誕有盛寵，深以為恨，伯源不以介懷。

translations.literal: When the court gathered to debate he held to his view as before.
translations.idiomatic: At court debate he held the same line.

sentences.zh: 及孝文議伐齊，伯源表以為萬乘親戎，轉運難繼。

translations.literal: Feng Dan held great favor and deeply resented this; Boyuan did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan, deeply favored, hated him for it; Boyuan was unbothered.

sentences.zh: 詔雖不從，而優答之。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen debated attacking Qi, Boyuan memorialized that the Son of Heaven in person on campaign would make supply hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen planned war on Qi, Boyuan argued that the emperor's personal campaign would strain logistics.

sentences.zh: 尋以齊武帝殂，停師。

translations.literal: Though the edict was not followed, the reply was gracious.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not agree but answered him kindly.

sentences.zh: 時涇州羌叛，殘破城邑。

translations.literal: Soon Qi Emperor Wu died and the army halted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qi Emperor Wu died and the campaign stopped.

sentences.zh: 伯源以步騎六千號三萬，徐行而進。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang of Jing rebelled and ravaged towns.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qiang in Jing rebelled and smashed walled places.

sentences.zh: 未經三旬，賊眾逃散。

translations.literal: Boyuan took six thousand foot and horse, reported them as thirty thousand, and advanced slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan led six thousand foot and horse, claimed thirty thousand, and marched slowly.

sentences.zh: 降者數萬口，唯梟首惡，餘悉不問。

translations.literal: In less than thirty days the rebels scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Within thirty days the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔兼侍中。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands surrendered; only the ringleaders were beheaded, the rest not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands surrendered; only leaders were killed, the rest spared.

sentences.zh: 初，伯源年十四，嘗詣長安。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 將還，餞送者五十餘人，別於渭北。

translations.literal: Earlier, at fourteen, Boyuan had visited Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Boyuan had once visited Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 有相者扶風人王逵曰：「諸君皆不如此盧郎，雖位不副實，然得聲名甚盛，望逾公輔。

translations.literal: When he was to return, more than fifty people saw him off and parted north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, over fifty men saw him off north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 後二十餘年，當制命關右，願不相忘。

translations.literal: A physiognomist of Fufeng, Wang Kui, said: "None of you gentlemen equals this Lu lad; though rank may not match his worth, his fame will run very high, his prospects past the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The physiognomist Wang Kui of Fufeng said: "None of you matches this Lu youth—rank may lag talent, yet his name will thunder and his horizon exceed the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 」此行也，相者年過八十，詣軍門請見，言敘平生。

translations.literal: In twenty-odd years he will hold command west of the Pass; do not forget me."
translations.idiomatic: In twenty years he will govern the west—remember me."

sentences.zh: 未幾，守儀曹尚書。

translations.literal: On this campaign the physiognomist, past eighty, came to camp to see him and recalled their lives.
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign Kui, past eighty, came to camp, asked audience, and reminisced.

sentences.zh: 及齊雍州刺史曹武請降，乃以伯源為使持節、安南將軍，督前鋒諸軍，徑赴樊、鄧。

translations.literal: Before long he was Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 辭以儒生不行軍事，帝不許。

translations.literal: When Cao Wu, Inspector of Yong in Qi, asked to surrender, Boyuan was made Commissioner with Full Powers, General Who Pacifies the South, and commander of the vanguard, hurrying to Fan and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi's Yong inspector Cao Wu offered surrender, Boyuan was given full powers as General Who Pacifies the South to lead the vanguard to Fan and Deng.

sentences.zh: 伯源曰：「臣恐曹武為周魴耳。

translations.literal: He declined on the ground that a Confucian does not conduct warfare; the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded that a scholar should not wage war; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜審之。

translations.literal: Boyuan said: "I fear Cao Wu is another Zhou Fang."
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan said: "I fear Cao Wu is another Zhou Fang."

sentences.zh: 」武果偽降。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should examine this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should look closely."

sentences.zh: 伯源乃進攻赭陽，師敗，坐免官爵。

translations.literal: Wu indeed feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wu did feign surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋曹母憂。

translations.literal: Boyuan then attacked Zheyang, the army was defeated, and he was stripped of office and rank for it.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan attacked Zheyang, was beaten, and lost office and title.

sentences.zh: 服闋，兼太尉長史。

translations.literal: Soon Cao was in mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cao entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 後為徐州京兆王愉兼長史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended Boyuan served concurrently as Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 愉時年少，事無巨細，多決于伯源。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Clerk to Prince Yu of Xuzhou and Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was chief clerk to Prince Yu of Xuzhou and Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 伯源以誠信禦物，甚得東南人和。

translations.literal: Yu was then young; nothing large or small was decided without Boyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was young; Boyuan decided everything great or small.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史沈陵密謀叛，伯源屢有表聞，朝廷不納。

translations.literal: Boyuan governed men by sincerity and trust and won great goodwill in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled through sincerity and won the southeast's hearts.

sentences.zh: 陵果逃叛。

translations.literal: Shen Ling, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, plotted rebellion in secret; Boyuan repeatedly reported it, but the court did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xuzhou inspector Shen Ling plotted treason; Boyuan reported again and again, but court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 陵之餘黨，伯源皆撫而赦之，唯歸罪於陵，由是眾心乃安。

translations.literal: Ling indeed fled in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ling did flee and rebel.

sentences.zh: 景明初，卒于秘書監，年四十八，贈幽州刺史，復本爵固安伯。

translations.literal: Ling's remaining partisans Boyuan soothed and pardoned, laying guilt only on Ling; thus hearts were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned Ling's followers, blaming only Ling, and the region calmed.

sentences.zh: 諡曰懿。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingming he died as Secretariat Director at forty-eight; posthumously Inspector of You, restored to Baron of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingming he died as Secretariat Director at forty-eight; made posthumous Inspector of You and Baron of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 初，諶父志，法鐘繇書，子孫傳業，累世有能名。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Yi.

sentences.zh: 至邈以上，兼善草跡。

translations.literal: At first Chen's father Zhi studied Zhong You's calligraphy; descendants handed down the craft and for generations had renown for skill.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's father Zhi had studied Zhong You's script; the family kept the art and for generations were famed calligraphers.

sentences.zh: 伯源習家法，代京宮殿，多其所題。

translations.literal: From Miao upward they also excelled in cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: From Miao's generation they also mastered cursive.

sentences.zh: 白馬公崔宏亦善書，世傳衛瓘體。

translations.literal: Boyuan studied the family method; he inscribed many palaces in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan learned the house style and inscribed many capital palaces.

sentences.zh: 魏初工書者，崔、盧二門。

translations.literal: Duke of Baima Cui Hong was also skilled; the age handed down the Wei Guan manner.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Baima Cui Hong was skilled too; the age knew the Wei Guan style through him.

sentences.zh: 伯源與李沖特相友善，沖重伯源門風，伯源私沖才官，故結為婚姻，往來親密。

translations.literal: In early Wei the masters of writing were the Cui and Lu houses.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei counted the Cui and Lu clans among its finest calligraphers.

sentences.zh: 至於伯源荷孝文意遇，頗亦由沖。

translations.literal: Boyuan and Li Chong were especially close; Chong valued Boyuan's house style and Boyuan privately admired Chong's talent and office, so they intermarried and were intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan and Li Chong were close friends—Chong prized the Lu house, Boyuan admired Chong's talent, they married kin and met constantly.

sentences.zh: 伯源有八子。

translations.literal: Boyuan's favor with Xiaowen owed something to Chong as well.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan's standing with Xiaowen owed something to Chong.

sentences.zh: 長子道將，字祖業。

translations.literal: Boyuan had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 應襲父爵而讓第八弟道舒，詔不許。

translations.literal: The eldest Daojiang, styled Zuye, should have inherited but yielded to the eighth brother Daoshu; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Daojiang (Zuye), should have inherited but yielded to the eighth brother Daoshu; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 道將引清河王國常侍韓子熙讓弟采魯陽男之例，詔乃許之。

translations.literal: Daojiang cited the precedent of Han Zixi of the Prince of Qinghe's kingdom yielding the fief to his younger brother and the enfeoffment of Cai as Baron of Luyang; the edict then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Daojiang cited Han Zixi yielding his younger brother the fief of Luyang—then the throne allowed it.

sentences.zh: 道將涉獵經史，風氣謇諤，頗有文才，為一家後來之寇，諸父並敬憚之。

translations.literal: Daojiang ranged through the classics and histories; his air was blunt and upright; he had considerable literary talent and was the coming scourge of the clan—all his uncles respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Daojiang read widely in the classics and histories, carried himself with blunt integrity, wrote well, and was the family's rising terror—uncles both respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰、任城王澄皆虛衿相待。

translations.literal: Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Prince Cheng of Rencheng both received him with open courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Xie of Pengcheng and Cheng of Rencheng treated him with unfeigned respect.

sentences.zh: 勰為中軍大將軍，辟行參軍。

translations.literal: Xie was Grand General of the Central Army and recruited him as Traveling Aide.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand General of the Central Army, Xie took him on as Traveling Aide.

sentences.zh: 累遷燕郡太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Administrator of Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Administrator of Yan.

sentences.zh: 道將下車表樂毅、霍原之墓，為之立祠。

translations.literal: On taking office he marked the tombs of Yue Yi and Huo Yuanzhi and built shrines for them.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he marked the tombs of Yue Yi and Huo Yuanzhi and raised shrines.

sentences.zh: 優禮儒生，厲勸學業，敦課農桑，墾田歲倍。

translations.literal: He honored scholars, urged learning, and pressed farming and sericulture; reclaimed fields doubled yearly.
translations.idiomatic: He honored scholars, urged study, and pushed farming—reclaimed land doubled each year.

sentences.zh: 卒于司徒司馬，贈太常卿，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: He died as Secretary of the Minister of Works, posthumously Grand Minister of Ceremonies; posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died as the Minister of Works' secretary, was posthumously Grand Minister of Ceremonies with the name Xian.

sentences.zh: 所為文筆數十篇。

translations.literal: His writings number several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of his compositions survive.

sentences.zh: 子懷祖，太學博士、員外散騎侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: His son Huainzu was Erudite of the Imperial University and Supernumerary Regular Attendant; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Son Huainzu was University Erudite and supernumerary Regular Attendant, then died.

sentences.zh: 子莊，少有美名，位都水使者，卒官。

translations.literal: Son Zhuang had a fine name early and held the post of Commissioner of Waterways; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhuang won early fame, served as Commissioner of Waterways, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 懷祖弟懷仁，字子友，涉學有辭。

translations.literal: Huainzu's younger brother Huairen, styled Ziyou, was learned and eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: Huainzu's brother Huairen, styled Ziyou, was learned and articulate.

sentences.zh: 性恬靜，蕭然有閒雅致。

translations.literal: His nature was tranquil; he had an easy, elegant leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil by nature, he had an air of unhurried elegance.

sentences.zh: 曆太尉記室、弘農郡守，不之任，卜居陳留界。

translations.literal: He served as Recorder to the Grand Minister of War and was named Administrator of Hongnong but did not take the post, settling on the border of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He was Recorder to the Grand Minister of War and named to Hongnong but never went, living on the Chenliu border.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦銘頌二萬餘言，撰《中表實錄》二十卷。

translations.literal: His poems, fu, inscriptions, and eulogies exceed twenty thousand words; he compiled Records of Central Tables in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote over twenty thousand words of verse and prose and compiled twenty juan of Records of Central Tables.

sentences.zh: 懷仁有行檢，善與人交。

translations.literal: Huairen had conduct and restraint and was good at friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Huairen was disciplined in conduct and gifted at friendship.

sentences.zh: 與琅邪王衍、隴西李壽之情好相得。

translations.literal: With Wang Yan of Langye and Li Shou of Longxi he was on terms of warm affection.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Wang Yan of Langye and Li Shou of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 常語衍云：「昔太丘道廣，許劭知而不顧；

translations.literal: He often told Yan: "In olden days Taqiu spread his way wide and Xu Shao knew him yet would not look;
translations.idiomatic: He told Yan: "Once Taqiu walked a broad path and Xu Shao knew him yet turned away;

sentences.zh: 嵇生峭立，鐘會遇而絕言。

translations.literal: Ji Kang stood sharp and Zhong Hui met him yet broke off speech.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang stood aloof and Zhong Hui met him yet would not speak.

sentences.zh: 吾處季、孟之間，去其太甚。

translations.literal: I stand between Ji and Meng and cut away the excess."
translations.idiomatic: I keep between those extremes and trim the excess."

sentences.zh: 」衍以為然。

translations.literal: Yan thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Yan agreed.

sentences.zh: 子彥卿，有學尚，仕隋位御史。

translations.literal: His son Yanqing was devoted to learning and in Sui held the post of Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yanqing was scholarly and in Sui became Censor.

sentences.zh: 撰《後魏紀》三十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Annals of Later Wei in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote thirty juan of Annals of Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中位石門令、東宮學士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was Magistrate of Shimen and Academician of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he was Magistrate of Shimen and Eastern Palace academician.

sentences.zh: 道將弟道亮，字仲業，隱居不仕。

translations.literal: Daojiang's younger brother Daoliang, styled Zhongye, lived in seclusion and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Daojiang's brother Daoliang, styled Zhongye, lived in hiding and never took office.

sentences.zh: 子思道。

translations.literal: His son Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Sidao.

sentences.zh: 思道字子行，聰爽俊辯，通侻不羈。

translations.literal: Sidao, styled Zixing, was clever, sharp, handsome in debate, open and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao, styled Zixing, was bright, quick-tongued, and famously unbound by convention.

sentences.zh: 年十六，中山劉松為人作碑銘，以示思道。

translations.literal: At sixteen Liu Song of Zhongshan wrote an inscription for someone and showed it to Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Liu Song of Zhongshan showed him an inscription he had written for another.

sentences.zh: 思道讀之，多所不解。

translations.literal: Sidao read it and much he did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao read it and could not follow much of it.

sentences.zh: 乃感激讀書，師事河間邢子才。

translations.literal: Stirred thereby he took up books and studied under Xing Zicai of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Stung to shame, he threw himself into books under Xing Zicai of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 後復為文示松，松不能甚解。

translations.literal: Later he wrote a piece and showed Song; Song could not understand it well.
translations.idiomatic: Later he showed Song his own writing; Song could barely follow it.

sentences.zh: 乃喟然歎曰：「學之有益，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "Learning has its use—was it in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Song sighed: "So study does profit a man—it was not for nothing!

sentences.zh: 」因就魏收借異書。

translations.idiomatic: (end of quotation)

sentences.zh: 數年間，才學兼著。

translations.literal: He then borrowed rare books from Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed rare books from Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 然不持操行，好輕侮人物。

translations.literal: Within a few years his talent and learning both stood out.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years talent and learning both shone.

sentences.zh: 齊天保中，《魏史》成，思道多所非毀。

translations.literal: Yet he did not keep his conduct and liked to slight others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept loose morals and loved to mock people.

sentences.zh: 由是前後再被笞辱，因而落泊不調。

translations.literal: In Qi Tianbao the History of Wei was completed; Sidao disparaged it at many points.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi's History of Wei was finished in Tianbao, Sidao tore it apart in many places.

sentences.zh: 後左僕射楊遵彥薦之于朝，解褐司空行參軍、長兼員外散騎侍郎，直中書省。

translations.literal: For this he was flogged again and again and sank into neglect and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten repeatedly for it and fell into shabby neglect.

sentences.zh: 文宣帝崩，當朝文士各作輓歌十首，擇其善者而用之。

translations.literal: Later Left Vice Minister Yang Zunyan recommended him to court; he left the cloth for Attendant of the Minister of Works, long-term concurrent Supernumerary Regular Attendant, and duty in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Zunyan recommended him; he entered service as the Minister of Works' attendant, supernumerary Regular Attendant, and Secretariat duty.

sentences.zh: 魏收、陽休之、祖孝征等不過得一二首，唯思道獨有八篇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan died each leading writer composed ten dirges; the best were chosen for use.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenxuan's death every leading writer submitted ten dirges; the best were kept.

sentences.zh: 故時人稱為「八米盧郎」。

translations.literal: Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Zu Xiaozheng, and the like had no more than one or two chosen; Sidao alone had eight.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, and Zu Xiaozheng won one or two at most; Sidao alone had eight.

sentences.zh: 後漏泄省中語，出為丞相西閣祭酒。

translations.literal: Hence men of the time called him "Eight-Rice Lu Lang."
translations.idiomatic: Hence his nickname: "Eight-Rice Lu Lang."

sentences.zh: 曆太子舍人、司徒錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Later he leaked palace talk and was sent out as Libationer of the Chancellor's Western Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He leaked inner-court talk and was exiled as Libationer of the Chancellor's Western Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 每居官，多被譴辱。

translations.literal: He served as Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Recorder under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was heir's household attendant and recorder under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 後以擅用庫錢，免歸家。

translations.literal: In every post he was often rebuked and shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Every office brought rebuke.

sentences.zh: 嘗於薊北，悵然感慨，為五言詩見意，世以為工。

translations.literal: Later for unauthorized use of treasury funds he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for dipping into treasury funds.

sentences.zh: 後為給事黃門侍郎，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: Once north of Ji he gave voice to melancholy in pentasyllabic verse; the age thought it skilled.
translations.idiomatic: North of Ji he wrote pentasyllabic verse of regret that the age praised.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，授儀同三司，追赴長安。

translations.literal: Later he was Supervising Secretary and Attendant at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Supervising Secretary and attendant at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 與同輩陽休之等數人作《聽蟬鳴篇》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi he was made Colonel Third Class and summoned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's Emperor Wu conquered Qi he was made Colonel Third Class and hurried to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 思道所為，詞意清切，為時人所重。

translations.literal: With peers Yang Xiuzhi and others he composed "On Hearing the Cicada."
translations.idiomatic: With Yang Xiuzhi and others he wrote "On Hearing the Cicada."

sentences.zh: 新野庾信遍覽諸同作者，而深歎美之。

translations.literal: Sidao's piece, its wording clear and keen, was valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao's lines were clear and piercing and won the age's regard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，母疾，還鄉。

translations.literal: Yu Xin of Xinye read all the co-authors and deeply admired his.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin of Xinye read every contributor and marveled at his.

sentences.zh: 遇同郡祖英伯及從兄昌期等舉兵作亂，思道豫焉。

translations.literal: Before long his mother fell ill and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his mother fell ill and he went home.

sentences.zh: 柱國宇文神舉討平之。

translations.literal: He met Zu Yingbo of his commandery and cousin Changqi and others raising troops in revolt; Sidao took part.
translations.idiomatic: He fell in with Zu Yingbo and cousin Changqi raising troops; Sidao joined them.

sentences.zh: 思道罪當斬，已在死中。

translations.literal: Pillar of State Yuwen Shenju suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Yuwen Shenju crushed the rising.

sentences.zh: 神舉素聞其名，引出，令作露布。

translations.literal: Sidao's crime merited decapitation; he was already as good as dead.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao deserved beheading and was as good as dead.

sentences.zh: 援筆立成，文不加點。

translations.literal: Shenju had long heard his name, brought him out, and ordered him to write a victory bulletin.
translations.idiomatic: Shenju, knowing his name, pulled him out and ordered a victory bulletin.

sentences.zh: 神舉嘉而宥之。

translations.literal: He took brush and finished at once, the text needing no dot.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote at a stroke, flawless.

sentences.zh: 後除掌教上士。

translations.literal: Shenju praised him and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenju admired him and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，遷武陽太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director of Instruction, Senior Grade.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Director of Instruction, senior grade.

sentences.zh: 位下，不得志，為《孤鴻賦》以寄其情。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor he was moved to Administrator of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui's Wendi was Chancellor he was sent to Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Rank was low and his will frustrated; he wrote "Rhapsody on the Lone Goose" to lodge his feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Low in rank and thwarted, he wrote "Rhapsody on the Lone Goose" for his mood.

sentences.zh: 餘志學之歲，自鄉里游京師，便見識知音，曆受群公之眷。

translations.literal: Its preface reads:
translations.idiomatic: The preface runs:

sentences.zh: 年登弱冠，甫就朝列；

translations.literal: In the year I set my heart on learning I left my district for the capital and at once found knowing friends; I received the favor of many lords in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the year I vowed myself to learning I left home for the capital, found patrons at once, and passed from one great man's favor to another.

sentences.zh: 談者過誤，遂竊虛名。

translations.literal: At weak-capping I had just entered the court ranks;
translations.idiomatic: At twenty I had barely joined the court rolls;

sentences.zh: 通人楊令君、邢特進以下，皆分庭致敬，倒屣相接，翦拂吹噓，長其光價。

translations.literal: talkers erred and I stole a hollow name.
translations.idiomatic: gossips erred, and I stole a hollow name.

sentences.zh: 而才本駑拙，性實疏懶，勢利貨殖，淡然不營。

translations.literal: Men of insight from Vice Minister Yang down to Special Advance Xing and below all paid court across the threshold, met me shoe in hand, trimmed and puffed me, and raised my price.
translations.idiomatic: From Vice Minister Yang and Special Advance Xing downward, men of insight met me at the gate, shoes in hand, polished my name, and inflated my price.

sentences.zh: 雖籠絆朝市，且三十載，而獨往之心，未始去懷抱也。

translations.literal: Yet my talent was by nature clumsy and my disposition truly lax; profit, power, and trade I coldly would not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet talent in me was dull and nature lazy—I would not chase profit or power.

sentences.zh: 攝生舛和，有少氣疾。

translations.literal: Though bound in the market of court for nearly thirty years, the heart that walks alone never left my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court held me thirty years, the lone heart never left my breast.

sentences.zh: 分符坐嘯，作守東原。

translations.literal: My regimen was out of harmony and I had a slight breath ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Care of life went awry and I had a slight breath sickness.

sentences.zh: 洪河之湄，沃野彌望，囂務既屏，魚鳥為鄰。

translations.literal: With a tally I sat and whistled, guarding the eastern plain.
translations.idiomatic: With seal in hand I governed the eastern plain.

sentences.zh: 有離群之鴻，為羅者所獲，野人馴養，貢之于餘。

translations.literal: On the mighty river's bank the fertile fields stretched wide; clamor was shut out and fish and birds were neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Along the great river fertile fields ran to the horizon; noise fell away and fish and birds were my neighbors.

sentences.zh: 置諸池庭，朝夕賞玩，既用銷憂，兼以輕疾。

translations.literal: A goose apart from the flock was taken by a fowler; a rustic tamed it and presented it to me.
translations.idiomatic: A stray goose was netted; a countryman tamed it and gave it to me.

sentences.zh: 《大易》稱「鴻漸于陸」，羽儀盛也。

translations.literal: I set it in the pool garden and admired it morning and evening; it eased sorrow and lightened illness.
translations.idiomatic: I kept it in the pool court, admired it dawn and dusk; it eased grief and lightened sickness.

sentences.zh: 揚子曰「鴻飛冥冥」，騫翥高也。

translations.literal: The Changes says "the goose advances on the land"—its feathered majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says the goose "advances on the land"—ceremonial splendor.

sentences.zh: 《淮南子》云「東歸碣石」，違溽暑也。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong says "the goose flies in the dark"—soaring height.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong says "the goose flies in the dark"—lofty flight.

sentences.zh: 平子賦「南翔衡陽」，避祁寒也。

translations.literal: Huainanzi says "eastward to Jieshi"—fleeing summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: Huainanzi says "east to Jieshi"—escaping summer's steam.

sentences.zh: 若其雅步清音，遠心高韻，鵷鸞已降，罕見其儔。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's fu says "southward to Hengyang"—shunning severe cold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's rhapsody says "south to Hengyang"—fleeing bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 而鎩翮牆陰，偶影獨立，唼喋秕稗，雞鶩為伍，不亦傷乎。

translations.literal: In elegant step and clear tone, far heart and high rhyme, even the yuan and luan descend—rare is his peer.
translations.idiomatic: In grace of gait and clarity of song, heart distant and tone high—even phoenix birds stoop; few match him.

sentences.zh: 餘五十之年，忽焉已至，永言身事，慨然多緒，乃為之賦，聊以自慰云。

translations.literal: Yet with wings clipped in the wall's shade he stands alone in paired shadow, pecking chaff, keeping company with chickens— is it not pitiable?
translations.idiomatic: Yet wings clipped in the courtyard shade he stands alone, pecking chaff beside barnyard fowl—is it not pitiable?

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以母老，表請解職，優詔許之。

translations.literal: My fifty years have suddenly arrived; speaking forever of life's affairs, I am moved to many threads, and so I write this fu to console myself.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty years come sudden; brooding on life's business stirs many threads—thus this fu, to comfort myself.

sentences.zh: 思道恃才地，多所陵轢，由是官途淪滯。

translations.literal: At the start of Kaihuang, because his mother was old, he memorialized asking to leave office; a gracious edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang, his mother being old, he asked to resign; a kind edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 既而又著《勞生論》，指切當世。

translations.literal: Sidao relied on talent and standing and often bullied others; hence his official path sank and stalled.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao leaned on talent and rank, bullied many, and his career stalled.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，奉詔郊勞陳使。

translations.literal: Then he also wrote "On Toiling Life," cutting at the present age.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote "On Toiling Life," skewering his own times.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遭母憂。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was ordered by edict to greet the Chen envoy in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: A year on, edict ordered him to greet Chen's envoy in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起為散騎侍郎，參內史侍郎事。

translations.literal: Soon he was in mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 于時，議置六卿，將除大理。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as Regular Attendant and assisted the Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Regular Attendant assisting the Secretariat vice director.

sentences.zh: 思道上奏曰：「省有駕部，寺留太僕；

translations.literal: At that time they debated establishing the Six Ministers and were about to appoint the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Court debated the Six Ministers and meant to seat the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 省有刑部，寺除大理。

translations.literal: Sidao memorialized: "The Department has a Bureau of Transport; the Temple keeps the Minister of the Imperial Stud;
translations.idiomatic: Sidao wrote: "The ministry keeps Transport while the temple keeps the Stud—

sentences.zh: 斯則重畜產而賤刑名，誠為不可。

translations.literal: the Department has a Bureau of Punishments; the Temple removes the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: the ministry keeps Punishments while the temple drops Justice.

sentences.zh: 」又陳殿庭非杖罰之所，朝臣犯笞罪，請以贖論。

translations.literal: That values livestock and cheapens punishment— truly it cannot be."
translations.idiomatic: That exalts herds and cheapens law—unacceptable."

sentences.zh: 上悉嘉納之。

translations.literal: He also stated that the palace hall is no place for flogging; when courtiers merit the bastinado, ransom should be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the throne hall is no beating ground—when courtiers deserve the rod, let them redeem the blow.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒于京師。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and took all of it.

sentences.zh: 上甚惜之，遣使弔祭焉。

translations.literal: That year he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 集二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly regretted it and sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and sent envoys to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子赤松，大業中，位河東縣長。

translations.literal: Twenty juan of his collected works circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty juan of his works circulate.

sentences.zh: 道亮弟道裕，字甯祖。

translations.literal: His son Chisong in the Daye era was Magistrate of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chisong in Daye was Magistrate of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少以學尚知名，風儀兼美。

translations.literal: Daoliang's younger brother Daoyu, styled Ningzu.
translations.idiomatic: Daoliang's brother Daoyu, styled Ningzu.

sentences.zh: 尚獻文女樂浪長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Young he was famed for devotion to learning; his bearing was also beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Young he was famed for scholarship and handsome bearing.

sentences.zh: 歷位中書侍郎、太子中庶子、幽州大中正，卒于涇州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Lelang, daughter of Emperor Xianwen, and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Xianwen's daughter, Princess of Lelang, and became Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 道虔好《禮》學，難齊尚書令王儉《喪服集記》七十餘條。

translations.literal: Daoqian loved the study of the Rites and disputed more than seventy articles in Minister Wang Jian's "Collected Notes on Mourning Garments."
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian loved ritual studies and challenged more than seventy articles in Wang Jian's "Collected Notes on Mourning Garments."

sentences.zh: 為尚書同寮于草屋下設雞黍之膳，談者以為高。

translations.literal: Fellow Ministers set out chicken-and-millet fare for him in a thatched hut; talkers held this high.
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial colleagues served him plain chicken and millet in a thatched hut—men of taste admired it.

sentences.zh: 昧旦將上省，必見其弟然後去。

translations.literal: At dawn, about to enter the ministry, he always saw his younger brother before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn, heading to the ministry, he always visited his brother first.

sentences.zh: 奴在馬上彈琵琶，道虔聞之，杖奴一百。

translations.literal: A slave played pipa on horseback; Daoqian heard it and had the slave beaten a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing a slave play pipa on horseback, Daoqian had him beaten a hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 公主二子，昌寓宇、昌仁。

translations.literal: The princess had two sons: Changyu and Changren.
translations.idiomatic: The princess bore Changyu and Changren.

sentences.zh: 昌宇不慧，昌仁早卒。

translations.literal: Changyu was dull; Changren died young.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu lacked wit; Changren died young.

sentences.zh: 道虔又娶司馬氏，有子昌裕。

translations.literal: Daoqian also married a lady of the Sima clan and had Changyu.
translations.idiomatic: He also married a Sima and had Changyu.

sentences.zh: 後司馬氏見出，更娉元氏，甚聰悟，常升高座講《老子》。

translations.literal: Later the Sima lady was dismissed; he married again into the Yuan clan, very clever, and often lectured on the Laozi from a high seat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he dismissed the Sima wife and married a clever Yuan who lectured on the Laozi from a high seat.

sentences.zh: 道虔從弟元明隔紗帷以聽焉。

translations.literal: His cousin Yuanming listened from behind a gauze curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Yuanming listened behind a gauze screen.

sentences.zh: 元氏生二子，昌斯、昌衡，昌衡最知名。

translations.literal: The Yuan lady bore two sons, Changsi and Changheng; Changheng was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Changsi and Changheng; Changheng was best known.

sentences.zh: 昌衡字子均，小字龍子。

translations.literal: Changheng, styled Zijun, childhood name Longzi.
translations.idiomatic: Changheng, styled Zijun, childhood name Longzi.

sentences.zh: 沈靖有才識，風神淡雅，容止可法。

translations.literal: Calm and deep, with talent and insight; his spirit was elegant and light; bearing and deportment could serve as model.
translations.idiomatic: Calm, perceptive, elegant in spirit—his bearing was a model.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，工草行書。

translations.literal: He ranged through classics and histories and was skilled in cursive and running script.
translations.idiomatic: He read classics and histories and excelled at cursive and running script.

sentences.zh: 從弟思道，小字釋奴，宗中稱英妙，昌衡與之俱被推重。

translations.literal: His cousin Sidao, childhood name Shinu, was called the clan's wonder; Changheng was pushed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Sidao, childhood name Shinu, was the clan's prodigy; Changheng stood beside him in renown.

sentences.zh: 故幽州語曰：「盧家千里，釋奴、龍子。

translations.literal: Hence a saying of You Province: "A thousand li of the Lu house—Shinu and Longzi."
translations.idiomatic: You Province said: "A thousand li of Lu—Shinu and Longzi."

sentences.zh: 」仕魏，兼太尉外兵參軍。

translations.literal: " In Wei he served concurrently as Outside Army Aide to the Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he was Outside Army Aide to the Grand Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，曆平恩令。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate he served in succession as Magistrate of Ping'en.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne he was Magistrate of Ping'en in turn.

sentences.zh: 右僕射祖孝征薦為尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: Right Vice Minister Zu Xiaozheng recommended him as Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Minister Zu Xiaozheng made him Revenue Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 孝征每曰：「吾用盧子均為尚書郎，自謂無愧幽明。

translations.literal: Xiaozheng often said: "In appointing Lu Zijun Minister Gentleman I am clear before the living and the dead."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozheng said: "Using Lu Zijun as Minister Gentleman I owe nothing to living or dead."

sentences.zh: 」始天保中，尚書王昕以雅談獲罪，諸弟尚守而不墜。

translations.literal: " From Tianbao on, Minister Wang Xin was punished for elegant talk; the younger brothers still held to it without falling away.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianbao, when Minister Wang Xin was punished for salon talk, the younger men still kept the tradition.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，此道浸微。

translations.literal: From then this path gradually faded.
translations.idiomatic: After that the fashion waned.

sentences.zh: 昌衡與頓丘李若、彭城劉瑉、河南陸彥師、隴西辛德源、王循並為後進風流之士。

translations.literal: Changheng with Li Ruo of Dunqiu, Liu Min of Pengcheng, Lu Yanshi of Henan, Xin Deyuan of Longxi, and Wang Xun were all rising men of elegant fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Changheng, Li Ruo, Liu Min, Lu Yanshi, Xin Deyuan, and Wang Xun were the new salon set.

sentences.zh: 後兼散騎侍郎，迎勞周使。

translations.literal: Later he served concurrently as Regular Attendant and received Zhou envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Regular Attendant greeting Zhou envoys.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，授司玉中士，與大宗伯斛斯征修《禮令》。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wu pacified Qi he was made Director of Jade, Middle Grade, and with Grand Minister of Ceremonies Husi Zheng revised the Rites Code.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou conquered Qi he was Director of Jade and with Husi Zheng revised the Rites Code.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，拜尚書祠部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Sui Kaihuang he was made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Sui Kaihuang he was Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗大集群下，令自陳功，人皆競進，昌衡獨無所言。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once gathered his ministers and ordered each to state his merits; all competed to advance, but Changheng alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi once gathered officials to boast of merit; all pushed forward but Changheng was silent.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲目而異之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister Gao Jiong looked at him with surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister Gao Jiong eyed him in wonder.

sentences.zh: 陳使賀徹、周濆相繼來聘，朝廷每令昌衡接對之。

translations.literal: Chen envoys He Che and Zhou Fen came in succession on embassy; the court always had Changheng receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen envoys He Che and Zhou Fen came in turn; court always sent Changheng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為徐州總管長史，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Chief Clerk to the Xuzhou Grand Governor; he had a great name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was chief clerk to Xuzhou's grand governor and famed for competence.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書蘇威考之曰：「德為世表，行為士則。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Su Wei assessed him: "Virtue is the age's measure; conduct the gentleman's rule."
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei of Personnel wrote: "His virtue is the age's yardstick; his conduct the gentleman's rule."

sentences.zh: 」論之者以為美談。

translations.literal: " Discussants took it as a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: Talkers made a proverb of it.

sentences.zh: 常行至浚儀，所乘馬為人牛所觸致死。

translations.literal: Once traveling to Junyi, the horse he rode was struck dead by another man's ox.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Junyi, another man's ox killed his horse.

sentences.zh: 牛主陳謝，求還價直。

translations.literal: The ox's owner apologized and asked to repay the value.
translations.idiomatic: The owner apologized and offered payment.

sentences.zh: 昌衡謂曰：「六畜相觸，自關常理，此豈人情也，君何謝焉？

translations.literal: Changheng said: "When beasts collide it is ordinary rule—how is this a matter of human feeling? Why apologize?
translations.idiomatic: Changheng said: "Beasts collide by nature—not a human affair. Why apologize?

sentences.zh: 」拒而不受。

translations.literal: " He refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused payment.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚不校，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and he did not contend— all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and uncontentious—he was always thus.

sentences.zh: 轉壽州總管長史。

translations.literal: He was moved to Chief Clerk to the Shouzhou Grand Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk at Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 宇文述甚敬之，委以州務。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu greatly respected him and entrusted him with provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu respected him and gave him the province's business.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷金州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was moved to Inspector of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: A year on he was Inspector of Jin.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，奉詔持節為河南道巡省大使。

translations.literal: In Renshou he was ordered by edict with full powers as Touring Commissioner of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou he toured Henan circuit with full powers.

sentences.zh: 及還，以奉使稱旨，授儀同三司，賜物二百段。

translations.literal: On return, because the mission answered the intent, he was made Colonel Third Class and given two hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Returning with a mission that pleased the throne, he was Colonel Third Class with two hundred rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 昌衡自以年在縣車，上表乞骸骨，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Changheng thought himself at the age of the seventy-year staff and memorialized begging to retire; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking himself at retirement age, he begged to retire; a kind edict refused.

sentences.zh: 大業初，徵為太子左庶子，行詣洛陽，道卒。

translations.literal: At the start of Daye he was summoned as Left Companion of the Heir Apparent; on the road to Luoyang he died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he was summoned as the heir's left companion and died on the road to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 子寶素、寶胤。

translations.literal: Sons Baosu and Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Baosu and Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 道虔弟道侃，字希祖，沈雅有學尚，位州主簿，卒。

translations.literal: Daoqian's younger brother Daokan, styled Xizu, was deep, elegant, and devoted to learning; he was Prefectural Clerk and died.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Daokan, styled Xizu, scholarly and refined, was prefectural clerk and died.

sentences.zh: 以弟道約子正達為後。

translations.literal: Daoyue's son Zhengda was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyue's son Zhengda was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 道侃弟道和，字叔雍，兄弟之中，人望最下。

translations.literal: Daokan's younger brother Daohe, styled Shuyong, had the lowest standing among the brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Daohe, styled Shuyong, ranked lowest among the brothers.

sentences.zh: 位冀州中軍府中兵參軍，卒。

translations.literal: He was Army Aide in the Central Army Office of Ji Province and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was army aide in Ji's central staff and died.

sentences.zh: 子景猷，弘農太守。

translations.literal: His son Jingyou was Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Son Jingyou was Administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 景猷子士彥，有風概，隋開皇中，為蜀王秀屬。

translations.literal: Jingyou's son Shiyan had spirit and bearing; in early Sui Kaihuang he was retainer to Prince Xiu of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shiyan had force of character; early in Kaihuang he served Prince Xiu of Shu.

sentences.zh: 以秀所為不軌，辭疾，終於家。

translations.literal: Because Xiu's conduct was improper he pleaded illness and ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu turned lawless he pleaded sickness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 道和弟道約，字季恭，位司徒屬、幽州大中正。

translations.literal: Daohe's younger brother Daoyue, styled Jigong, was Attendant of the Minister of Works and Grand Rectifier of You.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Daoyue, styled Jigong, was the Minister of Works' attendant and You Grand Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 興和末，除衛大將軍、兗州刺史，在州頗得人和。

translations.literal: At the end of Xinghe he was made Grand General of the Guard and Inspector of Yan; in the province he won men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xinghe he was Grand General of the Guard and Yan inspector and won the province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈儀同三司、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously Colonel Third Class and Inspector of You.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Colonel Third Class and You inspector.

sentences.zh: 子正通，少有令譽，位開府諮議，卒。

translations.literal: His son Zhengtong had a fine reputation early and was Counselor of the Opening Office; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhengtong had early fame, was Opening Office counselor, and died.

sentences.zh: 妻謝氏，與正通弟正思淫亂，為御史所劾，人士疾之。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Xie committed adultery with Zhengtong's younger brother Zhengsi; the censor impeached them and gentlemen despised it.
translations.idiomatic: Wife Lady Xie lay with brother Zhengsi; censors impeached them and gentlemen despised the house.

sentences.zh: 正思弟正山字公順，早以文學見知，為符璽郎，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: Zhengsei's younger brother Zhengshan, styled Gongshun, was known early for literature, was Seal Clerk, and attended the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zhengshan, styled Gongshun, was known for letters, seal clerk, Forest of Literature attendant.

sentences.zh: 正思兄弟以齊太后舅氏，武平中，並得優贈。

translations.literal: The Zhengsi brothers, as maternal uncles of the Qi empress dowager, in Wuping all received generous posthumous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: As the Qi empress dowager's kin, the brothers received lavish posthumous honors in Wuping.

sentences.zh: 道約弟道舒，字幼安，襲父爵，位中書侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: Daoyue's younger brother Daoshu, styled You'an, inherited his father's title and was Gentleman of the Secretariat; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Daoshu, styled You'an, inherited the title, was Secretariat Gentleman, and died.

sentences.zh: 子熙裕襲。

translations.literal: His son Xiyu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiyu inherited.

sentences.zh: 熙裕清虛守道，有古人風，為親表所敬。

translations.literal: Xiyu was pure, empty, and kept the Way; he had the air of the ancients and was respected by kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyu was pure, held the Way, seemed a man of old times, and kin revered him.

sentences.zh: 伯源弟敏，字仲通，小字洪崖，少有大量。

translations.literal: Boyuan's younger brother Min, styled Zhongtong, childhood name Hongya, had great breadth early.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan's brother Min, styled Zhongtong, childhood name Hongya, was magnanimous from youth.

sentences.zh: 孝文器之，納其女為嬪。

translations.literal: Xiaowen valued him and took his daughter as a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen prized him and took his daughter as consort.

sentences.zh: 位儀曹郎，早卒，贈威遠將軍、范陽太守，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He was Gentleman of Ceremonies, died young, posthumously General of Awesome Far Reach and Administrator of Fanyang; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was Ceremonies Gentleman, died young, posthumously General of Awesome Far Reach and Fanyang Administrator with posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 五子。

translations.literal: Five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons.

sentences.zh: 長義僖，字遠慶，早有學尚，識度沈雅。

translations.literal: The eldest Yixi, styled Yuanqing, was early devoted to learning; his insight was deep and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Yixi, styled Yuanqing, was early scholarly, deep and elegant in judgment.

sentences.zh: 年九歲喪父，便有至性，少為僕射李沖所歎美。

translations.literal: At nine he lost his father and showed utmost filial nature; young he was admired by Vice Minister Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he lost his father and showed perfect filial piety; young he won Li Chong's praise.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，累遷冠軍將軍、中散大夫，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He began as Secretariat Gentleman, rose to General Who Overcomes Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Leisure, and left office for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Secretariat Gentleman, rose to General Who Overcomes Barbarians and Palace Leisure Grand Master, then mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 幽州刺史王誦與之交款，每與故舊李神俊等書曰：「盧冠軍在此，時復惠存，輒連數日，得以諮詢政道。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Song of You was on close terms with him and often wrote old friends Li Shenjun and others: "General Lu is here; he sometimes favors us and for several days running we may consult on the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: You inspector Wang Song was close and wrote Li Shenjun: "General Lu is here—when he favors us we consult on government for days.

sentences.zh: 」其見重若此。

translations.literal: " He was valued to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his esteem.

sentences.zh: 後拜征虜將軍、太中大夫，散秩多年，澹然自得。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Punishes Barbarians and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was General Who Punishes Barbarians and Palace Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 李神俊勸其幹謁當途，義僖曰：「既學先王之道，貴行先王之志，何得苟求富貴也？

translations.literal: For many years he held idle rank and was calm and self-sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Many years on idle salary he was content.

sentences.zh: 」孝昌中，除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun urged him to solicit those in power; Yixi said: "Having studied the former kings' Way, one should honor the former kings' will—how can one crudely seek wealth and rank?
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun urged him to court the powerful; Yixi said: "I study the former kings' Way—how can I grub for rank and gold?

sentences.zh: 時靈太后臨朝，黃門侍郎李神軌勢傾朝野，求結婚姻。

translations.literal: " In Xiaochang he was made Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang he was Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 義僖慮其必敗，拒而不許。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Ling held court; Palace Attendant Li Shengui's power tilted the court; he sought marriage ties.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ruled; Li Shengui's power bent the court and he sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 王誦謂義僖曰：「昔人不以一女易五男，卿易之也？

translations.literal: Yixi feared he must fail and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi feared ruin and refused.

sentences.zh: 」義僖曰：「所以不從，正為此耳。

translations.idiomatic: Wang Song said: "Men once would not trade one daughter for five sons—will you?

sentences.zh: 從，恐禍大而連速。

translations.idiomatic: Yixi said: "I refuse for exactly that reason.

translations.idiomatic: Song seized his hand: "I have heard fate—do not change what I tell you.

sentences.zh: 」遂適他族。

translations.literal: " He then married into another clan.
translations.idiomatic: He married elsewhere.

translations.literal: On the eve of the wedding Empress Dowager Ling sent Palace Attendant Fu Jing to his home with an order to stop it; inside and outside were terrified; Yixi was calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding eve Ling sent Fu Jing to halt it; the household panicked; Yixi was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，除都官尚書、驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.idiomatic: In Putai he was Minister of Justice, General of Agile Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 義僖寬和畏慎，不妄交款。

translations.literal: Yixi was broad, harmonious, cautious, and fearful; he did not make friends lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi was broad, gentle, cautious, and slow to befriend.

sentences.zh: 性清儉，不營財利。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and frugal; he did not pursue wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and frugal, he did not chase wealth.

sentences.zh: 少時，幽州頻遭水旱，先有數萬石穀貸人，義僖以年穀不熟，乃燔其契，州閭悅其恩德。

translations.literal: In youth You suffered flood and drought in succession; he had earlier lent tens of thousands of bushels of grain; because the year's grain did not ripen Yixi burned the bonds, and the district rejoiced in his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: You had floods and drought; he had lent tens of thousands of bushels—when grain failed he burned the IOUs and the district blessed him.

sentences.zh: 雖居顯位，每至困乏，麥飯蔬食，怡然甘之。

translations.literal: Though in a lofty post, whenever he was in want he ate wheat and vegetables and was gladly content.
translations.idiomatic: Though high in office, in want he ate wheat gruel and greens gladly.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈大將軍、儀同三司、瀛州刺史，諡曰孝簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously Grand General, Colonel Third Class, and Inspector of Ying; posthumous name Xiaojian.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Grand General, Colonel Third Class, Ying inspector, posthumous name Xiaojian.

sentences.zh: 子遜之，清靖寡欲，位太尉記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xunzhi was pure, quiet, and free of desire; he was Recorder to the Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xunzhi was pure, quiet, without craving, Recorder to the Grand Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 義僖四弟，並遠不逮兄也。

translations.literal: Yixi's four younger brothers all fell far short of the elder.
translations.idiomatic: Four younger brothers never matched him.

sentences.zh: 敏弟昶，字叔達，小字師顏，學涉經史，早有時譽。

translations.literal: Min's younger brother Chang, styled Shuda, childhood name Shiyan, ranged through classics and histories and had early fame.
translations.idiomatic: Min's brother Chang, styled Shuda, childhood name Shiyan, read widely and was famed early.

sentences.zh: 太和中，兼員外散騎常侍，使于齊。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served concurrently as Supernumerary Regular Attendant on embassy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he was supernumerary Regular Attendant on embassy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 孝文詔昶曰：「密邇江揚，不早當晚，會是朕物。

translations.literal: Xiaowen instructed Chang: "Close to the Jiang and Yang—sooner or later, not early or late, it will be mine.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen told Chang: "Hard by Jiang and Yang—sooner or later it is mine.

sentences.zh: 卿等欲言便言，無相疑難。

translations.literal: You gentlemen may speak if you wish; do not be doubtful or difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Speak freely; do not hold back.

sentences.zh: 」又敕副使王清石曰：「卿莫以南人語致疑盧昶。

translations.literal: " He also charged Deputy Envoy Wang Qingshi: "Do not let southern speech make you suspect Lu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He charged deputy Wang Qingshi: "Do not let southern talk make you doubt Lu Chang.

sentences.zh: 若彼先有知識，欲見但見，須論即論。

translations.literal: If they already have acquaintances and wish to meet, meet; if discussion is needed, discuss.
translations.idiomatic: If they know someone and wish a meeting, meet; if debate is wanted, debate.

sentences.zh: 昶正寬柔君子，無多文才，或主客命卿作詩，莫以昶不作，便罷也。

translations.literal: Chang is a mild and gentle gentleman, without much literary talent; if the host orders you to compose verse, do not stop the banquet because Chang does not write.
translations.idiomatic: Chang is a mild gentleman, no great poet—if the host demands verse, do not end the feast because Chang stays silent.

sentences.zh: 凡使人以和為貴，勿相矜誇，見於色貌。

translations.literal: In sending envoys harmony is precious; do not boast against one another in face or bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys should prize harmony, not strut and sneer in each other's faces.

sentences.zh: 」及至彼，遇齊明立，孝文南討，昶兄伯源為別道將。

translations.literal: " When they reached Qi, Qi Ming had just taken the throne; Xiaowen campaigned south and Chang's elder brother Boyuan was a general on a separate route.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, Qi Ming had just risen; Xiaowen marched south while Chang's brother Boyuan led another column.

sentences.zh: 而齊明以朝廷加兵，遂酷遇之。

translations.literal: Because Qi Ming saw the court adding troops, he treated them harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Ming, seeing more Northern Wei troops, treated them harshly.

sentences.zh: 昶等本非骨鯁，大怖，淚汗橫流。

translations.literal: Chang and the rest were no men of stiff backbone; greatly afraid, tears and sweat ran together.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's party were no iron spines—they shook, wept, and sweated.

sentences.zh: 齊明以腐米臭魚莝豆供之。

translations.literal: Qi Ming supplied them with rotten rice, stinking fish, and chaff beans.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Ming fed them rotten rice, foul fish, and bean husks.

sentences.zh: 而謁者張思寧，辭氣謇愕，遂以壯烈死於館中。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the usher Zhang Sining, blunt and unyielding in speech, died a heroic death in the hostel.
translations.idiomatic: The usher Zhang Sining spoke bluntly and died heroically in the hostel.

sentences.zh: 昶還，孝文責之曰：「銜命之禮，有死無辱，雖流放海隅，猶宜抱節致殞。

translations.literal: When Chang returned, Emperor Xiaowen rebuked him: "The protocol of bearing commission permits death but not dishonor; even exiled to the sea's edge one ought to hold integrity until death.
translations.idiomatic: Chang returned, and Xiaowen rebuked him: "An envoy may die but must not be shamed; exiled to the sea's edge, he should still die holding his integrity."

sentences.zh: 卿不能長纓羈首，已是可恨。

translations.literal: You could not tie your hair and present your head bound—a thing already hateful.
translations.idiomatic: You would not even bind your hair and offer your head—that was hateful enough.

sentences.zh: 乃俛眉飲啄，自同犬馬。

translations.literal: Instead you bowed your brows and pecked at food like a dog or horse.
translations.idiomatic: Then you bowed and ate like a dog or horse.

sentences.zh: 有生必死，修短幾何？

translations.literal: Life must end in death; how long or short is it?
translations.idiomatic: All who live must die; how long does it matter?

sentences.zh: 卿若殺身成名，貽之竹素，何如甘彼芻菽，以辱君父。

translations.literal: Had you died to achieve a name and left it in bamboo and silk, how would that compare to willingly eating fodder and shaming lord and father?
translations.idiomatic: Had you died for a name in the histories, how would that compare to eating fodder and shaming your lord and father?

sentences.zh: 縱不能遠慚蘇武，寧不近愧思寧！

translations.literal: Even if you cannot be ashamed before Su Wu from afar, can you not be ashamed before Sining nearby!
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot match Su Wu from afar, can you not be ashamed before Sining beside you!

sentences.zh: 」遂見罷黜。

translations.literal: He was then dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎、本州大中正、散騎常侍，兼尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, promoted to Supervisor of Attendants of the Yellow Gate, Grand Rectifier of the province, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jingming he became Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Yellow Gate Supervisor, provincial rectifier, regular attendant, and concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽縣獲白鼠。

translations.literal: At that time Luoyang County captured a white rat.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang County then caught a white rat.

sentences.zh: 昶奏，以為案《瑞典》，外鎮刺史二千石令長不祗上命，刻暴，百姓怨嗟，則白鼠至。

translations.literal: Chang memorialized, holding that according to the canon of auspicious omens, when frontier governors and prefectural officials of two thousand bushels do not respect imperial orders but are harsh and violent and the people groan, white rats appear.
translations.idiomatic: Chang memorialized that the canon of auspicious omens says white rats appear when frontier governors and two-thousand-bushel magistrates defy orders, act brutally, and the people groan.

sentences.zh: 因陳時政，多所勸誡。

translations.literal: He thereupon set forth current affairs, mostly admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: He then addressed current affairs, mostly in admonition.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒美其意。

translations.literal: An edict praised his intent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his meaning.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中，又兼吏部尚書，尋即正，仍侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrently Minister of Personnel, soon made regular minister while still Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant and concurrent Minister of Personnel, soon regular minister while still attendant.

sentences.zh: 昶守職而已，無所激揚，與侍中元暉等更相朋附，為宣武所寵，時人鄙之。

translations.literal: Chang merely held his post without stirring anyone up; with Palace Attendant Yuan Hui and others he formed a clique, was favored by Emperor Xuanwu, and men of the time despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang only kept his post without stirring things up; he and Attendant Yuan Hui cliqued together, won Xuanwu's favor, and contemporaries despised them.

sentences.zh: 出為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 昶既儒生，本少將略，又羊社子燮為昶司馬，專任戎事，掩昶耳目，將士怨之。

translations.literal: Chang was a Confucian by origin and naturally lacked military grasp; moreover Yang Sheo's son Xie served as Chang's Major, monopolizing military affairs and blocking Chang's eyes and ears, and officers resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was a scholar by birth and knew little of war; Yang Sheo's son Xie was his major, monopolized military affairs, kept Chang in the dark, and the troops resented it.

sentences.zh: 朐山戍主傅文驥糧樵俱罄，以城降梁。

translations.literal: Fu Wenyi, garrison chief of Mount Xiong, exhausted grain and firewood and surrendered the city to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wenyi, garrison chief at Mount Xiong, ran out of grain and fuel and surrendered the city to Liang.

sentences.zh: 昶見城降，先走退，諸軍相尋奔遁。

translations.literal: When Chang saw the city surrender he fled first in retreat, and the armies in succession broke and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the surrender, Chang fled first; the armies then broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 遇大寒，軍人凍死及落手足者太半。

translations.literal: A great cold struck; soldiers who froze to death or lost hands and feet were more than half.
translations.idiomatic: In bitter cold more than half the men froze to death or lost hands and feet.

sentences.zh: 自魏經略江右，唯中山王英敗于鐘離，昶於朐山失利，最為甚焉。

translations.literal: Since Wei began strategy on the south bank of the Yangtze, only Prince of Zhongshan Ying was defeated at Zhongli; Chang's setback at Mount Xiong was the severest.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei began campaigning south of the Yangtze, only Prince of Zhongshan Ying had lost at Zhongli; Chang's defeat at Mount Xiong was worse.

sentences.zh: 宣武遣黃門甄琛馳驛鎖昶，窮其敗狀，詔以免官論。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu sent Yellow Gate Attendant Zhen Chen post-haste to bind Chang and probe his defeat; an edict ordered dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu sent Yellow Gate Attendant Zhen Chen by post relay to bind Chang and investigate the defeat; an edict stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 自餘將統以下，悉聽依赦復任。

translations.literal: From other commanders and leaders downward, all were permitted restoration by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Other commanders and leaders were all allowed restoration by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜太常卿，仍除雍州刺史，進號鎮西將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies, then made Governor of Yong Province, advanced to Defender-General of the West, with addition as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Minister of Ceremonies, then Governor of Yong, Defender-General of the West, and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 昶寬和矜恕，善於綏懷。

translations.literal: Chang was lenient and forbearing in pity, skilled at soothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was gentle, forgiving, and skilled at soothing people.

sentences.zh: 其在徐州，戍兵有疾，親自檢恤，至番兵年滿不歸，容充後役，終昶一政，然後始還，人庶稱之。

translations.literal: At Xuzhou, when garrison soldiers fell ill he personally inspected them; when frontier troops whose term expired did not return, he allowed them to fill later labor—throughout Chang's tenure they only then returned, and the populace praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou he personally tended sick garrison troops; when frontier men whose terms had expired did not return, he let them serve later terms—only after his tenure ended did they go home, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 子元聿，字仲訓，無他才能。

translations.literal: His son Yuan Yu, styled Zhongxun, had no other talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan Yu, styled Zhongxun, had no other ability.

sentences.zh: 尚孝文女義陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Xiaowen's daughter the Princess of Yiyang, was appointed Commandant of Horse Caparisons.
translations.idiomatic: He married Xiaowen's daughter Princess Yiyang and became Commandant of Horse Caparisons.

sentences.zh: 位太尉司馬、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posts as Grand Marshal's Major, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He held posts as Grand Marshal's major and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中書監。

translations.literal: He died; enfeoffed as Director of the Palace Secretariat posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子士晟，儀同開府掾。

translations.literal: His son Shi Sheng, aide to the Grand Minister with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies opening a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Sheng was aide to a minister with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 元聿第五弟元明，字幼章。

translations.literal: Yuan Yu's fifth younger brother Yuan Ming, styled Youzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu's fifth brother Yuan Ming, styled Youzhang.

sentences.zh: 涉曆群書，兼有文義，風彩閑潤，進退可觀。
