translations.literal: He ranged through many books and also had literary skill; his bearing was leisurely and moist, his advances and retreats admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and wrote well; his manner was easy and polished, his bearing admirable.

sentences.zh: 永安初，長兼尚書令、臨淮王彧欽愛之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he long served concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing and was cherished by Prince of Linhuai Wang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yong'an he long served as concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing and was cherished by Prince of Linhuai Wang Yu.

sentences.zh: 及彧開府，引為兼屬，仍領部曲。

translations.literal: When Yu opened a staff he was brought in as concurrent aide and still led a personal detachment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu opened a staff he became concurrent aide and still led his own troops.

sentences.zh: 孝武登阼，以郎任行禮，封城陽縣子，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne he served as Lang performing ceremonies and was enfeoffed Baron of Chengyang, promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu ascended the throne he performed ceremonial duties as Lang, was enfeoffed Baron of Chengyang, and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，居洛東緱山，乃作《幽居賦》焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi he lived on Mount Gou east of Luoyang and wrote his "Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi he lived on Mount Gou east of Luoyang and wrote his Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling.

sentences.zh: 于時，元明友人王由居潁川，忽夢由攜酒就之言別，賦詩為贈。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Ming's friend Wang You lived in Yingchuan; suddenly he dreamed You came with wine to speak farewell and presented a poem as gift.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming's friend Wang You was in Yingchuan; suddenly You dreamed Wang came with wine to say farewell and left a parting poem.

sentences.zh: 及明，憶其詩十字，云：「自茲一去後，市朝不復遊。

translations.literal: When day broke he recalled the poem's ten characters: "From this day when I go forth / the markets and courts I shall visit no more."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he recalled ten lines: "From this day I go—/ no more the markets and courts."

sentences.zh: 」元明歎曰：「由性不狎俗，旅寄人間，乃有今夢，詩復如此，必有他故。

translations.literal: Yuan Ming sighed: "You by nature did not linger with the vulgar; lodging a while among men—and now this dream, and the poem too—surely there is another cause."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming sighed: "You never kept company with the vulgar; you only lodged among men—and now this dream and poem. Something else must be at hand."

sentences.zh: 」經三日，果聞由為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: After three days he indeed heard You was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he learned You had been killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 尋其亡日，乃是發夢之夜。

translations.literal: Searching the date of his death, it was the very night the dream came.
translations.idiomatic: The date of his death was the night of the dream.

sentences.zh: 天平中，兼吏部郎中，副李諧使梁，南人稱之。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he concurrently served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and assisted Li Xie on an embassy to Liang; Southerners praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he served concurrently as director in the Ministry of Personnel and assisted Li Xie's embassy to Liang; Southerners praised him.

sentences.zh: 還，拜尚書右丞，轉散騎常侍，監起居。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, transferred to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and supervised the diarists.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then regular attendant supervising the diarists.

sentences.zh: 積年在史館，了不措意。

translations.literal: He accumulated years in the historiography office and paid no mind to it at all.
translations.idiomatic: He spent years in the historiography office and paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 又兼黃門郎、本州大中正。

translations.literal: Also concurrently Yellow Gate Attendant and Grand Rectifier of the province.
translations.idiomatic: He also held Yellow Gate Attendant and provincial rectifier concurrently.

sentences.zh: 元明善自標置，不妄交遊，飲酒賦詩，遇興忘返。

translations.literal: Yuan Ming knew how to set himself apart; he did not socialize idly, drinking wine and composing poetry—when inspiration came he forgot to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming held himself apart; he did not socialize lightly, but drank and wrote poetry and forgot to return when inspiration took him.

sentences.zh: 性好玄理，作史子雜論數十篇，諸文別有集錄。

translations.literal: He loved arcane reasoning and wrote several tens of essays on history, masters, and miscellaneous topics; his other writings are collected separately.
translations.idiomatic: He loved metaphysics and wrote dozens of essays on history, masters, and miscellany; other works are collected elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 少時，常從鄉還洛，途遇相州刺史、中山王熙。

translations.literal: In youth when returning from his district to Luoyang, on the road he met the Governor of Xiangzhou, Prince of Zhongshan Xi.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth returning from his district to Luoyang, he met on the road Xiangzhou Governor Prince of Zhongshan Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙，博識之士，見而歎曰：「盧郎有如此風神，唯須誦《離騷》，飲美酒，自為佳器。

translations.literal: Xi, a man of broad knowledge, saw him and exclaimed: "Young Master Lu has such spirit—he need only recite the 'Encountering Sorrow,' drink fine wine, and is himself a fine vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Xi, a learned man, saw him and exclaimed: "Young Master Lu has such spirit—he need only recite the Encountering Sorrow, drink good wine, and he is a vessel fit for use."

sentences.zh: 」遂留之數日，贈帛及馬而別。

translations.literal: He kept him several days and gave silk and a horse on parting.
translations.idiomatic: He kept him several days and on parting gave silk and a horse.

sentences.zh: 元明凡三娶，次妻鄭氏與元明兄子士啟淫汙，元明不能離絕。

translations.literal: Yuan Ming married three times in all; his second wife the Lady Zheng had improper relations with Yuan Ming's elder brother's son Shi Qi, and Yuan Ming could not cut her off.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming married three times; his second wife Lady Zheng had relations with his elder brother's son Shi Qi, and Yuan Ming could not sever her.

sentences.zh: 又好以世地自矜，時論以此貶之。

translations.literal: He also liked to boast of his family's standing; opinion of the time depreciated him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He also boasted of his family's standing, for which contemporaries looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 元明弟元緝，字幼緒，凶粗好酒，曾於婦氏飲宴，小有不平，手刃其客。

translations.literal: Yuan Ming's younger brother Yuan Ji, styled Youxu, was brutal and fond of wine; once at his wife's clan drinking, over a slight offense he cut down a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming's brother Yuan Ji, styled Youxu, was brutal and fond of wine; once at his wife's kin he killed a guest over a slight.

sentences.zh: 位輔國將軍、司徒司馬，贈驃騎大將軍、吏部尚書、幽州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Post: General Who Assists the State, Grand Marshal's Major; posthumously enfeoffed General-in-Chief of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Personnel, Governor of Youzhou; posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He reached General Who Assists the State and Grand Marshal's major; posthumously he was made General-in-Chief of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Personnel, Governor of Youzhou, posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 昶弟尚之，字季儒，小字羨夏。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Shangzhi, styled Jiru, childhood name Xianxia.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Shangzhi, styled Jiru, childhood name Xianxia.

sentences.zh: 亦以儒素見重，位司徒左長史、前將軍、濟州刺史、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He too was valued for Confucian purity, posts: Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal, General of the Vanguard, Governor of Jizhou, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He too was valued for scholarly purity and reached left chief clerk of the Grand Marshal, vanguard general, Governor of Jizhou, and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 長子文甫，字元祐，涉曆文史，有名譽于時。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wenfu, styled Yuanyou, ranged through literature and history and had reputation in the time.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wenfu, styled Yuanyou, ranged through literature and history and was renowned.

sentences.zh: 位司空行參軍。

translations.literal: Post: Aide in the Secretariat of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was aide in the Minister of Works' secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文甫弟文翼，字仲祐，少甚輕躁，晚頗改節。

translations.literal: Wenfu's younger brother Wenyi, styled Zhongyou, was very impetuous in youth and in later years much reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu's brother Wenyi, styled Zhongyou, was very rash in youth but reformed much in later years.

sentences.zh: 以軍功賜爵范陽子，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Fanyang and made Grand Masters of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Fanyang and made grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 文翼弟文符，字叔偉，性通率，位通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Wenyi's younger brother Wenfu, styled Shuwei, was open and direct by nature, post: Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary attached to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi's brother Wenfu, styled Shuwei, was frank by nature and reached regular cavalier attendant attached to the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子潛。

translations.literal: His son Qian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qian.

sentences.zh: 潛容貌瑰偉，善言談，少有成人志尚，累遷大將軍府中兵參軍，機事強濟，為文襄所知，言其終可大用。

translations.literal: Qian's appearance was striking and he spoke well; in youth he had the ambition of a grown man; he rose repeatedly to Military Service Aide in the Grand General's office, was forceful and capable in affairs, known to Wen Xiang, who said he would ultimately be greatly useful.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was striking in appearance and eloquent; in youth he had a man's ambition; he rose to military service aide in the grand general's office, was forceful in affairs, and Wen Xiang said he would prove greatly useful.

sentences.zh: 王思政見獲於潁川，文襄重其才識。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng was captured at Yingchuan; Wen Xiang treasured his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng was captured at Yingchuan; Wen Xiang prized his talent.

sentences.zh: 潛常從容白文襄：「思政不能死節，何足可重？

translations.literal: Qian calmly told Wen Xiang: "Sizheng could not die holding integrity—how is he worth prizing?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian calmly told Wen Xiang: "Sizheng could not die holding his integrity—why prize him?"

sentences.zh: 」文襄謂左右曰：「我有盧潛，便是更得一王思政。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang said to those around him: "With Lu Qian I have gained another Wang Sizheng."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang told his attendants: "With Lu Qian I have gained another Wang Sizheng."

sentences.zh: 」天保中，除左戶郎中。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was appointed Director of the Left Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao he was appointed director of the left household bureau.

sentences.zh: 坐譏議《魏書》，與王松年、李庶等俱被禁止。

translations.literal: For criticizing the Wei History he was, with Wang Songnian, Li Shu and others, all placed under prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: For criticizing the Wei History he was, with Wang Songnian and Li Shu, placed under prohibition.

sentences.zh: 會清河王嶽救江陵，特赦潛為岳行台郎。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue rescued Jiangling, Qian alone was specially pardoned as Yue's mobile staff secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue rescued Jiangling, Qian alone was specially pardoned to serve on Yue's mobile staff.

sentences.zh: 還，曆中書、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he passed through Vice Director of Secretariat and Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On return he served as vice director of the secretariat and yellow gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 為奴誣告謀反，文宣明之，以奴付潛，潛不之責。

translations.literal: A slave falsely accused him of plotting rebellion; Emperor Wenxuan clarified the matter and handed the slave over to Qian, who did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: A slave falsely accused him of rebellion; Wenxuan cleared him and gave the slave to Qian, who did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 黃門鄭子默奏潛從清河王岳南討，嶽令潛說梁將侯瑱，大納瑱賂遺，還不奏聞。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Zheng Zimo memorialized that when Qian followed Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue on the southern campaign, Yue had Qian persuade Liang general Hou Tian, who greatly accepted bribes from Tian, and on return did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Zheng Zimo memorialized that on the southern campaign with Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue, Yue had Qian persuade Liang general Hou Tian; Qian took large bribes from Tian and did not report it on return.

sentences.zh: 文宣杖潛一百，仍截其須，潛顏色不變。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan gave Qian a hundred blows with the rod and still cut off his beard; Qian's color did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan had Qian beaten a hundred strokes and cut off his beard; Qian's face did not change.

sentences.zh: 曆魏尹丞、懷州別駕、江州刺史，所在有善政。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Luoyang Prefecture, Administrator of Huai Province, Governor of Jiangzhou—wherever he went there was good government.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of Luoyang prefecture, administrator of Huai, and governor of Jiang—wherever he went his rule was good.

sentences.zh: 孝昭作相，以潛為揚州道行台左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao became Chancellor, Qian was made Left Aide of the mobile staff on the Yangzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao became chancellor, Qian was made left aide of the Yangzhou mobile staff.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁將王琳擁其主蕭莊歸壽陽，朝廷以琳為揚州刺史，敕潛與琳為南討經略。

translations.literal: Earlier Liang general Wang Lin had brought his lord Xiao Zhuang to Shouyang; the court made Lin Governor of Yangzhou and ordered Qian with Lin as southern campaign strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liang general Wang Lin had brought his lord Xiao Zhuang to Shouyang; the court made Lin governor of Yangzhou and ordered Qian to strategize the southern campaign with him.

sentences.zh: 後除行台尚書、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later appointed Mobile Staff Director of Masters of Writing and Peer with protocol equal to Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made mobile staff director of the masters of writing with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 王琳銳意圖南，潛以為時事未可，由是與琳有隙，更相表列。

translations.literal: Wang Lin was bent on plans south; Qian held the times not yet ripe, hence he and Lin had a rift and repeatedly memorialized against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin was bent on advancing south; Qian held the time not ripe, so they quarreled and repeatedly memorialized against each other.

sentences.zh: 武成追琳入鄴，除潛揚州刺史，領行台尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng recalled Lin to Ye and appointed Qian Governor of Yangzhou, holding concurrent Mobile Staff Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng recalled Lin to Ye and made Qian governor of Yangzhou, concurrently mobile staff director.

sentences.zh: 潛在淮南十三年，大樹風績，為陳人所憚。

translations.literal: Qian was in Huainan thirteen years and planted great achievements; Chen men feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian spent thirteen years in Huainan and built a great record; the Chen feared him.

sentences.zh: 陳主與其邊將書云：「盧潛猶在，卿宜深備之。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler wrote his frontier generals: "Lu Qian is still there—you should prepare deeply."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler wrote his frontier generals: "Lu Qian is still there—you must prepare deeply."

sentences.zh: 」文宣初平淮南，給復十年，年滿後，逮天統、武平中，徵稅頗雜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan first pacified Huainan, tax relief was granted ten years; when the term expired, by the Tiantong and Wuping eras levies were rather mixed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan first pacified Huainan, tax relief was granted for ten years; after it expired, under Tiantong and Wuping levies grew tangled.

sentences.zh: 又高元海執政，斷漁獵，人家無以自資。

translations.literal: Moreover Gao Yuanhai held power and cut off fishing and hunting; households had no way to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Gao Yuanhai held power and banned fishing and hunting, so households could not support themselves.

sentences.zh: 諸商胡負官責息者，宦者陳德信縱其妄注淮南富家，令州縣征責。

translations.literal: Various merchant Hu with state debt interest, eunuch Chen Dexin indulged their reckless entries against rich Huainan families and had prefectures and counties collect debts.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant Hu owed the state interest; eunuch Chen Dexin let them post reckless claims against rich Huainan families and had prefectures collect.

sentences.zh: 又敕送突厥馬數千匹于揚州管內，令土豪貴買之，錢直始入。

translations.literal: Also an edict sent several thousand Turkish horses within Yangzhou's jurisdiction and ordered local magnates to buy them at high price—the money only just entered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also sent several thousand Turkish horses into Yangzhou and ordered local magnates to buy them dear—the money had barely entered.

sentences.zh: 便出敕括江、淮間馬並送官廄。

translations.literal: Then came an edict to round up horses between the Jiang and Huai and send them to the government stables.
translations.idiomatic: Then came an edict to round up horses between the Jiang and Huai and send them to government stables.

sentences.zh: 由是百姓騷擾，切齒嗟怨。

translations.literal: Hence the people were disturbed and gnashed teeth in lament.
translations.idiomatic: The people were in turmoil and gnashed their teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 潛隨事撫慰，兼行權略，故得寧靖。

translations.literal: Qian soothed affairs as they arose and also exercised expedients, so there was calm.
translations.idiomatic: Qian soothed matters as they arose and used expedients, so the region grew calm.

sentences.zh: 武平三年，徵為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuping he was recalled as Director of the Five Armies Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuping he was recalled as director of the five armies bureau.

sentences.zh: 揚州吏人以潛斷酒肉，篤信釋氏，大設僧會，以香花緣道流涕送之。

translations.literal: Yangzhou clerks and people, because Qian had abstained from wine and meat and devoutly believed in Buddhism, held great Buddhist assemblies and with incense and flowers lined the road weeping to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou clerks and people, because Qian abstained from wine and meat and devoutly believed in Buddhism, held great assemblies and with incense and flowers lined the road weeping to send him off.

sentences.zh: 潛歎曰：「正恐不久復來耳！

translations.literal: Qian sighed: "I fear before long I shall come again!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian sighed: "I fear I shall soon be back!"

sentences.zh: 」至鄴未幾，復為揚州道行台尚書。

translations.literal: At Ye not long after, he was again made Mobile Staff Director on the Yangzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye, before long, he was again made mobile staff director on the Yangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，陳將吳明徹來寇，領軍封輔相赴援。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Chen general Wu Mingche came to raid; the army commander Feng Fuxiang went to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Chen general Wu Mingche raided; army commander Feng Fuxiang went to rescue.

sentences.zh: 陳兵及峴，輔相不從，潛固爭不得，憂憤發病，臥幕下，果敗。

translations.literal: Chen troops reached Xian; Fuxiang would not follow; Qian argued firmly in vain, worried and angry fell ill, lay under the tent, and was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chen troops reached Xian; Fuxiang would not follow; Qian argued in vain, fell ill with worry and anger, lay under the tent, and defeat followed.

sentences.zh: 陳人遂圍壽陽，壅芍陂，以水灌之。

translations.literal: Chen men then besieged Shouyang, dammed the Shao Pond, and flooded it with water.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen then besieged Shouyang, dammed the Shao Pond, and flooded the city.

sentences.zh: 詔王長春為南討都督。

translations.literal: An edict made Wang Changchun southern campaign commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wang Changchun commander-in-chief of the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 長春軍次河南，多給兵士糧，便鳴角欲引，而賤糴其米；

translations.literal: Changchun's army halted south of the river, much issuing grain to soldiers, then sounded horns intending to withdraw yet selling rice cheap;
translations.idiomatic: Changchun's army halted south of the river, issued much grain to the troops, then sounded horns to withdraw while selling rice cheap;

sentences.zh: 及頓兵，更貴糶其米。

translations.literal: When encamped he sold rice dear again.
translations.idiomatic: When he encamped he sold rice dear again.

sentences.zh: 乃與皮景和擁眾十萬於淮北，不進。

translations.literal: Then he and Pi Jinghe held a host of a hundred thousand on the north bank of the Huai and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He and Pi Jinghe held a hundred thousand on the north bank of the Huai and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 壽陽城中青黑龍升天，城尋陷。

translations.literal: In Shouyang city a blue-black dragon rose to heaven; the city soon fell.
translations.idiomatic: A blue-black dragon rose from Shouyang; the city soon fell.

sentences.zh: 潛及行台僕射王貴顯、特進巴陵王王琳、扶風王可硃渾孝裕、武衛將軍奚永樂、儀同索景和、仁州刺史酈伯偉、霍州刺史封子繡、泰州刺史高子植、行台左丞李騊駼等督將五十八，軍士一萬，皆沒焉。

translations.literal: Qian and Mobile Staff Vice Director Wang Guixian, Special Advancement Prince of Baling Wang Lin, Prince of Fufeng Kezhuhun Xiaoyu, Martial Guard General Xi Yongle, Peer Suo Jinghe, Governor of Renzhou Li Bowei, Governor of Huozhou Feng Zixiu, Governor of Taizhou Gao Zizhi, Mobile Staff Left Aide Li Taotu, and other supervising generals—fifty-eight in all—and ten thousand soldiers were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, mobile staff vice director Wang Guixian, special advancement Prince of Baling Wang Lin, Prince of Fufeng Kezhuhun Xiaoyu, martial guard general Xi Yongle, peer Suo Jinghe, governors Li Bowei, Feng Zixiu, and Gao Zizhi, mobile staff left aide Li Taotu, and fifty-eight other supervising generals with ten thousand soldiers were all lost.

sentences.zh: 陳人殺王琳，餘皆囚於東冶。

translations.literal: The Chen killed Wang Lin; the rest were all imprisoned in the eastern foundry.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen killed Wang Lin; the rest were imprisoned in the eastern foundry.

sentences.zh: 陳主欲知齊之虛實，乃出潛，曰：「囚本屬幽州，于河北最小，口有五十萬，落陳者，唯與酈伯偉二人耳。」

translations.literal: The Chen ruler wished to know Qi's strength and weakness, so he released Qian and said: "Prisoners originally belong to Youzhou; of Hebei's smallest districts one has five hundred thousand people—those who fell to Chen are only you and Li Bowei."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler wished to know Qi's strength and released Qian, saying: "Prisoners belong to Youzhou; of Hebei's smallest districts there are five hundred thousand people—those who fell to Chen are only you and Li Bowei."

sentences.zh: 時李騊駼將逃歸，並要潛。

translations.literal: At the time Li Taotu was about to escape and return, and also urged Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Taotu was about to escape and urged Qian to come.

sentences.zh: 潛曰：「我此頭面，何可誑人？

translations.literal: Qian said: "With this face of mine, how could I deceive people?
translations.idiomatic: Qian said: "With this face, how could I deceive anyone?"

sentences.zh: 吾少時，相者云：沒在吳越地。

translations.literal: In my youth a physiognomist said I would perish in Wu-Yue lands.
translations.idiomatic: In youth a physiognomist said I would die in Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 死生已定，弟其行也。

translations.literal: Life and death are already fixed; brother, go on your way.
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are fixed; brother, go.

sentences.zh: 」因寄書與弟士邃曰：「吾夢汝以某月某日得患，某月某日漸損。

translations.literal: He then sent a letter to his younger brother Shi Sui saying: "I dreamed you would fall ill on such-and-such month and day, and on such-and-such month and day would gradually recover."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a letter to his brother Shi Sui: "I dreamed you would fall ill on such a day and recover on such a day."

sentences.zh: 」皆如其言。

translations.literal: It all happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It all came true.

sentences.zh: 既而歎曰：「壽陽陷，吾以頸血濺城而死，佛教不聽自殺，故荏苒偷生，今可死矣！

translations.literal: Then he sighed: "Shouyang has fallen; I ought to have splashed the city with the blood of my neck, but Buddhism forbids suicide, so I have dragged on in stolen life—now I may die!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he sighed: "Shouyang has fallen; I should have dyed the walls with my neck's blood, but Buddhism forbids suicide, so I dragged on—now I may die!"

sentences.zh: 」於是閉氣而絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he held his breath and died.
translations.idiomatic: He held his breath and died.

sentences.zh: 其家購屍歸葬，贈開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His family bought back the corpse for burial; he was posthumously enfeoffed Peer with Protocol Equal to Three Excellencies, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family bought back the corpse for burial; he was posthumously peer with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, left vice director of the masters of writing, and governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟士邃子元孝嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Shi Sui's son Yuan Xiaosi was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; his brother Shi Sui's son Yuan Xiaosi was made heir.

sentences.zh: 潛雅性貞固。

translations.literal: Qian's nature was upright and firm by habit.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was upright and firm by nature.

sentences.zh: 祖珽常要潛陷仁州刺史劉逖，許以高位。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ting often wanted Qian to entrap Governor of Renzhou Liu Di and promised him high office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ting often wanted Qian to entrap Renzhou governor Liu Di and promised high office.

sentences.zh: 潛曰：「如此事，吾不為也。

translations.literal: Qian said: "Such a thing I will not do."
translations.idiomatic: Qian said: "I will not do such a thing."

sentences.zh: 」行台慕容恃德常所推重，有疾，謂其子曰：「盧尚書教我為人，有如昆弟。

translations.literal: Mobile Staff Chief Murong Shide often promoted and valued him; when ill he told his son: "Director Lu taught me how to live, like elder and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile staff chief Murong Shide often valued him; when ill he told his son: "Director Lu taught me to live like brothers."

sentences.zh: 我死，持上騂馬與之。

translations.literal: When I die, present him with the best chestnut-colored horse.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, give him my best chestnut horse."

sentences.zh: 」其子以他馬往。

translations.literal: The son took another horse.
translations.idiomatic: The son brought another horse.

sentences.zh: 恃德柩出門自停，不可動，巫祝以為恃德聲怒曰：「何不與盧尚書我所騎騂馬？

translations.literal: When Shide's bier went out the gate it stopped of itself and could not move; the shaman said Shide's voice angrily said: "Why not give Director Lu the chestnut horse I rode?"
translations.idiomatic: Shide's bier stopped at the gate and would not move; the shaman said Shide angrily asked why they had not given Director Lu the chestnut horse he rode.

sentences.zh: 」其子遽奉命，柩乃行。

translations.literal: The son hastily obeyed, and then the bier moved.
translations.idiomatic: The son obeyed at once, and the bier moved.

sentences.zh: 潛以馬價為營福事。

translations.literal: Qian used the horse's price for merit-making.
translations.idiomatic: Qian used the horse's price for merit-making.

sentences.zh: 其為時重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he commanded.

sentences.zh: 士邃字子淹，少為崔昂所知。

translations.literal: Shi Sui, styled Ziyan, in youth was known to Cui Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui, styled Ziyan, was known in youth to Cui Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂云：「此昆季足為後生之俊，但恨其俱不讀書耳。

translations.literal: Ang said: "These brothers are enough to be outstanding men of the later generation—only a pity they do not read books."
translations.idiomatic: Ang said: "These brothers could be the finest of their generation—only it is a pity they do not read."

sentences.zh: 」位尚書左右丞、吏部郎中、中山太守帶定州長史。

translations.literal: Posts: Left and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Administrator of Zhongshan with concurrent Chief Clerk of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He reached left and right vice director of the masters of writing, director in the ministry of personnel, and administrator of Zhongshan with concurrent chief clerk of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊亡後，卒。

translations.literal: After Qi perished he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell he died.

sentences.zh: 度世之為濟州也，魏初平升城。

translations.literal: When Dushi was in Jizhou, in early Wei the city of Shengcheng was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Dushi was in Jizhou, in early Wei Shengcheng was pacified.

sentences.zh: 無鹽房崇吉母傅，度世繼外祖母兄之子婦也，兗州刺史申纂妻賈氏，崇吉之姑女也，皆亡破，老病憔悴。

translations.literal: Wu salt Fang Chongji's mother Fu—Dushi's wife by succession from his maternal cousin's son's wife—and Jia, wife of Yanzhou Governor Shen Zuan, Chongji's aunt's daughter, were both ruined in war, old, ill, and wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Chongji's mother Fu of Wuyan—Dushi's wife by succession through his maternal cousin's son's wife—and Jia, wife of Yanzhou governor Shen Zuan, Chongji's aunt's daughter, were ruined in war, old, ill, and wasted.

sentences.zh: 而度世推計中表，致其供恤。

translations.literal: Yet Dushi reckoned middle and outer kin and sent them support.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Dushi reckoned kinship and sent them support.

sentences.zh: 每覲見傅氏，跪問起居，隨時奉送衣被食物；

translations.literal: Whenever he saw the Lady Fu he knelt to ask after her health and at each season sent clothing and food;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw Lady Fu he knelt to ask after her and sent clothing and food each season;

sentences.zh: 亦存賑賈氏，供其服膳。

translations.literal: he also relieved the Lady Jia and supplied her meals.
translations.idiomatic: he also relieved Lady Jia and supplied her meals.

sentences.zh: 青州既陷，諸崔墜落，多所收贖。

translations.literal: When Qingzhou fell, many of the Cui clan were cast down and he ransomed many.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhou fell many Cui were ruined and he ransomed many.

sentences.zh: 及伯源、昶等，並循父風。

translations.literal: Boyuan, Chang, and the rest all followed their fathers' manner.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan, Chang, and the rest all followed their fathers' ways.

sentences.zh: 遠親疏屬，敘為尊行長者，莫不畢拜致敬。

translations.literal: Distant and close kin he ranked as elders; none failed to bow in full respect.
translations.idiomatic: Distant and close kin he treated as elders; all bowed to him in respect.

sentences.zh: 閨門之禮，為世所推。

translations.literal: Household ritual was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Household ritual was praised in the age.

sentences.zh: 謙退簡約，不與世競。

translations.literal: Humble, retiring, and simple, he did not compete with the world.
translations.idiomatic: He was humble, retiring, and simple and did not compete with the world.

sentences.zh: 父母亡後，同居共財，自祖至孫，家內百口。

translations.literal: After his parents died they lived together sharing property—from grandfather to grandson, a hundred mouths within the house.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died they lived together sharing property—from grandfather to grandson, a hundred mouths in one house.

sentences.zh: 在洛時，有饑年，無以自贍，然尊卑怡穆，豐儉同之。

translations.literal: In Luoyang there was a famine year and no means to support themselves, yet elders and juniors were harmonious and rich and poor shared alike.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang in a famine year they could not support themselves, yet elders and juniors were harmonious and rich and poor shared alike.

sentences.zh: 親從昆季，常旦省諸父，出坐別室，暮乃入內。

translations.literal: Close cousins would each morning visit their fathers, sit in a separate room, and only at evening enter the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Close cousins each morning visited their fathers, sat in a separate room, and only at evening entered within.

sentences.zh: 朝府之外，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Outside court and office they did not socialize idly.
translations.idiomatic: Outside court and office they did not socialize lightly.

sentences.zh: 其相勖以禮，如此。

translations.literal: They urged one another with ritual thus.
translations.idiomatic: They urged one another with ritual thus.

sentences.zh: 又一門三主，當世以為榮。

translations.literal: Moreover one household had three lords—a glory of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover one household had three lords, a glory of the age.

sentences.zh: 伯源兄弟亡，及道將卒後，家風衰損。

translations.literal: After Boyuan's brothers died and after Daojiang died, the family manner declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Boyuan's brothers and Daojiang died, the family manner declined.

sentences.zh: 子孫多有非法，幃薄混穢，為時所鄙。

translations.literal: Descendants often acted unlawfully; inner chambers were foul and mixed, and they were despised by the time.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants often broke the law; inner chambers were foul, and contemporaries despised them.

sentences.zh: 度世從祖弟神寶，位中書博士。

translations.literal: Dushi's younger cousin Shenbao, post: Doctor of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi's cousin Shenbao was doctor of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝文為弟高陽王雍納其女為妃。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen for his younger brother Prince of Gaoyang Wang Yong took Shenbao's daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen for his brother Prince of Gaoyang Wang Yong took Shenbao's daughter as consort.

sentences.zh: 初，玄從祖兄溥，慕容寶之末，統攝鄉部屯海濱，殺其鄉姻諸祖十餘人，稱征北大將軍、幽州刺史，攻掠郡縣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xuan's elder cousin's brother Pu, at the end of Murong Bao's reign, controlled the district by the sea, killed more than ten of his village kin and elders, styled himself Defender-General of the North and Governor of Youzhou, and raided prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xuan's elder cousin's brother Pu, at the end of Murong Bao's reign, controlled the coast district, killed more than ten village kin and elders, styled himself defender-general of the north and governor of Youzhou, and raided prefectures.

sentences.zh: 天興中，討禽之。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era he was captured in the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing he was captured in the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 溥玄孫洪，字曾孫。

translations.literal: Pu's great-grandson Hong, styled Zengsun.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's great-grandson was Hong, styled Zengsun.

sentences.zh: 太和中，位中書博士，樂陵、陽平二郡太守，幽州中正。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era posts: Doctor of the Palace Secretariat, Administrator of Leling and Yangping, Rectifier of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he was doctor of the palace secretariat, administrator of Leling and Yangping, and rectifier of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪三子。

translations.literal: Hong had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長子崇，少立美名，有識者許之以遠大，卒於驃騎府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: The eldest son Chong had early established a fine name; men of discernment promised him great future, but he died as Legal Affairs Aide in the Fast Cavalry Office.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest Chong early won a fine name; discerning men promised him a great future, but he died as legal affairs aide in the fast cavalry office.

sentences.zh: 崇子柔。

translations.literal: Chong's son was Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's son was Rou.

sentences.zh: 柔字子剛。

translations.literal: Rou, styled Zigang.
translations.idiomatic: Rou was styled Zigang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為叔母所養，撫視甚於其子。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised by his aunt, who cared for him more than for her own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his aunt, who cared for him more than her own sons.

sentences.zh: 柔盡心溫清，亦同己親，親族歎重之。

translations.literal: Rou devoted himself in warm attendance as to his own kin; kin praised and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Rou served her with full devotion as to his own kin; kin praised him.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏好學，未冠解屬文。

translations.literal: By nature clever and fond of learning, before the cap he could compose linked prose.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and fond of learning, before the cap he could compose linked prose.

sentences.zh: 但口吃，不能持論。

translations.literal: But he stammered and could not sustain debate.
translations.idiomatic: But he stammered and could not sustain debate.

sentences.zh: 頗使酒誕節，為世所譏。

translations.literal: He rather indulged wine and wild conduct, for which the age mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged wine and wild conduct, for which the age mocked him.

sentences.zh: 司徒、臨淮王彧見而器之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Prince of Linhuai Wang Yu saw and valued him, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Linhuai Wang Yu valued him and gave him his daughter.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武與齊神武有隙，詔賀拔勝出牧荊州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and Qi Shenwu had a rift, an edict had Heba Sheng go out to govern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu of Wei and Qi Shenwu quarreled, an edict sent Heba Sheng to govern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 柔謂因此可著功績，遂從勝之荊州。

translations.literal: Rou thought that through this he could achieve merit, and followed Sheng to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rou thought merit could be won thereby and followed Sheng to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以柔為大行台郎中，掌書記，軍之機務，柔多預之。

translations.literal: Rou was made Director of the Great Mobile Staff, in charge of records; military affairs Rou largely shared in.
translations.idiomatic: Rou was made director of the great mobile staff in charge of records; he largely shared in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 及勝為太保，以柔為掾。

translations.literal: When Sheng became Grand Tutor, Rou was made his aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng became grand tutor, Rou was made his aide.

sentences.zh: 孝武后召勝引兵赴洛，勝以問柔。

translations.literal: Later Xiaowu summoned Sheng to bring troops to Luoyang; Sheng asked Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaowu summoned Sheng to bring troops to Luoyang, and Sheng consulted Rou.

sentences.zh: 柔曰：「高歡托晉陽之甲，意實難知。

translations.literal: Rou said: "Gao Huan relying on the armor of Jinyang—his intent is truly hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Rou said: "Gao Huan with Jinyang's armies behind him—his intent is hard to know."

sentences.zh: 公宜席捲赴都，與決勝負，存沒以之，此忠之上策也。

translations.literal: My lord ought to sweep forward to the capital and decide victory or defeat with him, life or death by that—this is the loyal man's upper stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: You should sweep to the capital and decide victory with him, staking life and death on it—that is the loyal man's best plan."

sentences.zh: 若北阻魯陽，南並舊楚，東連兗、豫，西接關中，帶甲十萬，觀釁而動，亦中策也。

translations.literal: If you block north at Luyang, join south with the old Chu, link east with Yan and Yu, and connect west with Guanzhong, with a hundred thousand in armor watching for an opening to move—that is also the middle stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Block north at Luyang, join south with old Chu, link east with Yan and Yu, connect west with Guanzhong, keep a hundred thousand in armor and move when the moment comes—that is the middle plan."

sentences.zh: 舉三荊之地，通款梁國，可以庇身，功名去矣，策之下者。

translations.literal: Raise the three Jing provinces, send terms to Liang, and you may shelter your person—but fame and merit are gone; that is the lower stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Raise the three Jing provinces and treat with Liang—you may save yourself, but fame and merit are gone; that is the worst plan."

sentences.zh: 」勝輕柔年少，笑而不應。

translations.literal: Sheng thought Rou young and laughed without answering.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng deemed Rou too young and laughed without reply.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，東魏遣侯景襲穰。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu moved west, Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing to raid Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu fled west, Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing against Xiang.

sentences.zh: 勝敗，遂南奔梁，柔亦從之。

translations.literal: Sheng was defeated and fled south to Liang; Rou followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was beaten and fled south to Liang, Rou with him.

sentences.zh: 勝頻表梁武帝，求歸關中。

translations.literal: Sheng repeatedly memorialized Emperor Wu of Liang asking to return to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng repeatedly memorialized Liang Wudi asking to return to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝覽表，嘉其辭彩，既知柔所制，因遣舍人勞問，並遺縑錦。

translations.literal: Liang Wudi read the memorials, admired their literary color, and knowing Rou had composed them, sent an attendant to console him and also gave silk brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi read the memorials, admired their style, learned Rou had written them, sent an attendant to console him, and gave silk brocade.

sentences.zh: 後與勝俱還，行至襄陽。

translations.literal: Later he returned with Sheng; when they reached Xiangyang,
translations.idiomatic: He later returned with Sheng; at Xiangyang,

sentences.zh: 齊神武懼勝西入，遣侯景以輕騎邀之。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu feared Sheng would enter west and sent Hou Jing with light cavalry to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu feared Sheng would go west and sent Hou Jing with light cavalry to intercept.

sentences.zh: 勝及柔懼，乃棄船山行，贏糧冒險，經數百里。

translations.literal: Sheng and Rou were afraid and abandoned the boats to travel by mountain, carrying grain on their backs through danger for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Rou were afraid, abandoned their boats, went by mountain carrying grain on their backs through danger for several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 時屬秋霖，徒侶凍餒者，太半至於死。

translations.literal: It was autumn rains; companions who froze and starved were more than half, even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: It was autumn rain; more than half the party froze and starved, many unto death.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，至長安，封容城縣男。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong they reached Chang'an and he was enfeoffed Baron of Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong they reached Chang'an; he was enfeoffed Baron of Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 周文帝引為行台郎中，除從事中郎。

translations.literal: Zhou Wendi brought him in as mobile staff director, then made him Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wendi brought him in as mobile staff director, then attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 與郎中蘇綽掌機密。

translations.literal: With Director Su Chuo he managed secrets.
translations.idiomatic: With director Su Chuo he managed secrets.

sentences.zh: 時沙苑之役，大軍屢捷，汝、潁之間，多舉義來附。

translations.literal: At the time of the Shaye campaign the great army won repeatedly; between Ru and Ying many rose in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shaye campaign the army won repeatedly; between Ru and Ying many rose in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 書翰往反，日百餘牒，柔隨機報答，皆合事宜。

translations.literal: Letters went back and forth, more than a hundred documents a day; Rou answered as occasion required, all fitting the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Letters went back and forth, more than a hundred a day; Rou answered as occasion required, all fitting the matter.

sentences.zh: 進爵為子。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Baronet.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to baronet.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎，兼著作，撰直居注。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently in the Historiography Office writing the Straight Residence Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the secretariat, concurrently writing the straight residence annals.

sentences.zh: 後為黃門侍郎，周文知其貧，解衣賜之。

translations.literal: Later he was Yellow Gate Attendant; Zhou Wen knew he was poor and gave him his own robe.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was yellow gate attendant; Zhou Wen knew he was poor and gave him his robe.

sentences.zh: 後遷中書監。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，拜小內史大夫，進位開府儀同三司，卒於位。

translations.literal: When Zhou Xiaomin Di ascended the throne he was appointed Junior Inner History Grandee, advanced to Peer with Protocol Equal to Three Excellencies, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Xiaomin Di ascended he was junior inner history grandee, advanced to peer with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 所作詩、頌、碑、銘、檄、表、啟行於世者數十篇。

translations.literal: Poems, eulogies, steles, inscriptions, proclamations, memorials, and reports he composed that circulated in the world number several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Poems, eulogies, steles, inscriptions, proclamations, memorials, and reports circulating in the world number several tens.

sentences.zh: 子愷嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 愷字長仁。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Changren.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was styled Changren.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，神情穎悟，涉獵經史，有當世幹能，頗解屬文。

translations.literal: Filial and friendly by nature, keen in spirit and quick to understand, he ranged through classics and histories and had talent for the age, and could compose linked prose fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and friendly, keen and quick to understand, he ranged through classics and histories, had talent for the age, and could compose linked prose fairly well.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲引為記室。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Wang Xian brought him in as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Wang Xian brought him in as recorder.

sentences.zh: 從憲伐齊，說齊柏社鎮下之。

translations.literal: Following Xian's campaign against Qi he persuaded Qi to surrender the garrison of Baishe.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xian's campaign against Qi he persuaded Qi to surrender Baishe garrison.

sentences.zh: 遷小吏部大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 時染工王神歡者，以賂自進，塚宰宇文護擢為計部下大夫。

translations.literal: At the time the dyer Wang Shenhuan advanced by bribery; Grand Minister Yuwen Hu promoted him to Director under the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the time dyer Wang Shenhuan advanced by bribery; Grand Minister Yuwen Hu made him director under the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 愷諫曰：「古者，登高能賦，可為大夫；

translations.literal: Kai remonstrated: "In antiquity, one who from a high place could compose rhapsodies might become a grandee;
translations.idiomatic: Kai remonstrated: "In antiquity one who from a high place could compose rhapsodies might become a grandee;

sentences.zh: 求賢審官，理須詳慎。

translations.literal: seeking the worthy and examining officeholders—reason demands careful scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: seeking the worthy and examining officeholders demands careful scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 今神歡出自染工，更無殊異，徒以家富自通，遂與晉紳並列，實恐鵜翼之刺，聞之外境。

translations.literal: Now Shenhuan came from dyeing work with nothing extraordinary; he merely used family wealth to gain access and now stands among Jin gentry—a thing that truly fears the pelican's sting reaching foreign borders.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shenhuan came from dyeing with nothing extraordinary; he merely bought his way among Jin gentry—a thing that truly fears the pelican's sting will reach foreign borders.

sentences.zh: 」護竟寢其事。

translations.literal: Hu in the end shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Hu in the end shelved the matter.

sentences.zh: 轉內史下大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Inner History Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to junior inner history grandee.

sentences.zh: 武帝在雲陽宮，敕諸屯簡老牛，欲以享士。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was at Yunyang Palace and ordered the garrisons to select old oxen to feast the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di was at Yunyang Palace and ordered the garrisons to pick old oxen to feast the troops.

sentences.zh: 愷諫曰：「昔田子方贖老馬，君子以為美談。

translations.literal: Kai remonstrated: "Formerly Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse—the gentleman took it as a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: Kai remonstrated: "Formerly Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse—the gentleman praised it."

sentences.zh: 向奉明敕，欲以老牛享士，有虧仁政。

translations.literal: Now following the bright edict to feast the troops with old oxen harms humane government.
translations.idiomatic: Now following the edict to feast the troops with old oxen harms humane government.

sentences.zh: 」帝美其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部大夫，為聘陳使副。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grandee of the Ministry of Rites and served as deputy on the embassy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grandee of the ministry of rites and served as deputy on the embassy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 先是，行人多從其國禮，及愷為使，一依本朝，陳人莫能屈。

translations.literal: Earlier envoys mostly followed Chen ritual; when Kai was envoy he followed his own court entirely, and Chen men could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier envoys mostly followed Chen ritual; when Kai was envoy he followed his own court entirely, and the Chen could not bend him.

sentences.zh: 建德四年，李穆攻拔軹關、柏崖二鎮，命愷作露布。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiande Li Mu captured the garrisons of Zhiguan and Baiya and ordered Kai to compose a victory bulletin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiande Li Mu captured Zhiguan and Baiya garrisons and ordered Kai to compose a victory bulletin.

sentences.zh: 帝讀大悅曰：「盧愷文章大進，荀景茜故是令君之子。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and greatly rejoiced: "Lu Kai's writing has greatly advanced—Xun Jingqian is indeed Lord Ling's son."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and rejoiced: "Lu Kai's writing has greatly advanced—Xun Jingqian is indeed Lord Ling's son."

sentences.zh: 」大象元年，拜東都吏部大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang he was appointed Grandee of the Eastern Capital Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang he was grandee of the eastern capital ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，加上儀同三司，除尚書吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kai Kai was given superior protocol equal to Three Excellencies and made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui he was given superior protocol equal to the Three Excellencies and made vice director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，仍攝尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Marquis and still held concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to marquis and still held concurrent left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 每有敷奏，侃然正色，雖逢喜怒，不改其常。

translations.literal: Whenever he memorialized he spoke forthrightly with proper color; even meeting anger or joy he did not change his constant manner.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he memorialized he spoke forthrightly; even meeting anger or joy he did not change.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was given addition as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was given addition as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 八年，上親考百僚，以愷為上，固讓不敢受。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Emperor personally examined the hundred officials and ranked Kai first; he firmly declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor personally examined the hundred officials and ranked Kai first; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「當仁不讓，何愧之有？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "When duty calls one does not yield—what shame is there?
translations.idiomatic: Wen Di said: "When duty calls one does not yield—what shame is there?"

sentences.zh: 皆在朕心，無勞飾讓。

translations.literal: All is in Our heart; no need for false modesty.
translations.idiomatic: All is in my heart; no need for false modesty."

sentences.zh: 」歲餘，拜禮部尚書，攝吏部尚書事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Minister of Rites, holding charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was minister of rites, holding charge of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 會國子博士何妥與右僕射蘇威不平，奏威陰事，愷坐與相連。

translations.literal: When National University Erudite He Tuo and Right Vice Director Su Wei were at odds, Tuo memorialized Wei's secret matters and Kai sat connected.
translations.idiomatic: When national university erudite He Tuo and right vice director Su Wei quarreled, Tuo memorialized Wei's secret matters and Kai was implicated.

sentences.zh: 憲司奏愷曰：「房恭懿者，尉遲迥之党，不當仕進。

translations.literal: The censorate memorialized Kai: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yu Chi Tong and ought not to advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate memorialized Kai: "Fang Gongyi was Yu Chi Tong's partisan and ought not to advance."

sentences.zh: 威、愷二人，曲相薦達，累轉海州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei and Kai bent the rules to recommend and advance him, repeatedly promoting him to Governor of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Kai bent the rules to recommend him, repeatedly promoting him to governor of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 吏部預選者甚多，愷不即授官，皆注色而遣。

translations.literal: Many were pre-selected in the Ministry of Personnel; Kai did not immediately grant office but marked their names in color and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Many were pre-selected in the ministry of personnel; Kai did not immediately grant office but marked their names in color and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 威之從父弟徹、肅二人，並以鄉正征詣吏部。

translations.literal: Wei's younger cousins Che and Su were both summoned as village rectifiers to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger cousins Che and Su were both summoned as village rectifiers to the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 徹文狀後至，而先任用。

translations.literal: Che's literary documents arrived late yet he was appointed first.
translations.idiomatic: Che's documents arrived late yet he was appointed first.

sentences.zh: 肅左足攣蹇，才用無算，愷以威故，授朝請郎。

translations.literal: Su's left foot was crippled and his talent was unmeasured; Kai because of Wei made him Gentleman for Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Su's left foot was crippled and his talent unmeasured; Kai because of Wei made him gentleman for palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 愷之朋黨，事甚明白。

translations.literal: Kai's factional conduct was very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's factional conduct was very clear.

sentences.zh: 」上大怒曰：「愷敢將天官以為私惠！

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered: "Kai dares to treat the celestial offices as private favor!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered: "Kai dares to treat the celestial offices as private favor!"

sentences.zh: 」愷免冠頓首曰：「皇太子將以通事舍人蘇夔為舍人。

translations.literal: Kai doffed his cap and knocked his head: "The crown prince was about to make Su Kui of the Communications Office a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kai doffed his cap and knocked his head: "The crown prince was about to make Su Kui of the communications office a palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 夔，威之子，臣以夔未當遷，固啟而止。

translations.literal: Kui is Wei's son; your servant held Kui unfit for promotion and firmly remonstrated to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Kui is Wei's son; I held Kui unfit and firmly remonstrated to stop it.

sentences.zh: 臣若與威有私，豈當如此？

translations.literal: If I had private dealings with Wei, would I have acted thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Had I private dealings with Wei, would I have done so?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「威子，朝廷共知，卿乃固執，以徼身幸；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Wei's son the court all knows; you were obstinate to seek personal fortune;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wei's son the court all knows; you were obstinate to seek fortune;"

sentences.zh: 至所不知，便行朋附。

translations.literal: what you did not know you carried out as factional support.
translations.idiomatic: what you did not know, you backed as faction.

sentences.zh: 奸臣之行也。

translations.literal: That is the conduct of a treacherous minister.
translations.idiomatic: That is the conduct of a treacherous minister."

sentences.zh: 」於是除名，卒於家。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was removed from name and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 自周氏以降，選無清濁。

translations.literal: From the Zhou house onward selection had no clear or muddy.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou onward office selection had neither clear nor muddy ranks.

sentences.zh: 及愷攝吏部，與薛道衡、陸彥師等甄別士流，故涉黨錮之譖，遂及於此。

translations.literal: When Kai held charge of the Ministry of Personnel, with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others he sorted the gentry stream—hence he fell into the calumny of partisan prohibition and came to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai held the ministry of personnel, with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi he sorted the gentry stream—hence he fell into partisan calumny and came to this.

sentences.zh: 崇弟仲義，字小黑，知名於世，位員外散騎侍郎、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Zhongyi, styled Xiaohei, was renowned in the world, post: Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant, Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's brother Zhongyi, styled Xiaohei, was renowned, reaching supernumerary regular cavalier attendant and governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇兄弟官雖不達，婚姻常與玄家齊等。

translations.literal: Chong's brothers' offices though not high, their marriages were always equal to Xuan's house.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chong's brothers never rose high, their marriages always matched Xuan's house.

sentences.zh: 洪弟光宗，位尚書郎。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Guangzong, post: Director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's brother Guangzong was director in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 光宗子觀。

translations.literal: Guangzong's son was Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's son was Guan.

sentences.zh: 觀弟仲宣，小名金。

translations.literal: Guan's younger brother Zhongxuan, childhood name Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's brother Zhongxuan, childhood name Jin.

sentences.zh: 才學優洽，乃逾於觀，但文體頗細。

translations.literal: His learning was broad and harmonious and surpassed Guan, but his literary style was rather fine-grained.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was broad and surpassed Guan, but his style was rather fine.

sentences.zh: 兄弟俱以文章顯，論者美之。

translations.literal: The brothers were all famed for literature; opinion praised them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers all won fame in letters, and opinion praised them.

sentences.zh: 位太尉屬。

translations.literal: Post: Aide in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: He reached aide in the grand marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊帝初，遇害河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang of Wei he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 及兄觀並無子，文集莫為撰次，罕有存者。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Guan both had no sons; collected works were not compiled and few survive.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brother Guan both had no sons; collected works were not compiled and few survive.

sentences.zh: 仲宣弟叔彪。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's younger brother Shubiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's brother was Shubiao.

sentences.zh: 叔彪在鄉時，有粟千石，每至春夏，鄉人無食者，令自載取。

translations.literal: Shubiao in his district had a thousand piculs of grain; each spring and summer when villagers had no food he let them load and take.
translations.idiomatic: Shubiao kept a thousand piculs in his district; each spring and summer when neighbors had no food he let them load what they needed.

sentences.zh: 至秋，任還其價而不計。

translations.literal: In autumn he let them return the price without reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he let them repay the price without counting interest.

sentences.zh: 歲歲常得倍餘。

translations.literal: Year after year he regularly gained more than double.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he still came out more than double ahead.

sentences.zh: 既在朝通貴，自以年老，兒子又多，遂營一大屋，曰：「歌于斯，哭於斯。

translations.literal: Once in court at high rank, seeing himself old with many sons, he built a great house and said: "We sing here, we weep here."
translations.idiomatic: Once he stood high in court, old and with many sons, he built a great house and said, "Here we sing; here we weep."

sentences.zh: 」魏收常來詣之，訪以洛京舊事。

translations.literal: Wei Shou often came to visit him and asked about old matters of the Luoyang capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou often came to visit and asked about old Luoyang matters.

sentences.zh: 不待食而起，云：「難為子費。

translations.literal: Without waiting for food he would rise and say: "Hard to be a burden on the young."
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for food he would rise and say: "Hard to burden the young."

sentences.zh: 」叔彪留之，良久食至，但有粟飡葵菜，木碗盛之，片脯而已。

translations.literal: Shubiao kept him; long after, food came—only millet meal and sunflower greens in a wooden bowl, with a slice of dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: Shubiao kept him; long after food came—only millet meal and sunflower greens in a wooden bowl, with a slice of dried meat.

sentences.zh: 所將僕從，亦盡設食，一與此同。

translations.literal: The servants he brought were all fed the same.
translations.idiomatic: The servants he brought were all fed the same.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，歸范陽。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he returned to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he returned to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 遭亂城陷，與族弟士邃皆以寒餒斃。

translations.literal: In the chaos the city fell; he and his cousin Shi Sui both died of cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos the city fell; he and his cousin Shi Sui both perished of cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 周將宇文神舉以二人有名德，收而葬之。

translations.literal: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, because the two had fame and virtue, collected and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, honoring their fame and virtue, gathered and buried them.

sentences.zh: 洪從弟附伯，附伯弟侍伯，並有學識。

translations.literal: Hong's younger cousin Fubo; Fubo's younger brother Shibo—both had learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's cousin Fubo; Fubo's brother Shibo—both had learning.

sentences.zh: 附伯位滄州平東府長史，侍伯南岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Fubo, post: Chief Clerk of Pingdong Office in Cangzhou; Shibo, Governor of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fubo was chief clerk of Pingdong office in Cangzhou; Shibo was governor of southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 侍伯從弟文偉。

translations.literal: Shibo's younger cousin Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo's cousin was Wenwei.

sentences.zh: 文偉字休族。

translations.literal: Wenwei, styled Xiuzu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei was styled Xiuzu.

sentences.zh: 父敞，位議郎，後以文偉勳，贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chang, post: Gentleman for Discussion, later because of Wenwei's merit enfeoffed Governor of Youzhou posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang was gentleman for discussion; later because of Wenwei's merit he was posthumously enfeoffed governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 文偉少孤，有志尚，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: Wenwei was orphaned young, had ambition, and ranged somewhat through classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei lost his father young, had ambition, and read somewhat in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province summoned him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 年三十八，始舉秀才，除本州平北府長流參軍。

translations.literal: At thirty-eight he first passed the cultivated-talent examination and was made Chief Clerk of the Long Flow in the Pacify-the-North Office of the province.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-eight he first passed the cultivated-talent examination and was made chief clerk of the long flow in the pacify-the-north office.

sentences.zh: 說刺史裴俊案舊跡修督亢陂，溉田萬餘傾，人賴其利。

translations.literal: He persuaded Governor Pei Jun to repair the Duguang embankment by old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing of fields; people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded Governor Pei Jun to repair the Duguang embankment by old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing; people relied on the benefit.

sentences.zh: 俊修立之功，多以委之。

translations.literal: Jun's merit in the repair he largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun largely entrusted the repair to him.

sentences.zh: 文偉既善於營理，兼展私力，家素貧儉，因此致富。

translations.literal: Wenwei was skilled at management and also expended private effort; the family had always been poor and frugal, and thereby grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei was skilled at management and also spent private effort; the family had always been poor and frugal, and thereby grew rich.

sentences.zh: 及北方將亂，文偉積稻穀于范陽城，時經荒儉，多所振贍，彌為鄉里所歸。

translations.literal: When the north was about to fall into chaos, Wenwei stored grain in Fanyang city; in years of famine he gave much relief and was all the more trusted by the district.
translations.idiomatic: When the north was about to fall into chaos, Wenwei stored grain in Fanyang; in famine years he gave much relief and was all the more trusted by the district.

sentences.zh: 及韓樓據薊城，文偉率鄉閭守范陽。

translations.literal: When Han Lou held Jicheng, Wenwei led the district to defend Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Lou seized Jicheng, Wenwei led the district in defending Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 樓平，以功封大夏縣男，除范陽太守。

translations.literal: When Lou was pacified, for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Daxia and made Administrator of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lou was pacified, for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Daxia and made administrator of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 莊帝崩，文偉與幽州刺史劉靈助同謀起義。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang of Wei died, Wenwei plotted uprising with Youzhou Governor Liu Lingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang Di of Wei died, Wenwei plotted uprising with Youzhou governor Liu Lingzhu.

sentences.zh: 靈助克瀛州，留文偉行州事，自率兵赴定州，為爾硃榮將侯深所敗。

translations.literal: Lingzhu took Yingzhou and left Wenwei to act for the province; he himself led troops to Dingzhou and was defeated by Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhu took Yingzhou and left Wenwei to act for the province; he led troops to Dingzhou and was defeated by Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen.

sentences.zh: 文偉走還本郡，仍與高乾兄弟相影響。

translations.literal: Wenwei fled back to his commandery and still moved in concert with the Gao brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei fled home and still acted in concert with the Gao brothers.

sentences.zh: 屬神武至信都，文偉遣子懷道奉啟陳謝。

translations.literal: When Shenwu reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with a memorial of apology.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with an apology.

sentences.zh: 中興初，除安州刺史，不之官，尋轉幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made Governor of Anzhou but did not take office; soon transferred to Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made governor of Anzhou but did not take office; soon transferred to governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 安州刺史盧曹亦從靈助舉兵。

translations.literal: Anzhou Governor Lu Cao also followed Lingzhu in raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhou governor Lu Cao also followed Lingzhu in raising troops.

sentences.zh: 靈助敗，因據幽州降爾硃兆。

translations.literal: When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao then held Youzhou and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao held Youzhou and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 兆仍以為刺史，據城不下，文偉不得入。

translations.literal: Zhao still made him governor; he held the city and would not descend, and Wenwei could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao still made him governor; he held the city and would not yield, and Wenwei could not enter.

sentences.zh: 後除青州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 文偉輕財愛客，善於撫接；

translations.literal: Wenwei was light with wealth and loved guests, skilled at soothing;
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei spent freely and loved guests, and was skilled at winning men;

sentences.zh: 好為小惠。

translations.literal: he liked to do small favors.
translations.idiomatic: he liked to do small favors.

sentences.zh: 是以所在頗得人情。

translations.literal: Hence wherever he went he largely won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he largely won people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 經紀生資，常若不足，致財積聚，承候寵要，餉遺不絕。

translations.literal: Managing livelihood he was always as if insufficient; amassing wealth and gathering stores, he attended on favor and power and gifts never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Managing livelihood he was always as if insufficient; amassing wealth, he attended on favor and power and gifts never ceased.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒公、尚書右僕射，諡曰孝威。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of the Secretariat, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous title Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously enfeoffed duke of the secretariat, right vice director of the masters of writing, posthumous title Xiaowei.

sentences.zh: 子恭道，性溫良，頗有文學。

translations.literal: His son Gongdao was gentle and kind and had some literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongdao was gentle, kind, and had some learning in letters.

sentences.zh: 位范陽郡太守，有德惠。

translations.literal: Post: Administrator of Fanyang Commandery, with virtue and grace.
translations.idiomatic: He was administrator of Fanyang commandery, with virtue and grace.

sentences.zh: 先文偉卒。

translations.literal: He died before Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Wenwei.

sentences.zh: 贈度支尚書，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Director of Revenue, posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed director of revenue, posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 子詢祖，襲祖爵大夏男。

translations.literal: His son Xunzu inherited the grandfather's enfeoffment as Baron of Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xunzu inherited his grandfather's barony of Daxia.

sentences.zh: 有術學，文辭華美，為後生之俊。

translations.literal: He had technical learning and splendid literary style—a outstanding man of the later generation.
translations.idiomatic: He had technical learning and splendid style—a outstanding man of his generation.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，至鄴。

translations.literal: He passed the cultivated-talent examination and reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the cultivated-talent examination and went to Ye.

sentences.zh: 趙郡李祖勳嘗宴諸文士。

translations.literal: Zhao commandery Li Zuxun once feasted various literary gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuxun of Zhao commandery once feasted various literary gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣使小黃門敕祖勳母曰：「蠕蠕既破，何無賀表？

translations.literal: Qi Wensuan sent a minor yellow gate to instruct Zuxun's mother: "The Rouran are broken—why no congratulatory memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: Wensuan sent a minor yellow gate to tell Zuxun's mother: "The Rouran are broken—where is your congratulatory memorial?"

sentences.zh: 」使者待之。

translations.literal: The envoy waited.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy waited.

sentences.zh: 諸賓皆為表，詢祖俄頃便成。

translations.literal: All the guests composed memorials; Xunzu finished his in a moment.
translations.idiomatic: All the guests wrote memorials; Xunzu finished his in an instant.

sentences.zh: 其詞云：「昔十萬橫行，樊將軍請而受屈；

translations.literal: His wording ran: "Once a hundred thousand rode rampant; General Fan begged and was humbled;
translations.idiomatic: His lines read: "Once a hundred thousand swept the land; Fan the general begged and bowed;

sentences.zh: 五千深入，李都尉降而不歸。

translations.literal: Five thousand pushed deep; Commandant Li surrendered and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand went deep; Commandant Li surrendered and never came back.

sentences.zh: 」時重其工。

translations.literal: " At the time they prized his craft.
translations.idiomatic: " People then prized his skill.

sentences.zh: 後朝廷大遷除，同日催拜。

translations.literal: Later the court made many transfers and dismissals, with investitures urged on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court shuffled many posts and urged same-day appointments.

sentences.zh: 詢祖立於東止車門外，為二十餘人作表，文不加點，辭理可觀。

translations.literal: Xun Zu stood outside the East Stop-Carriage Gate and drafted memorials for more than twenty men without adding a dot; the wording was sound.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu stood at the East Stop-Carriage Gate and wrote twenty-odd memorials at a stroke, all clear and polished.

sentences.zh: 詢祖初襲爵，有宿德朝士謂曰：「大夏初成」，詢祖應聲曰：「且得燕雀相賀」。

translations.literal: When Xun Zu first inherited the title, an elder statesman said, "Great Xia is newly built"; Xun Zu answered at once, "At least the sparrows and swallows may congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: On first inheriting the marquisate, an elder said, "Great Xia is newly built"; Xun Zu shot back, "At least sparrows and swallows can congratulate."

sentences.zh: 天保末，為築長城子使。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was deputy commissioner for building the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao he was deputy commissioner for the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 自負其才，內懷鬱怏，遂毀容服如賤役者以見楊愔。

translations.literal: Confident in his talent yet inwardly resentful, he ruined his dress and appeared like a menial to see Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Sure of his gifts but inwardly bitter, he dressed like a laborer to see Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 愔曰：「故舊皆有所縻，唯大夏未加處分。

translations.literal: Yin said: "Old friends all have some tie; only Great Xia has not yet been dealt with."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "Old friends all have some hold on us—only Great Xia has not been handled."

sentences.zh: 」詢祖厲聲曰：「是誰之咎？

translations.literal: " Xun Zu said sharply, "Whose fault is that?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xun Zu snapped, "Whose fault is that?"

sentences.zh: 」既至役所，作《築長城賦》以寄其意。

translations.literal: Once he reached the labor site he wrote "Fu on Building the Long Wall" to lodge his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: At the work site he wrote a "Fu on Building the Long Wall" to vent his mood.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「板則紫栢，杵則木瓜，何期材而斯用也？

translations.literal: In outline it runs: "Planks are purple cypress, pestles are papaya—who expected such timber for this use?
translations.idiomatic: It says in part, "Planks of purple cypress, pestles of papaya—who thought such wood for this job?

sentences.zh: 草則離離靡靡，緣岡而殖。

translations.literal: Grass spreads lush along the ridges and takes root.
translations.idiomatic: Grass grows thick along the hills.

sentences.zh: 但使十步而有一芳，余亦何辭間於荊棘。

translations.literal: If only every ten paces held one fragrant plant, I too would not mind dwelling among thorns."
translations.idiomatic: If every ten paces had a fragrant blade, I would not mind living among thorns."

sentences.zh: 」邢邵常戲曰：「卿小年才學富盛，戴角者無上齒，恐卿不壽。

translations.literal: Xing Shao often jested: "You are young yet your learning overflows; horned beasts have no upper teeth—I fear you will not live long."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao teased him: "Young as you are, your learning overflows; horned beasts lack upper teeth—I fear you will die young."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「詢祖初聞此言，實懷惕懼；

translations.literal: " He answered: "When Xun Zu first heard this I truly felt fear;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "At first I was afraid;

sentences.zh: 見丈人蒼蒼在鬢，差以自安。

translations.literal: seeing my elder's temples already gray, I took some comfort."
translations.idiomatic: but seeing your gray temples, I felt easier."

sentences.zh: 」邵甚重其敏贍。

translations.literal: " Shao greatly valued his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao prized his sharp tongue.

sentences.zh: 既有口辯，好臧否人物。

translations.literal: He had eloquence and loved to praise or blame people.
translations.idiomatic: Eloquent, he loved judging others.

sentences.zh: 眾共嫉之，言其淫于從妹。

translations.literal: All envied him, saying he had relations with a cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Many envied him, claiming an affair with a cousin.

sentences.zh: 宗人思道謂曰：「大夏何為招四海議？

translations.literal: Clansman Simiao said to him: "Great Xia, why invite talk from the four seas?"
translations.idiomatic: Kinsman Simiao asked, "Great Xia, why draw gossip from all under heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」詢祖曰：「骨肉還相殘，何況執玉帛者萬國。

translations.literal: " Xun Zu said: "Flesh and bone still tear at each other—how much more the ten thousand states bearing jade and silk."
translations.idiomatic: " Xun Zu said, "Kin still tear each other apart—what of ten thousand states bearing tribute?"

sentences.zh: 」與思道俱為北州人俊，魏收楊譽思道而以詢祖為不及。

translations.literal: " He and Simiao were both northern talents; Wei Shou praised Simiao and held Xun Zu inferior.
translations.idiomatic: He and Simiao were northern stars; Wei Shou praised Simiao and ranked Xun Zu below.

sentences.zh: 詢祖謂人曰：「見未能高飛者，借其羽毛；

translations.literal: Xun Zu told people: "Those who see one unable to soar high borrow his feathers;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu said, "Those who see one who cannot fly high borrow his feathers;

sentences.zh: 知逸勢沖天者，翦其翅翮。

translations.literal: those who know one whose momentum will pierce the sky clip his wings."
translations.idiomatic: those who know one destined to soar cut his pinions."

sentences.zh: 」既諸謗毀日至，素論皆薄其為人。

translations.literal: As slander mounted day by day, common opinion all slighted his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Slander piled up daily and opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 長廣太守邢子廣曰：「詢祖有規檢禰衡，思道無冰稜文舉。

translations.literal: Changguang prefect Xing Ziguang said: "Xun Zu has Mi Heng's standards; Simiao lacks Kong Rong's edge."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xing Ziguang said, "Xun Zu has Mi Heng's discipline; Simiao lacks Kong Rong's bite."

sentences.zh: 」後頗折節。

translations.literal: Later he somewhat restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he curbed himself somewhat.

sentences.zh: 曆太子舍人、司徒記室，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Crown Prince Attendant and Secretariat Recorder, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was Crown Prince Attendant and Secretariat Recorder, then died.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，皆遺逸。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls, all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ten scrolls of writings survive only by report.

sentences.zh: 恭道弟懷道，性輕率好酒，頗有慕尚。

translations.literal: Gongdao's younger brother Huaidao was light and fond of wine, with considerable ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Gongdao's brother Huaidao was reckless and fond of wine, yet ambitious.

sentences.zh: 既家預義舉，神武親待之。

translations.literal: Since his house took part in the righteous rising, Shenwu treated him with personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: His house had joined the righteous rising and Shenwu favored him personally.

sentences.zh: 卒于烏蘇鎮城都督。

translations.literal: He died as garrison commander of Wusu.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Wusu garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 懷道弟宗道，性粗率，動作狂俠，位南營州刺史。

translations.literal: Huaidao's younger brother Zongdao was coarse and rash, given to wild gallantry, and held the post of southern Yingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zongdao was rough and brash, a wild gallant, and southern Yingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 嘗于晉陽置酒，賓遊滿座；

translations.literal: Once at Jinyang he set out wine and guests filled the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Once in Jinyang he held a feast and the hall was full;

sentences.zh: 中書舍人馬士達目其彈箜篌女妓，雲手甚纖素，宗道即以遺之。
