translations.literal: Palace Attendant Ma Shida eyed his konghou girl and said her hands were very fine; Zongdao at once gave her to him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Ma Shida admired his konghou player's slender hands; Zongdao gave her to him at once.

sentences.zh: 士達固辭，宗道便命其家人，將解其腕，士達不得已而受之。

translations.literal: Shida firmly declined; Zongdao ordered his household to cut off her wrist, and Shida had no choice but to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shida refused; Zongdao ordered her wrist cut; Shida had to accept.

sentences.zh: 將赴營州，於督亢城坡，大集鄉人，殺牛聚會。

translations.literal: About to go to Yingzhou, at Dugu Slope he gathered the township, slaughtered oxen, and held a feast.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving for Yingzhou he feasted the township at Dugu Slope with slaughtered oxen.

sentences.zh: 有一舊門人，醉言疏失，宗道令沈之于水。

translations.literal: An old retainer, drunk, spoke loosely; Zongdao had him drowned.
translations.idiomatic: A drunken old retainer misspoke; Zongdao had him drowned.

sentences.zh: 後坐酷濫除名。

translations.literal: Later for cruel excess he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was removed for cruel excess.

sentences.zh: 玄族子輔，字顯光，本州別駕。

translations.literal: Xuanzu's son Fu, styled Xian-guang, was native-prefecture vice-governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzu's son Fu, styled Xian-guang, was native vice-governor.

sentences.zh: 子同。

translations.literal: Son Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Son Tong.

sentences.zh: 同字叔倫，身長八尺，容貌魁偉，善於處世。

translations.literal: Tong, styled Shulun, stood eight feet, with a towering look, skilled in dealing with the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, styled Shulun, stood eight feet tall, imposing, and skilled in affairs.

sentences.zh: 太和中，起家北海王詳國常侍。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he began as regular attendant in Prince of Beihai Xiang's state.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he began as regular attendant to Prince of Beihai Xiang.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiping he rose in succession to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiping he rose to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史奚康生征百姓歲調，皆長七八十尺，以邀憂公之譽，部內患之。

translations.literal: At the time Xiangzhou inspector Xi Kangsheng levied the annual tax in lengths of seventy or eighty feet to win a reputation for caring for the public; the commandery suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xi Kangsheng levied annual dues in seventy- or eighty-foot lengths to seem public-spirited; the region groaned.

sentences.zh: 同於歲祿，官給長絹。

translations.literal: Tong, from the year's salary, had the office supply long silk.
translations.idiomatic: Tong used his salary to have the office supply long silk.

sentences.zh: 同乃舉案康生度外徵調。

translations.literal: Tong then impeached Kangsheng for levies beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Tong impeached Kangsheng for excess levies.

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔科康生罪，兼褒同在公之績。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached court, an edict punished Kangsheng and also praised Tong's public merit.
translations.idiomatic: The throne punished Kangsheng and praised Tong's public service.

sentences.zh: 明帝世，朝政稍稀，人多竊冒軍功。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time court discipline grew slack and many stole military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming discipline slackened and many falsified military merit.

sentences.zh: 同閱吏部勳書，因加檢核，得竊階者三百餘人。

translations.literal: Tong reviewed the Ministry of Personnel merit rolls and on inspection found more than three hundred who had stolen ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Tong checked Personnel merit rolls and found over three hundred false claimants.

sentences.zh: 乃表言：

translations.literal: He then memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 竊見吏部勳簿，多皆改換，乃校中兵秦案，並復乖舛。

translations.literal: I observe that Ministry of Personnel merit registers are largely altered, and when checked against the Central Army Qin records they still disagree.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel merit registers are widely altered and still disagree with Central Army Qin records.

sentences.zh: 愚謂罪雖恩免，猶須刊定。

translations.literal: I hold that though crimes were pardoned by grace, they still must be corrected in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Though crimes were pardoned, the registers still need correction.

sentences.zh: 請遣一都令史，與令僕省事各一人，總集吏部、中兵二局勳簿，對句奏案。

translations.literal: Please send one chief clerk and one secretariat aide each from the Left and Right Vice Directors to gather Personnel and Central Army merit registers and check them line by line against memorial cases.
translations.idiomatic: Send one chief clerk and one aide from each Vice Director to collate Personnel and Central Army rolls against memorial cases.

sentences.zh: 若名級相應者，即于黃素楷書大字，具件階級數，令本曹尚書以硃印印之。

translations.literal: Where name and rank match, at once write the rank count in large characters on yellow plain silk and have the bureau director stamp it in vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: Where name and rank match, write ranks in large script on yellow silk and have the bureau director vermilion-stamp it.

sentences.zh: 明造兩通，一關吏部，一留兵局，與奏案對掌。

translations.literal: Clearly make two copies—one to Personnel, one kept at the Army bureau—to be held against the memorial case.
translations.idiomatic: Make two clear copies—one for Personnel, one for the Army bureau—to match the memorial case.

sentences.zh: 進則防揩洗之偽，退則無改易之理。

translations.literal: Going forward blocks erasure fraud; going back leaves no ground to alter.
translations.idiomatic: Going forward blocks erasures; going back blocks alterations.

sentences.zh: 從前以來，勳書上省，唯列姓名，不載本屬。

translations.literal: From old times merit books sent up listed only names, not original commands.
translations.idiomatic: Merit books sent up listed only names, not original commands.

sentences.zh: 致令竊濫之徒，輕為苟且。

translations.literal: Hence thieves of merit treated the matter lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Hence merit thieves grew bold.

sentences.zh: 今請征職白身，具列本州郡縣三長之所；

translations.literal: Now I ask that commoners in service list their native province, commandery, county, and ward head;
translations.idiomatic: Now ask commoners in service to list province, commandery, county, and ward;

sentences.zh: 其實官正職者，亦列官名曹別錄曆。

translations.literal: those with real official posts should also list office, bureau, and service record.
translations.idiomatic: real officials should list office, bureau, and service record.

sentences.zh: 皆仰本軍印記其上，然後印縫，各上所司。

translations.literal: All should bear the native army's seal above, then seal the seam and send each to its superior.
translations.idiomatic: All should bear the native army seal, then seam-seal and send up.

sentences.zh: 統將、都督，並皆印記，然後列上行台。

translations.literal: Commanding generals and area commanders should all seal, then list up to the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders and area commanders should seal, then send to the Mobile Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行台關太尉。

translations.literal: The Mobile Secretariat passes it to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The Mobile Secretariat forwards to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 太尉檢練精實，乃始關刺。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant examines for truth, and only then passes it to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant verifies truth, then passes to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 省重究括，然後奏申。

translations.literal: The Secretariat weighs it closely, then memorializes.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reviews closely, then memorializes.

sentences.zh: 奏出之日，黃素硃印，關付吏部。

translations.literal: On the day the memorial issues, yellow silk with vermilion seal is sent to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial issues, stamped yellow silk goes to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 頃來，非但偷階冒名，改換勳簿而已，或一階再取，或易名受級，凡如此者，其人不少。

translations.literal: Recently it has not been only stealing ranks and false names or altering merit registers—some take one rank twice, or change names to receive grades; such men are not few.
translations.idiomatic: Lately men steal ranks, swap names, or take one grade twice—not a few.

sentences.zh: 良由吏部無法，防塞失方。

translations.literal: Truly because Personnel lacks law and the barriers fail.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel lacks law and the barriers fail.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 吏部加階之後，簿不注記，緣此之故，易生僥倖。

translations.literal: After Personnel adds a rank the register is not annotated; for this reason opportunism is easy.
translations.idiomatic: After ranks are added the register is not noted, so fraud is easy.

sentences.zh: 自今敘階之後，名簿具注，加補日月，尚書印記，然後付曹，郎中別作抄目，遷代相付。

translations.literal: From now on, after ranks are granted the name register should fully note them, add the date, have the director stamp, then hand to the bureau; the bureau director should make a separate copy handed on at each transfer.
translations.idiomatic: After each grant, note name, date, and director stamp, then hand to the bureau with a copied roster at each transfer.

sentences.zh: 此制一行，差止奸罔。

translations.literal: Once this rule operates, fraud will largely cease.
translations.idiomatic: This rule would largely stop fraud.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted.

sentences.zh: 同又奏曰：

translations.literal: Tong again memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Tong memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 臣伏思黃素勳簿，政可粗止奸偽，然在軍虛詐，猶未可盡。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that yellow-silk merit registers can only roughly stop fraud in the registers; fraud in the army is not yet ended.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-silk registers only roughly stop register fraud; army fraud remains.

sentences.zh: 請自今在軍閱簿之日，行台、軍司、監軍、都督各明立文案，處處記之。

translations.literal: From now on, on the day army registers are reviewed, Mobile Secretariat, army secretariat, supervising army, and area commander should each keep clear documents and record everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: On review day, Mobile Secretariat, army secretariat, supervisor, and commander should each keep records.

sentences.zh: 斬首成一階以上，即令給券。

translations.literal: For one rank from beheaded heads or more, issue a warrant at once.
translations.idiomatic: One rank from heads or more gets a warrant at once.

sentences.zh: 其券，一紙之上，當中大書，起行台、統軍位號，勳人甲乙。

translations.literal: The warrant, on one sheet, should have in large characters at the center the Mobile Secretariat and commanding general's titles and the merit-holder's name.
translations.idiomatic: The warrant should center the Mobile Secretariat and commander titles and the merit-holder's name in large script.

sentences.zh: 斬三賊及被傷成階以上，亦具書於券，各盡一行，當行豎裂。

translations.literal: For three slain rebels or wounds earning a rank or more, also write it on the warrant, each on one line, with a vertical tear down the center.
translations.idiomatic: Three rebels slain or wounds earning rank should each get a line on the warrant, torn vertically down the center.

sentences.zh: 其券，前後皆起年號日月，破某處陣，某官某勳，印記為驗。

translations.literal: The warrant should front and back bear reign era, month, day, the battle broken, the officer and merit, and seals as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Front and back should bear era, date, battle, officer, merit, and seals.

sentences.zh: 一支付勳人，一支付行台。

translations.literal: One copy to the merit-holder, one to the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: One copy to the holder, one to the Mobile Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 記至京，即送門下，別丞守錄。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital it goes to the Gate Department for separate keeping.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital it goes to the Gate Department for filing.

sentences.zh: 又自遷都以來，戎車屢捷，所以征勳轉多，敘不可盡者，良由歲久生奸，積年長偽，巧吏階緣，偷增遂甚。

translations.literal: Since the move of the capital, campaigns have often won; merit grants multiplied and could not all be entered—long years bred fraud, piled years bred falsehood, clever clerks climbed by links, and theft grew extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capital moved, victories multiplied merit grants beyond entry—years bred fraud and clever clerks stole ranks.

sentences.zh: 請自今為始，諸有勳簿已經奏賞者，即廣下遠近，雲某處勳判，咸令知聞。

translations.literal: From now, for all merit registers already memorialized and rewarded, broadly announce to far and near that such-and-such merit was judged, so all may know.
translations.idiomatic: Announce every judged merit register far and near so all may know.

sentences.zh: 立格酬敘，以三年為斷。

translations.literal: Set a standard for reward with a three-year limit.
translations.idiomatic: Set rewards on a three-year limit.

sentences.zh: 其職人及出身，限內悉令銓除；

translations.literal: Commoners in service and those entering office should all be ranked out within the limit;
translations.idiomatic: Commoners and entrants should be ranked out within the limit;

sentences.zh: 實官及外號，隋才加授。

translations.literal: real offices and external titles should be granted by talent.
translations.idiomatic: real offices and external titles by talent.

sentences.zh: 庶使酬勤速申，立效者勸，事不經久，僥倖易息。

translations.literal: Thus reward for toil would be quick, the effective encouraged, affairs not long delayed, and opportunism easy to end.
translations.idiomatic: Reward would be swift, workers encouraged, and opportunism curbed.

sentences.zh: 或遭窮難，州無中正者，不在此限。

translations.literal: Or if hardship leaves a province without a Rectifier, that is outside this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces without a Rectifier in hardship are excepted.

sentences.zh: 又勳簿之示，征還之日，即應申送。

translations.literal: Also, showing merit registers should happen on the day of return from campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Merit registers should be shown on return day.

sentences.zh: 然頃來，行台、督將至京始造，或一年二歲，方上勳書。

translations.literal: Yet recently Mobile Secretariat commanders and generals only draft them on reaching the capital, or after one or two years only then send merit books up.
translations.idiomatic: Lately commanders draft only at the capital, or send books up a year or two late.

sentences.zh: 奸偽之原，實自由此。

translations.literal: The root of fraud truly lies here.
translations.idiomatic: That is the root of fraud.

sentences.zh: 於今以後，軍還之日，便通勳簿，不聽隔月。

translations.literal: Henceforth, on the army's return day pass merit registers at once; no delay past a month.
translations.idiomatic: On return, pass registers at once—no delay past a month.

sentences.zh: 詔復依行。

translations.literal: An edict again followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted again.

sentences.zh: 元叉之廢靈太后也，相州刺史、中山王熙起兵於鄴。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Xiangzhou inspector Prince of Zhongshan Xi raised troops at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, Xiangzhou inspector, rose at Ye.

sentences.zh: 敗之。

translations.literal: He was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was defeated.

sentences.zh: 叉以同為持節兼黃門侍郎慰勞使，乃就州刑熙。

translations.literal: Cha made Tong concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant and consolation commissioner and had him execute Xi in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Cha sent Tong as Yellow Gate Attendant to console the province and execute Xi there.

sentences.zh: 還，授正黃門。

translations.literal: On return he was made regular Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and became regular Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 同善事在位，為叉所親。

translations.literal: Tong was skilled at serving those in power and was close to Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Tong served the powerful well and was Cha's favorite.

sentences.zh: 戮熙之日，深窮黨與，以希叉旨，論者非之。

translations.literal: On the day Xi was executed he pursued the clique deeply to please Cha; opinion condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was killed he hunted the clique to please Cha; opinion condemned him.

sentences.zh: 同兄琇，少多大言，常雲公侯可致。

translations.literal: Tong's elder brother Xiu from youth talked big and often said marquis and duke were within reach.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Xiu had long boasted that marquis and duke were within reach.

sentences.zh: 至此，始為都水使者。

translations.literal: Only now did he become Director of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Only now did he become Director of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 同啟求回身二階以加琇。

translations.literal: Tong memorialized asking to return two ranks from himself to add to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Tong asked to strip two ranks from himself for Xiu.

sentences.zh: 琇遂除安州刺史，論者稱之。

translations.literal: Xiu was then made Anzhou inspector; opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu became Anzhou inspector; opinion praised it.

sentences.zh: 營州城人就德興謀反，除同度支尚書，持節使營州慰勞，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou townsman Jiu Dexing plotted rebellion, Tong was made Minister of Revenue and commissioner with credentials to console Yingzhou, with expedient authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiu Dexing rebelled at Yingzhou, Tong became Minister of Revenue and commissioner to console Yingzhou with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 同乃遣賊家口三十人，並免家奴為良，齎書喻之。

translations.literal: Tong sent thirty dependents of rebel households and freed household slaves to commoner status, bearing letters to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent thirty rebel dependents, freed slaves to commoner status, and wrote instructing them.

sentences.zh: 德興乃降，安輯其人而還。

translations.literal: Dexing then surrendered; Tong settled the people and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Dexing surrendered; Tong pacified the region and returned.

sentences.zh: 德興復反，詔同為幽州刺史，兼尚書行台，慰勞之。

translations.literal: When Dexing rebelled again, an edict made Tong Youzhou inspector and concurrent Mobile Secretariat Director to console them.
translations.idiomatic: Dexing rebelled again; Tong was Youzhou inspector and Mobile Secretariat Director to console them.

sentences.zh: 同慮德興難信，勒眾而往，為德興所擊，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Tong feared Dexing could not be trusted, led troops thither, was struck by Dexing, and returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Dexing, he led troops out, was routed, and fled back.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以同叉黨，除名。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, as Cha's partisan Tong was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Ling regained power, Tong was removed as Cha's man.

sentences.zh: 莊帝踐祚，詔復本秩，除都官尚書，復兼七兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended, an edict restored his former rank; he was made Minister of Justice and again concurrent Director of the Seven Arms.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang restored his rank, made him Minister of Justice, and again Director of the Seven Arms.

sentences.zh: 以前慰勞德興功，封章武縣伯，正除七兵。

translations.literal: For earlier merit in consoling Dexing he was enfeoffed Baron of Zhangwu and made regular Director of the Seven Arms.
translations.idiomatic: For consoling Dexing he was Baron of Zhangwu and regular Director of the Seven Arms.

sentences.zh: 轉殿中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Director.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Director.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除侍中，進號驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the start of Putai he was made Palace Attendant, advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Putai made him Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 同時久病，牽強啟乞儀同。

translations.literal: Tong had long been ill; forcing himself he memorialized begging the Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Long ill, he forced himself to beg the Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 初同之為黃門也，與節閔帝俱在門下，同異其為人，素相款托。

translations.literal: When Tong had been Yellow Gate Attendant he and Emperor Jiemin were both at the Gate Department; Tong thought him unusual and they were close.
translations.idiomatic: As Yellow Gate Attendant he had known Jiemin at the Gate Department and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 帝以恩舊，許之，除儀同三司。

translations.literal: The emperor, for old kindness, granted it and made him Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: For old ties the emperor granted Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，薨，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongxi he died; posthumously Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi he died; posthumously Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 四子，長子斐嗣。

translations.literal: Four sons; the eldest Fei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons; eldest Fei inherited.

sentences.zh: 斐字子章，性殘忍，以強斷知名。

translations.literal: Fei, styled Zizhang, was cruel and famed for harsh judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Fei, styled Zizhang, was cruel and known for harsh judgment.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄引為大將軍府刑獄參軍，謂云：「狂簡，斐然成章，非嘉名字也。

translations.literal: Qi Wenxiang made him penal commissioner in the Grand General's office and said: "Reckless and terse, yet your name means 'patterned'—not a name to praise."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang made him penal commissioner and said, "Reckless and terse, yet your name means patterned—not praiseworthy."

sentences.zh: 」天保中，稍遷尚書左丞，別典京畿詔獄。

translations.literal: In Tianbao he rose gradually to Left Vice Director and separately handled capital-region imperial cases.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao he rose to Left Vice Director and handled capital-region cases.

sentences.zh: 酷濫非人情所為，無問事之大小，拷掠過度，于大棒車輻下死者非一。

translations.literal: His cruelty exceeded what human feeling allows; regardless of the case's size he tortured beyond measure, and under the great club at the cart wheel more than one died.
translations.idiomatic: His cruelty exceeded humanity; he tortured every case beyond measure, and many died under the great club at the cart wheel.

sentences.zh: 或嚴冬至寒，置囚於冰雪之上；

translations.literal: Sometimes in deep winter cold he set prisoners on ice and snow;
translations.idiomatic: In deep winter he set prisoners on ice;

sentences.zh: 或盛夏酷熱，暴之日下，枉陷人致死者，前後百數人。

translations.literal: sometimes in midsummer heat he exposed them under the sun—those wrongly killed numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: in midsummer he exposed them in the sun—hundreds died wrongfully.

sentences.zh: 伺察官人罪失，動即奏聞。

translations.literal: He watched officials' faults and at once memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: He spied on officials and memorialized at once.

sentences.zh: 朝士見之，莫不重跡屏氣，皆目之為校事。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen who saw him all walked softly and held their breath, all calling him a secret investigator.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen walked softly and called him a secret investigator.

sentences.zh: 斐揚揚得志，言必自矜。

translations.literal: Fei swaggered in triumph and always spoke with pride.
translations.idiomatic: Fei swaggered and always spoke with pride.

sentences.zh: 後以謗史事，與李庶俱病鞭杖，死獄中。

translations.literal: Later for slandering the histories he and Li Shu were both flogged and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later for slandering the histories he and Li Shu were flogged to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 斐弟筠，青州中從事。

translations.literal: Fei's younger brother Jun was Qingzhou vice-inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Jun was Qingzhou vice-inspector.

sentences.zh: 同兄靜，好學有風度，飲酒至數斗不亂。

translations.literal: Tong's elder brother Jing loved learning and had bearing; he could drink several dou without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Jing loved learning, had bearing, and could drink several dou without disorder.

sentences.zh: 終於太常丞。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Director of the Ancestral Temples.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as temple vice director.

sentences.zh: 大統初，贈太僕卿、平州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong he was posthumously Grand Master of the Stud and Pingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Datong posthumously made him Grand Master of the Stud and Pingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 靜子景裕。

translations.literal: Jing's son Jingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Son Jingyu.

sentences.zh: 景裕字仲孺，小字白頭。

translations.literal: Jingyu, styled Zhongru, childhood name Whitehead.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu, styled Zhongru, nicknamed Whitehead.

sentences.zh: 少敏，專經為學。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick and devoted himself to classical study.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick and studied the classics.

sentences.zh: 居拒馬河，將一老婢作食，妻子不自隨從。

translations.literal: He lived on the Juma River, had one old maid cook, and his wife and children did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: On the Juma River he kept one old maid to cook; wife and children did not follow.

sentences.zh: 又避地大寧山，不營世事。

translations.literal: He also withdrew to Great Peace Mountain and did not pursue worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Great Peace Mountain and ignored worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 居無二業，唯在注解。

translations.literal: He had no second trade; only commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He had no second trade—only commentary.

sentences.zh: 其叔父同職居顯要，而景裕止於園舍，情均郊野。

translations.literal: His uncle Tong held a lofty post, yet Jingyu stayed in his garden lodge, his heart like the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Tong was powerful, yet Jingyu stayed in his garden, heart in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 謙恭守道，貞素自得，由是世號居士。

translations.literal: Humble, guarding the Way, chaste and self-content—hence the world called him Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and chaste, he was called Recluse by the world.

sentences.zh: 節閔初，除國子博士，參議正聲，其見親遇，待以不臣之禮。

translations.literal: At Jiemin's start he was made Doctor of the National University and discussed correct pitch; he was favored and treated with the courtesy due a non-subject.
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin made him National University doctor to discuss pitch; he was favored beyond subject courtesy.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，以例解。

translations.literal: At Yongxi's start he was dismissed by rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi he was dismissed by rule.

sentences.zh: 天平中，還鄉里。

translations.literal: In Tianping he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping he went home.

sentences.zh: 與邢子才、魏季景、魏收、邢昕等同征赴鄴，景裕寓托僧寺，講聽不已。

translations.literal: With Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin he went on summons to Ye; Jingyu lodged in a monastery and lectured without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to Ye with Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin, he lodged in a monastery and lectured on.

sentences.zh: 未幾，歸本郡。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned home.

sentences.zh: 河間邢摩納與景裕從兄仲禮據鄉作逆，逼其同反，以應西魏。

translations.literal: Hejian's Xing Monuo and Jingyu's cousin Zhongli held the township in rebellion and forced him to join, responding to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Monuo and cousin Zhongli rebelled in the township and forced him to join Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 齊神武命都督賀拔仁討平之。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu ordered Area Commander Helu Ren to crush them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent Helu Ren to crush them.

sentences.zh: 聞景裕經明行著，驛馬特徵。

translations.literal: Hearing Jingyu's classics were clear and his conduct manifest, he was specially summoned by post horse.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his learning and conduct, the court summoned him by post horse.

sentences.zh: 既而舍之，使教諸子，在館十日一歸家，隨以鼎食。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and made to teach the sons; in the lodge he went home every ten days and was given full meals.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he taught the sons, went home every ten days from the lodge, and was fed like a noble.

sentences.zh: 景裕風儀言行，雅見嗟賞。

translations.literal: Jingyu's bearing and conduct won warm praise.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing won warm praise.

sentences.zh: 先是，景裕注《周易》、《尚書》、《孝經》、《論語》、《禮記》、《老子》，其《毛詩》、《春秋左氏》未訖。

translations.literal: Earlier Jingyu had commented on the "Changes," "Documents," "Classic of Filial Piety," "Analects," "Record of Rites," and "Laozi"; the "Odes" and "Zuo Commentary" were unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: He had commented on the Changes, Documents, Filial Piety, Analects, Rites, and Laozi; Odes and Zuo were unfinished.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄入相，於第開講；

translations.literal: When Qi Wenxiang entered the chancellorship he opened lectures at his residence;
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang became chancellor he lectured at his residence;

sentences.zh: 招延時俊，令景裕解所注《易》。

translations.literal: he gathered the day's talents and had Jingyu expound his "Changes" commentary.
translations.idiomatic: he gathered scholars and had Jingyu expound his Changes.

sentences.zh: 景裕理義精微，吐發閒雅。

translations.literal: Jingyu's reasoning was subtle and his delivery refined.
translations.idiomatic: His reasoning was subtle and delivery refined.

sentences.zh: 時有問難，或相詆訶，大聲厲色，言至不遜。

translations.literal: When there were challenges some abused him, shouting loudly with harsh color and speech beyond courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Some challengers abused him with loud, harsh speech beyond courtesy.

sentences.zh: 而景裕神彩儼然，風誦如一，從容往復，無際可尋，由是士君子嗟美之。

translations.literal: Yet Jingyu's spirit remained grave, his recitation even, his replies easy and without gap to seize—hence gentlemen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remained grave, recited evenly, and replied without gap—gentlemen praised him.

sentences.zh: 初，元顥入洛，以為中書郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he was made Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang he was Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，復除國子博士。

translations.literal: In Putai he was again made National University doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Putai he was again National University doctor.

sentences.zh: 進退其間，未曾有得失之色。

translations.literal: Through advance and retreat he never showed gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: Through rise and fall he never showed gain or loss.

sentences.zh: 性清靜，淡于榮利，弊衣粗食，恬然自安，終日端嚴，如對賓客。

translations.literal: By nature quiet, indifferent to glory and profit, in worn clothes and coarse food he was content, all day grave as facing guests.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet, indifferent to profit, in worn clothes and coarse food he stayed grave as before guests all day.

sentences.zh: 興和中，補齊王開府屬，卒于晉陽。

translations.literal: In Xinghe he was made staff officer to Prince of Qi's establishment and died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghe he was staff to Prince of Qi and died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 神武悼惜之。

translations.literal: Shenwu mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu mourned him.

sentences.zh: 景裕雖不聚徒教授，所注《易》大行於世。

translations.literal: Though Jingyu did not gather disciples, his "Changes" commentary spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: Though he taught no disciples, his Changes spread widely.

sentences.zh: 又好釋氏，通其大義。

translations.literal: He also loved Buddhism and grasped its great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved Buddhism and grasped its meaning.

sentences.zh: 天竺胡沙門道悕，每譯諸經論，輒托景裕為之序。

translations.literal: The Indian monk Daoxi, whenever he translated sutras and treatises, always asked Jingyu to write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Monk Daoxi always asked him to preface his translations.

sentences.zh: 景裕之敗也，系晉陽獄，至心誦經，枷鎖自脫。

translations.literal: When Jingyu was defeated he was bound in Jinyang prison; chanting sutras with full heart, stocks and shackles fell away.
translations.idiomatic: When defeated he was jailed at Jinyang; chanting sutras, his shackles fell away.

sentences.zh: 是時，又有人負罪當死，夢沙門教講經，覺時如所夢，謂誦千遍，臨刑刀折。

translations.literal: At the time another man guilty of death dreamed a monk taught him to recite a sutra; waking as in the dream, he said a thousand recitations made the execution blade break.
translations.idiomatic: Another condemned man dreamed a monk taught a sutra; awake, a thousand recitations broke the blade.

sentences.zh: 主者以聞，赦之。

translations.literal: The officer reported it and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The officer reported it and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 此經遂行，號曰《高王觀世音》。

translations.literal: That sutra then spread, called "High King Avalokitesvara."
translations.idiomatic: The sutra spread as "High King Avalokitesvara."

sentences.zh: 景裕弟辯。

translations.literal: Jingyu's younger brother Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Bian.

sentences.zh: 辯字景宣，少好學，博通經籍。

translations.literal: Bian, styled Jingxuan, from youth loved learning and mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Bian, styled Jingxuan, from youth mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 正光初，舉秀才，為太學博士。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengguang he was presented as Presented Scholar and made Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengguang he was Presented Scholar and Academy erudite.

sentences.zh: 以《大戴禮》未有解詁，辯乃注之。

translations.literal: Because the "Greater Dai Rites" lacked commentary, Bian commented it.
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Dai Rites lacked commentary; Bian supplied it.

sentences.zh: 其兄景裕為當時碩儒，謂辯曰：「昔侍中注《小戴》，今汝注《大戴》，庶纂前修矣。

translations.literal: His elder brother Jingyu was the age's great scholar and told Bian: "Once the Attendant commented the Lesser Dai; now you comment the Greater Dai—you may follow the forebears."
translations.idiomatic: Elder Jingyu, the age's great scholar, said, "Once the Attendant commented Lesser Dai; now you comment Greater Dai—you follow the forebears."

sentences.zh: 」節閔帝立，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin was enthroned, Bian was made Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin made him Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 屬齊神武起兵信都，既破爾硃氏，遂鼓行指洛。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu raised troops at Xindu, after breaking the Erzhu clan he marched on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu raised troops at Xindu, broke the Erzhu, and marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 節閔遣辯持節勞之於鄴。

translations.literal: Jiemin sent Bian with credentials to console him at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin sent Bian with credentials to console Shenwu at Ye.

sentences.zh: 神武令辯見其所奉中興主，辯抗節不從。

translations.literal: Shenwu had Bian see the Restoration Sovereign he supported; Bian held his staff and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu made him see the Restoration Sovereign; Bian refused.

sentences.zh: 神武怒曰：「我舉大義，誅群醜，車駕在此，誰遣爾來？

translations.literal: Shenwu angrily said: "I raised great righteousness and executed the foul; the imperial carriage is here—who sent you?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu raged: "I raised righteousness and killed the foul; the emperor is here—who sent you?"

sentences.zh: 」辯抗言酬答，守節不撓。

translations.literal: Bian answered sharply and held his integrity without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Bian answered sharply and did not yield.

sentences.zh: 神武異之，舍而不逼。

translations.literal: Shenwu marveled and let him go without pressing.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu marveled and let him go.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，以辯為廣平王贊師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended, Bian was made tutor to Prince of Guangping Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu made him tutor to Prince of Guangping Zan.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，平等浮屠成，孝武會萬僧於寺。

translations.literal: In Yongxi year two the Equal-Height Buddha was completed; Xiaowu gathered ten thousand monks at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi 2 the Equal-Height Buddha was done; Xiaowu gathered ten thousand monks.

sentences.zh: 石佛低舉其頭，終日乃止。

translations.literal: The stone Buddha slowly raised its head and only at day's end stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The stone Buddha slowly raised its head and stopped at day's end.

sentences.zh: 帝禮拜之。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed to it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed.

sentences.zh: 辯曰：「石立社移，自古有此，陛下何怪。

translations.literal: Bian said: "When a stone statue moves, it has happened since antiquity—why should Your Majesty wonder?"
translations.idiomatic: Bian said, "Stone statues move in every age—why wonder?"

sentences.zh: 」及帝入關，事起倉卒，辯不及至家，單馬而從。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the passes affairs were sudden; Bian had no time to reach home and followed on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the passes Bian had no time for home and followed alone.

sentences.zh: 或問辯曰：「得辭家不？

translations.literal: Someone asked Bian: "Did you take leave of home?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked if he had bid his household farewell.

sentences.zh: 」辯曰：「門外之道，以義斷恩，復何辭也。」

translations.literal: Bian said: "The way outside the gate breaks kinship by righteousness—what farewell is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Bian said, "Outside the gate the Way breaks kinship by righteousness—what farewell?"

sentences.zh: 孝武至長安，封范陽縣公。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu reached Chang'an he was enfeoffed Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an Xiaowu enfeoffed him Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 歷位給事黃門侍郎，領著作，加本州大中正。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Supervising Secretariat Gentleman, headed the History Office, and was made native-prefecture Grand Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Supervising Secretariat Gentleman, headed the History Office, and was native Grand Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 周文帝以辯有儒術，甚禮之，朝廷大議，常召顧問。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Wendi, because Bian had Confucian learning, greatly honored him; on great court debates he was often summoned for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi honored his learning and often summoned him for great debates.

sentences.zh: 遷太子少保，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and National University Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was Junior Tutor and National University Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 趙青雀之亂，魏太子出居渭北，辯時隨從，亦不告家人。

translations.literal: During Zhao Qingque's rebellion the Wei crown prince went to live north of the Wei River; Bian followed without telling his household.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhao Qingque's revolt the crown prince moved north of the Wei; Bian followed without telling home.

sentences.zh: 其執志敢決，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His firm resolve was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His firm resolve was always thus.

sentences.zh: 尋除太常卿、太子少傅，轉少師，魏太子及諸王等皆行束脩之禮，受業於辯，進爵范陽郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Director of the Ancestral Temples and Junior Tutor, then Junior Preceptor; the Wei crown prince and princes all performed the pupil ceremony and studied under Bian, and he was advanced to Duke of Fanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was temple director, junior tutor, then preceptor; princes studied under him and he became Duke of Fanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 自孝武西遷，朝儀湮墜，于時朝廷憲章、乘輿法服、金石律呂、晷刻渾儀，皆令辯因時制宜。

translations.literal: After Xiaowu moved west court ritual was lost; then court statutes, imperial regalia, metal and stone pitch, clepsydra and armillary sphere—all were ordered adapted to the times by Bian.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu moved west ritual collapsed; court law, regalia, pitch pipes, clepsydra, and armillary sphere were all adapted by Bian.

sentences.zh: 皆合軌度，多依古禮。

translations.literal: All matched the standards and largely followed ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: All matched standards and largely followed ancient rites.

sentences.zh: 性強記默識，能斷大事，凡所創制，處之不疑。

translations.literal: He had strong memory and silent retention, could decide great affairs, and whatever he created he handled without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He remembered silently, decided great affairs, and handled his creations without doubt.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，累遷尚書令。

translations.literal: He was made General of Agile Cavalry and Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies, and rose in succession to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He became General of Agile Cavalry, Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及建門官，為師氏中大夫。

translations.literal: When gate officials were established he was Master of the Guard, middle grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When gate offices were set he was Master of the Guard, middle grandee.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，遷小宗伯，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended he was made Junior Director of the Ancestral Temples and advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Ming made him Junior Temple Director and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與諸公幸其第，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited his residence with the nobles—a scholar's glory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once visited his house with nobles—scholarly glory.

sentences.zh: 出為宜州刺史，以患不之部。

translations.literal: He went out as Yizhou inspector but, ill, did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Made Yizhou inspector, he did not take office for illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰獻，配食文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Xian, with sacrifice in Wendi's temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died, posthumous name Xian, with sacrifice in Wendi's temple.

sentences.zh: 子慎嗣。

translations.literal: Son Shen inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shen inherited.

sentences.zh: 位復州刺史。

translations.literal: Held the post of Fuzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was Fuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 慎弟詮，性趫捷，善騎射，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: Shen's younger brother Quan was quick and skilled at riding and archery, and held Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Quan was quick, skilled at archery, and held Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，以辯前代名德，追封沈國公。

translations.literal: At the start of Sui Kaihuang, for Bian's fame in earlier ages he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang posthumously enfeoffed him Duke of Shen for earlier fame.

sentences.zh: 初，周文欲行《周官》，命蘇綽專掌其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Wendi wished to implement the "Offices of Zhou" and ordered Su Chuo to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi wished to implement the Offices of Zhou and ordered Su Chuo to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 未幾而綽卒，乃令辯成之。

translations.literal: Before long Chuo died and Bian was ordered to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo soon died and Bian was ordered to finish.

sentences.zh: 於是依《周禮》建六官，革漢、魏之法。

translations.literal: Thereupon by the "Rites of Zhou" six ministries were built, reforming Han and Wei law.
translations.idiomatic: By the Rites of Zhou six ministries were built, reforming Han and Wei law.

sentences.zh: 以魏恭帝三年，始命行之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wei Gongdi it was first ordered implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gongdi year three it was first implemented.

sentences.zh: 六卿之外，置太師、太傅、太保各一人，是曰三孤。
