sentences.zh: 四征中鎮撫將軍府、正七命州列曹參軍；

translations.literal: Four Campaigns, Center, Pacification, and Suppression general's offices, orthodox seventh-rank provincial department staff officer;
translations.idiomatic: four-campaigns and pacification offices: orthodox seventh-rank department staff;

sentences.zh: 正五命郡丞。

translations.literal: Orthodox fifth-rank commandery aide.
translations.idiomatic: orthodox fifth-rank commandery aide.

sentences.zh: 正二命。

translations.literal: Orthodox second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Second orthodox rank.

sentences.zh: 掃寇將軍、武騎司馬；

translations.literal: General Who Sweeps the Wilderness of Bandits, Palace Crossbow Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Sweeping Wilderness general, palace crossbow marshal;

sentences.zh: 掃難將軍、武威司馬；

translations.literal: General Who Sweeps the Wilderness of Difficulty, Martial Prestige Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Sweeping Wilderness of Difficulty general, martial prestige marshal;

sentences.zh: 四平前右左後將軍府、七命州列曹參軍；

translations.literal: Four Pacifications, Front, Right, Left, and Rear general's offices, seventh-rank provincial department staff officer;
translations.idiomatic: four pacifications offices: seventh-rank department staff;

sentences.zh: 五命郡丞；

translations.literal: Fifth-rank commandery aide;
translations.idiomatic: fifth-rank commandery aide;

sentences.zh: 戍副。

translations.literal: Deputy Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: deputy garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 二命。

translations.literal: Second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank.

sentences.zh: 曠野將軍、殿中司馬；

translations.literal: General of the Open Wilderness, Palace Attendant Crossbow Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Open Wilderness general, palace attendant crossbow marshal;

sentences.zh: 橫野將軍、員外司馬；

translations.literal: General of the Broad Wilderness, Extra Master of Writing Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Broad Wilderness general, extra master-of-writing marshal;

sentences.zh: 冠軍輔國將軍府、正六命州列曹參軍。

translations.literal: Champion and Assistant-to-the-State general's offices, orthodox sixth-rank provincial department staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: champion and assistant-state offices: orthodox sixth-rank department staff.

sentences.zh: 正一命。

translations.literal: Orthodox first rank.
translations.idiomatic: First orthodox rank.

sentences.zh: 武威將軍、淮海都尉；

translations.literal: Martial Prestige General, Huaihai Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: Martial Prestige general, Huaihai commandant;

sentences.zh: 武邪將軍、山林都尉；

translations.literal: Martial Subdual General, Mountain-Forest Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: Martial Subdual general, mountain-forest commandant;

sentences.zh: 鎮遠建忠中堅甯朔寧遠揚烈伏波輕車將軍府列曹參軍。

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-Distant, Establishing-the-Loyal, Center Corps, Pacifying-the-North, Pacifying-the-Distant, Displaying-the-Fierce, Subduing-the-Waves, and Light-Chariot general's offices—department staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: those general's offices: department staff officers.

sentences.zh: 一命。

translations.literal: First rank.
translations.idiomatic: First rank.

sentences.zh: 周制：封郡縣五等爵者，皆加開國；

translations.literal: Under the Zhou system, those enfeoffed with five grades of commandery and county nobility all added "Founder of the State";
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou, five-grade commandery and county enfeoffments all added Founder of the State;

sentences.zh: 授柱國大將軍、開府、儀同者，並加使持節、大都督；

translations.literal: those granted Pillar of State, Opening Office, or Equal in Honor all also added "Commissioned with Staff" and "Great Commander";
translations.idiomatic: pillar-of-state, opening-office, or equal-in-honor grants also added Commissioned with Staff and Great Commander;

sentences.zh: 其開府又加驃騎大將軍、侍中；

translations.literal: the Opening Office further added Rapid-Cavalry Grand General and Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: opening office further added rapid-cavalry grand general and palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 其儀同又加車騎大將軍、散騎常侍；

translations.literal: the Equal in Honor further added Chariot-and-Horse Grand General and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary;
translations.idiomatic: equal in honor further added chariot-and-horse grand general and regular attendant;

sentences.zh: 其授總管、刺史，則加使持節、諸軍事。

translations.literal: those appointed Commander-in-Chief or Inspector added "Commissioned with Staff" and "Commander of All Military Affairs."
translations.idiomatic: commanders-in-chief and inspectors added Commissioned with Staff and Commander of All Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以此為常。

translations.literal: This was the constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: That was the constant rule.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，詔總管、刺史及行兵者，加持節，餘悉罷之。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Daxiang era, an edict ordered commanders-in-chief, inspectors, and those on campaign to hold staffs of authority; all others were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Daxiang year 1: commanders, inspectors, and field armies kept staffs; all others lost them.

sentences.zh: 辯所制定之後，又有改革。

translations.literal: After what Bian had fixed, there were further reforms.
translations.idiomatic: After Bian's codification there were further reforms.

sentences.zh: 今粗附之云。

translations.literal: Here they are roughly appended.
translations.idiomatic: They are roughly appended below.

sentences.zh: 辯弟光。

translations.literal: Bian's younger brother Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's younger brother was Guang.

sentences.zh: 光子景仁。

translations.literal: Guang's son Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's son was Jingren.

sentences.zh: 性溫謹，博覽群書，精於《三禮》，善陰陽，解鐘律，又好玄言。

translations.literal: Gentle and careful in nature, he read widely, was expert in the Three Rites, skilled in yin-yang lore, understood pitch-pipes and musical scales, and also loved Dark Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and careful, widely read, expert in the Three Rites, yin-yang, pitch-pipes, and Dark Learning.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，釋褐司空府參軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era he left the purple and was made a staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang's opening years he entered service as a Ministry of Works staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，光于山東立義，遙授晉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Guang raised righteous forces in Shandong and was appointed Inspector of Jin from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu moved west, Guang raised forces in Shandong and was remotely made Jin inspector.

sentences.zh: 大統六年，攜家西入，除丞相府記室參軍，賜爵范陽縣伯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Datong he brought his family west, was made Recorder in the Chancellor's Office, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 6 he went west with his family, became the chancellor's recorder, and was made Marquis of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 俄拜行台郎中，專掌書記，改封安息縣伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Mobile Secretariat Gentleman in charge of records and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was mobile secretariat gentleman in charge of records, enfeoffed Marquis of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 歷位京兆郡守、侍中、開府儀同三司、匠師中大夫，進爵燕郡公、虞州刺史，行陝州總管府長史，卒官。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Jingzhao, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Equal in Honor with the Three Dukes, Master of Craftsmen in the Inner Court, was advanced to Duke of Yancheng and Inspector of Yu, and was Acting Chief Clerk of the Shaanzhou Commander's Office; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was Jingzhao administrator, attendant, equal in honor, master of craftsmen, advanced to Duke of Yancheng and Yu inspector, acting chief clerk at Shaanzhou headquarters, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 周武帝少嘗受業於光，故贈賻有加恆典，贈少傅，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou had once studied under Guang as a youth, so funeral gifts exceeded the usual rule; he was posthumously made Junior Tutor with posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Emperor Wu had studied under him, so gifts exceeded custom; he was posthumously junior tutor, posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 光性崇佛道，至誠信敬。

translations.literal: Guang revered Buddhism and was utterly sincere in faith.
translations.idiomatic: Guang revered Buddhism with utter sincerity.

sentences.zh: 常從周文狩于檀臺山，時獵圍既合，帝遙指山上謂群公曰：「公等有所見不？

translations.literal: He once followed Zhou Emperor Wen on a hunt at Tanshan; when the beaters had closed the ring, the Emperor pointed to the mountain and asked the lords, "Do you gentlemen see anything?"
translations.idiomatic: Once on a hunt at Tanshan with Emperor Wen, when the ring closed the emperor pointed uphill and asked, "Do you see anything?"

sentences.zh: 」咸曰：無所見。

translations.literal: " All said they saw nothing.
translations.idiomatic: All said they saw nothing.

sentences.zh: 」光獨曰：「見一桑門。

translations.literal: " Guang alone said, "I see a monk."
translations.idiomatic: Guang alone said, "I see a monk."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「是也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "That is so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is."

sentences.zh: 」即解圍而還。

translations.literal: " He at once lifted the encirclement and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the encirclement and returned.

sentences.zh: 令光于桑門立處造浮圖。

translations.literal: He had Guang build a pagoda where the monk had stood.
translations.idiomatic: He had Guang build a pagoda where the monk stood.

sentences.zh: 掘基一丈，得瓦缽錫杖各一，帝稱歎，因立寺焉。

translations.literal: When they dug the foundation one zhang down, they found a pottery bowl and an iron staff; the Emperor marveled and thereupon founded a monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Digging one zhang down they found a bowl and iron staff; the emperor marveled and founded a monastery.

sentences.zh: 及為京兆，而郡舍先是數有妖怪，前後郡將，無敢居者。

translations.literal: When he became Administrator of Jingzhao, the prefectural residence had long had uncanny occurrences, and successive prefects dared not live there.
translations.idiomatic: As Jingzhao administrator the yamen had long been haunted and no prefect dared live there.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「吉凶由人，妖不妄作。

translations.literal: Guang said, "Fortune and misfortune depend on men; demons do not act without cause."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Fortune depends on men; demons do not act without cause."

sentences.zh: 」遂人居之。

translations.literal: " He then moved in.
translations.idiomatic: He moved in.

sentences.zh: 未幾，光所乘馬忽升査事，登床，南首而立。

translations.literal: Before long the horse Guang rode suddenly climbed the desk platform, mounted the bed, and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his horse climbed the desk platform, mounted the bed, and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 食器無故自破。

translations.literal: Food vessels broke for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: Food vessels broke without cause.

sentences.zh: 光並不以介懷，其精誠守正如此。

translations.literal: Guang took none of it to heart—such was his sincere uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Guang took none of it to heart—such was his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 注《道德經章句》行於世。

translations.literal: His Expository Chapters on the Dao De Jing circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Expository Chapters on the Dao De Jing circulated.

sentences.zh: 子賁。

translations.literal: Son Ben.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ben.

sentences.zh: 賁字子征。

translations.literal: Ben, styled Zizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ben, styled Zizheng.

sentences.zh: 略涉書記，頗解鐘律。

translations.literal: He had some acquaintance with writing and was fairly skilled in pitch-pipes and scales.
translations.idiomatic: He knew writing somewhat and understood pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 在周，襲爵燕郡公，歷位魯陽太守、太子少宮尹、儀同三司、司武上士。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he inherited the dukedom of Yancheng and served as Administrator of Luyang, Junior Palace Master of the Heir Apparent, Equal in Honor with the Three Dukes, and Senior Master of Martial Display.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he inherited Yancheng, was Luyang administrator, junior palace master, equal in honor, and senior master of martial display.

sentences.zh: 時隋文帝為大司馬，賁知帝非常人，深自推結。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Jian was Grand Marshal; Ben knew he was no ordinary man and attached himself deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was grand marshal, Ben saw he was no ordinary man and attached himself deeply.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，加開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ben was given an Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ben received an opening office.

sentences.zh: 及文帝被顧托，群情未一，引賁置左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was entrusted on his deathbed and opinion was not yet united, he kept Ben at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen was entrusted on his deathbed and opinion was divided, he kept Ben close.

sentences.zh: 帝將之東第，百官皆不知所去，帝潛令賁部伍仗衛，因召公卿而謂曰：「欲富貴者當相隨來！

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to go to the Eastern Residence; the hundred officials did not know where to go; the Emperor secretly ordered Ben to array guards and weapons, then summoned the lords and said, "Whoever wants wealth and honor should follow me!
translations.idiomatic: About to go to the Eastern Residence while officials wavered, the emperor secretly had Ben array guards, then told the lords, "Who wants wealth and honor should follow me!

sentences.zh: 」往往偶語，欲有去就。

translations.literal: " People whispered among themselves, wanting to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Men whispered, unsure whether to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 賁嚴兵而至，眾莫敢動。

translations.literal: Ben came with stern troops and none dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Ben came with stern troops and none dared move.

sentences.zh: 出崇陽門至東宮，門者拒不內，賁諭之不去，瞋目叱之，門者遂卻。

translations.literal: They went out Chongyang Gate to the Eastern Palace; the gatekeepers refused entry; Ben urged them in vain, then glared and shouted, and the gatekeepers fell back.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongyang Gate the Eastern Palace gatekeepers refused entry; Ben urged, then shouted, and they fell back.

sentences.zh: 既而帝得入，賁恆典宿衛，承間進說以應天順人之事，帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then entered; Ben constantly directed the night guard and seized chances to urge responding to Heaven and following the people; the Emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, Ben ran the night guard and urged responding to Heaven and the people; the emperor followed.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，命賁清宮，因典宿衛。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he ordered Ben to clear the palace and again put him in charge of the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the throne he had Ben clear the palace and again run the night guard.

sentences.zh: 賁乃奏改周旗幟，更為嘉名，其青龍、騶虞、硃雀、玄武、千秋、萬歲之旗，皆賁所創也。

translations.literal: Ben memorialized to change Zhou banners and give them auspicious names; the Azure Dragon, Zouyu, Vermilion Bird, Black Tortoise, Thousand Autumns, and Ten Thousand Years banners were all his creations.
translations.idiomatic: Ben memorialized to change Zhou banners to auspicious names—the Azure Dragon, Zouyu, Vermilion Bird, Black Tortoise, Thousand Autumns, and Ten Thousand Years were all his.

sentences.zh: 尋拜散騎常侍，兼太子左庶子、左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Left Commander of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was regular attendant, left tutor of the heir, and left palace guard commander.

sentences.zh: 及高熲、蘇威共掌朝政，賁甚不平。

translations.literal: When Gao Jiong and Su Wei jointly held court power, Ben was very resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jiong and Su Wei held power together, Ben was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 時柱國劉昉被疏忌，賁諷昉及上柱國元諧、李詢、華州刺史張賓等謀黜熲、威，五人相與輔政。

translations.literal: At that time Pillar of State Liu Fang was kept at a distance; Ben urged Fang and Senior Pillar of State Yuan Xie, Li Xun, and Huazhou Inspector Zhang Bin to plot removing Jiong and Wei so the five could jointly assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar Liu Fang was estranged; Ben urged Fang, senior pillar Yuan Xie, Li Xun, and Huazhou inspector Zhang Bin to oust Jiong and Wei and rule together.

sentences.zh: 又以晉王上之愛子，謀行廢立。

translations.literal: They also plotted deposition and enthronement because the Prince of Jin was the emperor's beloved son.
translations.idiomatic: They also plotted to depose the heir because Prince of Jin was the emperor's favorite.

sentences.zh: 復私謂皇太子曰：「賁將數謁殿下，恐為上譴，願察區區之心。

translations.literal: He again told the Crown Prince privately, "Ben will often visit Your Highness and fears imperial blame; I beg you to discern my humble heart."
translations.idiomatic: He told the crown prince privately, "I shall often visit you and fear blame from above; please see my humble heart."

sentences.zh: 」謀泄，昉等委罪於賓、賁。

translations.literal: " When the plot leaked, Fang and the others laid blame on Bin and Ben.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked, Fang and the others blamed Bin and Ben.

sentences.zh: 公卿奏二人坐當死，帝以龍潛之舊，不忍加誅，並除名。

translations.literal: The lords memorialized that the two deserved death; the Emperor, because of old ties from before he rose, could not bear to execute them and only struck their names from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The lords said both deserved death; the emperor, remembering ties before he rose, spared them and only struck their names.

sentences.zh: 賓未幾卒。

translations.literal: Bin died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Bin soon died.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，賁復爵位，檢校太常卿。

translations.literal: After more than a year Ben recovered his noble rank and was made Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Ben recovered rank and was acting grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 以古樂宮縣七八，損益不同，歷代通儒，議無定準，乃上表曰：「殷人以上，通用五音。

translations.literal: Because the ancient palace bell-stands numbered seven or eight and additions and reductions differed, and successive Confucians debated without fixed standard, he submitted a memorial saying, "From the Yin dynasty upward the five tones were used in common.
translations.idiomatic: Because palace bell-stands numbered seven or eight with no fixed standard, he memorialized, "From Yin upward five tones were common.

sentences.zh: 周武克殷，得鶉火天駟之應，其音用七。

translations.literal: When King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin he obtained the response of the Quail Fire and Heavenly Team—its pitch used seven.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou King Wu conquered Yin he got the Quail Fire and Heavenly Team response—seven tones.

sentences.zh: 漢興，加應鐘，故十六枚而在一虡。

translations.literal: When Han arose, the responding bell was added, so sixteen bells hung on one stand.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose the responding bell was added—sixteen bells on one stand.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注《周禮》，「二八十六為虡」，此則七八之義，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's note on the Rites of Zhou says, 'Two times eight is sixteen for a stand'—this is the meaning of seven or eight; it is of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan on the Rites of Zhou says two eights make sixteen on a stand—the seven-or-eight meaning is ancient.

sentences.zh: 然世有沿革，用舍不同。

translations.literal: Yet ages have had changes and use and abandonment differ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ages changed and use differed.

sentences.zh: 至周武帝復改縣七，以林鐘為宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou again changed the stand to seven and made the Forest Bell the keynote,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou again set seven bells and made Forest Bell keynote,

sentences.zh: 夫樂者，政之本也，故移風易俗，莫善於樂，是以吳劄觀而辯興亡。

translations.literal: music is the root of government; therefore to shift custom and change practice nothing is better than music—hence Wu Zha watched and distinguished rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: music is the root of government; to shift custom nothing beats music—hence Wu Zha watched and judged rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 然則樂也者，所以動天地，感鬼神，情發於聲，安危斯應。

translations.literal: Thus music moves Heaven and earth and touches ghosts and spirits; feeling bursts into sound and safety or peril responds.
translations.idiomatic: Music moves heaven and earth and touches spirits; feeling becomes sound and safety or peril responds.

sentences.zh: 周武以林鐘為宮，蓋將亡之征也。

translations.literal: Zhou Wu's taking Forest Bell as keynote was surely a sign of impending ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wu's Forest Bell keynote was a sign of ruin.

sentences.zh: 且林鐘之管，即黃種下生之義。

translations.literal: Moreover the Forest Bell pipe is precisely the meaning of Yellow Bell generating below.
translations.idiomatic: The Forest Bell pipe is Yellow Bell generating below.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘，君也，而生於臣，明於皇朝九五之應。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell is the ruler, yet generated from the subject—clear in the imperial house's correspondence to the nine-five.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell is ruler yet generated from subject—clear for the house's nine-five.

sentences.zh: 又陰者臣也，而居君位，更顯國家登極之祥。

translations.literal: Yin is the subject yet occupies the ruler's position—further showing the state's omen of ascending the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, the subject, occupies the ruler's place—further showing the throne omen.

sentences.zh: 斯實冥數相符，非關人事。

translations.literal: This truly matches hidden numbers and is not a matter of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This matches hidden numbers, not human affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣聞五帝不相沿樂，三王不相襲禮，此蓋隨時改制而不失雅正者也。

translations.literal: I have heard that the Five Emperors did not continue one another's music and the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites—this is surely reforming institutions to the times without losing elegant correctness.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Five Emperors did not continue one another's music nor the Three Kings one another's rites—reforming to the times without losing correctness.

sentences.zh: 」帝竟從之，改七縣八，黃鐘為宮。

translations.literal: " The Emperor in the end followed him, changed seven stands to eight, and made Yellow Bell the keynote.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed, changed seven stands to eight, and made Yellow Bell keynote.

sentences.zh: 詔賁與儀同楊慶和刊定周、齊音律。

translations.literal: He ordered Ben together with Equal-in-Honor Yang Qinghe to revise Zhou and Qi pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Ben and equal-in-honor Yang Qinghe to revise Zhou and Qi pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 未幾，曆郢、虢、懷三州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he served in succession as Inspector of Ying, Guo, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was inspector of Ying, Guo, and Huai in turn.

sentences.zh: 在懷州決沁水東注，名曰利人渠，又派入溫縣，名曰溫潤渠，以溉舄咸，人賴其利。

translations.literal: At Huai he diverted the Qin River east—calling it the Benefit-the-People Canal—and sent a branch into Wen County as the Warm-Moist Canal to irrigate salty fields; people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: At Huai he diverted the Qin east as the Benefit-the-People Canal and into Wen as the Warm-Moist Canal to irrigate salty fields.

sentences.zh: 後為齊州刺史，糶官米而自糶，坐除名。

translations.literal: Later as Inspector of Qi he sold official grain for himself and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Later as Qi inspector he sold official grain for himself and was struck off.

sentences.zh: 後從幸洛陽，帝從容謂曰：「我始為大司馬，及總百揆，頻繁左右，與卿足為恩舊。

translations.literal: Later following the emperor to Luoyang, the Emperor said at ease, "When I first was Grand Marshal and then directed all affairs, I kept you constantly at my side—we were truly old friends in grace.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Luoyang the emperor said, "When I was grand marshal and directed all affairs I kept you at my side—we were old friends in grace.

sentences.zh: 卿若無過，位與高熲齊。

translations.literal: Had you been without fault, your rank would have equaled Gao Jiong's.
translations.idiomatic: Without fault your rank would have equaled Gao Jiong's.

sentences.zh: 坐與凶人交構，由是廢黜。

translations.literal: Because you associated with wicked men you were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Because you joined wicked men you were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 言念疇昔之恩，復處牧伯之位，何乃不思報效，以至於此！

translations.literal: Thinking of past grace, I again gave you a shepherd's post—why did you not think to repay and come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Remembering past grace I gave you a province again—why not repay instead of this!

sentences.zh: 吾不忍殺卿，是屈法申私耳。

translations.literal: I could not bear to kill you; that was bending the law to show private favor.
translations.idiomatic: I could not kill you—that was bending law for private favor.

sentences.zh: 」賁俯伏陳謝。

translations.literal: " Ben prostrated himself and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Ben prostrated and apologized.

sentences.zh: 詔復本官。

translations.literal: An edict restored his original office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his office.

sentences.zh: 後數日，對詔失旨，又自敘功績，有怨言。

translations.literal: Several days later, in audience he missed the mark; he again recounted his merits and had resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: Days later in audience he missed the mark, recounted merits, and spoke with resentment.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謂群臣曰：「吾將與賁一州，觀此，不可復用。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and told the lords, "I was going to give Ben one province—seeing this, he cannot be used again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and told the lords, "I would give Ben one province—seeing this, he cannot be used again."

sentences.zh: 後皇太子為其言曰：「此輩並有佐命功，雖性行輕險，誠不可棄。

translations.literal: Later the Crown Prince spoke for him, saying, "These men all had merit in establishing the mandate; though their conduct is frivolous and dangerous, they truly cannot be cast away."
translations.idiomatic: Later the crown prince said, "These men helped establish the mandate; though frivolous, they should not be cast away."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我抑屈之，全其命也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I have bent them down and preserved their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I bent them down and kept them alive.

sentences.zh: 微劉昉、鄭譯及賁、柳裘、皇甫績等，則我不至此。

translations.literal: But for Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and Ben, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the like, I would not be here.
translations.idiomatic: Without Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, Ben, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the like I would not be here.

sentences.zh: 然此等皆反覆子也。

translations.literal: Yet such men are all turncoats.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are all turncoats.

sentences.zh: 當周宣帝時，以無賴得幸。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuan of Zhou's time they gained favor through rascality.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Emperor Xuan they gained favor through rascality.

sentences.zh: 及帝大漸，顏之儀等請以趙王輔政，此輩行詐，顧命於我。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was gravely ill, Yan Zhiyi and others asked that the Prince of Zhao assist in government; this crowd acted fraudulently and entrusted the mandate to me.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was gravely ill, Yan Zhiyi asked the Prince of Zhao to assist; this crowd cheated and entrusted the mandate to me.

sentences.zh: 我將為政，又欲亂之，故昉謀大逆於前，譯為巫蠱於後。

translations.literal: When I was about to govern they wanted to throw it into chaos again—hence Fang's great treason before and Yi's witchcraft after.
translations.idiomatic: When I was about to govern they wanted chaos again—hence Fang's treason before and Yi's witchcraft after.

sentences.zh: 如賁之例，皆不滿志，任之則不遜，致之則怨，自難信也，非我棄之。

translations.literal: Men like Ben were all dissatisfied; employ them and they are insubordinate, send them away and they resent—hard to trust; it is not that I cast them away.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ben were dissatisfied; employed they were insubordinate, sent away they resented—hard to trust; I did not cast them away lightly.

sentences.zh: 眾人見此，或有竊議，謂我薄于功臣，斯不然矣。

translations.literal: Those who see this sometimes whisper that I was stingy toward merit—men—that is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some whisper I was stingy toward merit—that is not so.

sentences.zh: 」蘇威進曰：「漢光武欲全功臣，皆以列侯奉朝請，至尊仁育，復用此道以安之。

translations.literal: Su Wei advanced and said, "Emperor Guangwu of Han wished to preserve his merit-holders and all made them marquises attending court; Your Majesty's humane nurture may again use this way to settle them."
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei said, "Han Guangwu wished to preserve merit-holders as marquises attending court; Your Majesty may use that way to settle them."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "So."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So."

sentences.zh: 」遂廢，卒於家。

translations.literal: " He was then dismissed and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and died at home.

sentences.zh: 勇字季禮，景裕從弟也。

translations.literal: Yong, styled Jili, was a cousin of Jingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, styled Jili, was Jingyu's cousin.

sentences.zh: 父璧，魏下邳太守。

translations.literal: Father Bi was Administrator of Xiapi under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi was Wei's Xiapi administrator.

sentences.zh: 勇初與景裕俱在學，其叔同曰：「白頭必以文通，季禮當以武達。

translations.literal: Yong at first studied with Jingyu; their uncle Tong said, "The white-haired one will excel through letters, Jili will reach the martial way.
translations.idiomatic: Yong first studied with Jingyu; uncle Tong said, "The white-haired will excel in letters, Jili in arms.

sentences.zh: 興吾門者，二子也。

translations.literal: To raise our house—these two sons."
translations.idiomatic: To raise our house—these two."

sentences.zh: 」幽州反者僕骨邢以勇為本郡范陽王，時年十八。

translations.literal: The Youzhou rebel Pugu Xing made Yong King of Fanyang for the commandery when he was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou rebel Pugu Xing made Yong King of Fanyang at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 後葛榮又以勇為燕王。

translations.literal: Later Ge Rong also made Yong King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ge Rong also made him King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 齊神武起兵，盧文偉召之，不應。

translations.literal: When Qi Emperor Shenwu raised troops, Lu Wenwei summoned him and he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Emperor Shenwu raised troops, Lu Wenwei summoned him and he did not come.

sentences.zh: 爾硃氏滅，乃赴晉陽。

translations.literal: After the Erzhu clan was destroyed he went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Erzhu were destroyed he went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 神武署丞相主簿。

translations.literal: Shenwu appointed him Chief Clerk in the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu made him chief clerk in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 屬山西霜儉，運山東租輸，皆令實載，違者罪之。

translations.literal: When Shanxi had frost and famine, transport of Shandong rent was ordered—all loads must be full; violators were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanxi had frost famine, Shandong rent was transported—loads must be full or punished.

sentences.zh: 令勇典其事。

translations.literal: Yong was ordered to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was ordered to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 鄉郡公主虛僦千餘車，勇劾之。

translations.literal: The commandery princess of Xiangjun falsely hired more than a thousand carts; Yong impeached her.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangjun commandery princess falsely hired 1,000+ carts; Yong impeached her.

sentences.zh: 公主訴于神武，而勇守法不虧。

translations.literal: The princess complained to Shenwu, yet Yong held to the law without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: She complained to Shenwu, yet Yong held to law.

sentences.zh: 神武謂郭秀曰：「盧勇懍懍，有不可犯色，真公人也。

translations.literal: Shenwu told Guo Xiu, "Lu Yong is stern and has an air no one may offend—truly a public man.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu told Guo Xiu, "Lu Yong is stern and unoffendable—a true public man.

sentences.zh: 方當委之大事，豈止納租而已。

translations.literal: " He was about to entrust him with great affairs—not only collecting rent.
translations.idiomatic: I shall entrust great affairs—not only rent."

sentences.zh: 」後行洛州事。

translations.literal: Later he acted for Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he acted for Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 元象初，官軍圍廣州，未拔，行台侯景聞西魏救兵將至，集諸將議之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the imperial army besieged Guangzhou without taking it; Mobile Secretariat Hou Jing, hearing Western Wei relief was coming, gathered the generals to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanxiang's opening the army besieged Guangzhou; Hou Jing, hearing Western Wei relief was near, called the generals.

sentences.zh: 勇請進觀形勢，於是率百騎，各攏一馬。

translations.literal: Yong asked to advance and observe the situation; he then led a hundred horsemen, each leading a spare horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yong asked to scout; he led a hundred horsemen, each with a spare horse.

sentences.zh: 至大騩山，知西魏將李景和將至。

translations.literal: Reaching Mount Daqiu, he learned Western Wei General Li Jinghe was coming.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Daqiu he learned Li Jinghe was coming.

sentences.zh: 勇乃多置幡旗於樹頭，分騎為數十隊，鳴角直前。

translations.literal: Yong set many banners on treetops, divided the horsemen into dozens of squads, sounded horns, and charged straight ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Yong set banners in trees, split into dozens of squads, sounded horns, and charged.

sentences.zh: 禽西魏儀同程華，斬儀同王征蠻而還。

translations.literal: He captured Western Wei Equal-in-Honor Cheng Hua, beheaded Equal-in-Honor Wang Zhengman, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He captured equal-in-honor Cheng Hua, beheaded equal-in-honor Wang Zhengman, and returned.

sentences.zh: 再遷陽州刺史，鎮宜陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Inspector of Yang and garrisoned Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Yang inspector and garrisoned Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 叛人韓木蘭、陳忻等常為邊患，勇大破之。

translations.literal: Rebels Han Mulan and Chen Xin were constant border troubles; Yong routed them badly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels Han Mulan and Chen Xin troubled the border; Yong routed them.

sentences.zh: 啟求入朝，神武賜勇書曰：「吾委卿陽州，安枕高臥，無西南之慮矣。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to enter court; Shenwu sent Yong a letter saying, "I entrusted you with Yangzhou to sleep on high pillows without worry for the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to enter court; Shenwu wrote, "I entrusted Yangzhou to you to sleep high without southwest worry.

sentences.zh: 表啟宜停，當使漢兒之中，無在卿前者。

translations.literal: Memorials should stop—among the Han men none should rank before you."
translations.idiomatic: Stop memorials—among Han men none should rank before you."

sentences.zh: 」卒，年三十二。

translations.literal: He died at thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 勇有馬五百匹，私造甲仗，遺啟盡獻之。

translations.literal: Yong had five hundred horses and privately made armor and weapons; in his final memorial he presented them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had 500 horses and private armor; his final memorial presented all.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、冀州刺史，諡武貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works and Inspector of Ji with posthumous title Wuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously minister of works and Ji inspector, posthumous title Wuzhen.

sentences.zh: 誕本名恭祖。

translations.literal: Dan was originally named Gongzu.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was originally named Gongzu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖晏，博學，善隸書，有名於世；

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Yan was erudite, skilled in clerical script, and famed in the world;
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Yan was erudite, skilled in clerical script, famed in the world;

sentences.zh: 仕慕容氏，位給事黃門侍郎，營丘、成周二郡守。

translations.literal: he served the Murong clan as Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Yingqiu and Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: he served Murong as yellow-gate attendant and Yingqiu and Chengzhou administrator.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，太子洗馬；

translations.literal: Grandfather Shou was Crown Prince's Reader;
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Shou was crown prince's reader;

sentences.zh: 慕容氏滅，入魏為魯郡守。

translations.literal: when the Murong fell he entered Wei as Administrator of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: when Murong fell he entered Wei as Lu administrator.

sentences.zh: 父叔仁，年十八，州辟主簿，舉秀才，除員外郎。

translations.literal: Father Shuren at eighteen was summoned as commandery chief clerk, nominated as Outstanding Talent, and made Extra Gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Father Shuren at eighteen was commandery chief clerk, nominated outstanding talent, made extra gentleman;

sentences.zh: 以親老乃辭歸就養。

translations.literal: because his parents were old he declined and returned to nurture them.
translations.idiomatic: his parents were old so he declined and returned to nurture them.

sentences.zh: 父母既沒哀毀六年，躬營墳壟，遂有終焉之志。

translations.literal: After both parents died he mourned in devastation six years, personally built the tombs, and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: After they died he mourned six years, built tombs himself, and meant to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 景明中，被征入洛，授武賁中郎將，非其好也。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he was summoned to Luoyang and made Martial Tiger Guard Central Commander—not his liking.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming he was summoned to Luoyang as martial tiger central commander—not his liking.

sentences.zh: 尋除鎮遠將軍、通直散騎常侍，並稱疾不朝。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Pacifying-the-Distant General and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and both times claimed illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon pacifying-distant general and regular attendant—both times illness kept him from court.

sentences.zh: 乃出為幽州司馬，又辭歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He then went out as Youzhou Marshal and again declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Youzhou marshal and again returned home.

sentences.zh: 當時咸稱其高尚焉。

translations.literal: At the time all praised his lofty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All praised his lofty conduct.

sentences.zh: 誕於度世為族弟。

translations.literal: Dan was a clansman cousin of Dushi.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was cousin to Dushi.

sentences.zh: 幼而通亮，博學，有祠彩。

translations.literal: Clever and bright from youth, erudite, with literary color.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, erudite, with literary color.

sentences.zh: 郡辟功曹，州舉秀才，不得。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as Merit Officer; the province nominated him as Outstanding Talent—he did not obtain office.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery summoned him as merit officer; province nominated outstanding talent—he did not obtain office.

sentences.zh: 起家侍御史，累遷輔國大將軍、太中大夫、幽州別駕、北豫州都督府長史。

translations.literal: He began as Attending Censor, rose to Assistant-to-the-State General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Youzhou Deputy Governor, and Chief Clerk of the Beiyu Commander's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as attending censor, rose to assistant-state general, grand master, Youzhou deputy, and Beiyu headquarters chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時刺史高仲密以州歸西魏，遣大將軍李遠率軍赴援，誕與文武二千餘人奉候大軍。

translations.literal: When Inspector Gao Zhongmi surrendered the province to Western Wei and sent Grand General Li Yuan with an army to aid, Dan with civil and military officials—more than two thousand—received the great army.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered to Western Wei and Li Yuan came with troops, Dan with 2,000+ civil and military men received the army.

sentences.zh: 以功授鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，封固安縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Pacifying-the-East General and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, enfeoffed Marquis of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was pacifying-east general, grand master with golden seal, Marquis of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎侍郎，拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was added Regular Attendant and made Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon regular attendant and yellow-gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 魏帝詔曰：「經師易求，人師難得。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor edicted, "A classics teacher is easy to find; a human teacher is hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor edicted, "A classics teacher is easy; a human teacher is hard.

sentences.zh: 朕諸兒稍長，欲令卿為師。

translations.literal: My sons are growing; I wish to make you their teacher."
translations.idiomatic: My sons are growing; I wish you to teach them."

sentences.zh: 」於是親幸晉王第，敕晉王以下皆拜之於帝前，因賜名曰誕。

translations.literal: He thereupon personally visited the Prince of Jin's residence and ordered the Prince of Jin and below all to bow to him before the Emperor; he was therefore given the name Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the Prince of Jin's residence and ordered the prince and below to bow before the emperor; he was therefore named Dan.

sentences.zh: 加征東將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was added Pacifying-the-East General and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Added pacifying-east general and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 周文帝又以誕儒宗學府，為當世所推，乃拜國子祭酒，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Wen also, because Dan was a Confucian lineage head praised by the age, made him Director of the National University and advanced him to Chariot-and-Horse Grand General and Equal in Honor with the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, because Dan was a praised Confucian head, made him national university director and chariot-and-horse grand general, equal in honor.

sentences.zh: 恭帝二年，除秘書監，後以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong he was made Director of the Secretariat; later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gong year 2 he was secretariat director; later he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 論曰：盧玄緒業著聞，首應旌命，子孫繼跡，為世盛門。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Lu Xuan's inherited work was renowned; he was first to answer the imperial summons, and descendants followed in his tracks as a great house of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Lu Xuan's inherited fame led the summons; descendants followed as a great house.

sentences.zh: 其文武功列殆無足紀，而見重于時，聲高冠帶，蓋德業儒素有過人者。

translations.literal: Their civil and military achievements are scarcely worth recording, yet they were valued in their time and their fame topped the gentry—surely their virtue, work, and Confucian plainness surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Their civil and military deeds scarcely merit record, yet they were valued and famed among gentry—virtue and Confucian plainness surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 伯源兄弟亦有二方之風流，雅道家聲，諸子不逮。

translations.literal: Boyuan's brothers also had the elegance of two regions; their refined family voice—the sons did not match.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan's brothers had two-region elegance and refined family voice—the sons did not match.

sentences.zh: 思道一代俊偉，而宦途寥落，雖曰窮通有命，抑亦不護細行之所致乎！

translations.literal: Sidao was a peerless talent of an age, yet his official path was sparse; though one says fortune has its mandate, perhaps it was also from not guarding small conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao was an age's peerless talent yet sparse in office; though fortune has mandate, perhaps not guarding small conduct.

sentences.zh: 潛及昌衡，雅素之紀，家風克嗣，堂構無虧。

translations.literal: Qian and Changheng were models of refined plainness; family style was well continued and the hall frame unimpaired.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and Changheng modeled refined plainness; family style continued and the frame unimpaired.

sentences.zh: 子剛使酒誕節，蓋亦明珠之類。

translations.literal: Zigang's wine-besotted eccentricity was still of the bright-pearl kind.
translations.idiomatic: Zigang's wine eccentricity was still bright-pearl kind.

sentences.zh: 長仁諫說可重，一簣而傾，惜矣！

translations.literal: Changren's remonstrance was weighty—one basket-tip and it toppled; pity!
translations.idiomatic: Changren's remonstrance was weighty—one basket-tip and toppled; pity!

sentences.zh: 伯舉、仲宣，文雅俱劭。

translations.literal: Boju and Zhongxuan were both strong in refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Boju and Zhongxuan were both strong in refinement.

sentences.zh: 叔彪志尚宏遠，任俠好謀。

translations.literal: Shubiao's aims were broad and far; he delighted in chivalry and loved stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Shubiao aimed broad and far, delighted in chivalry and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 文偉望重地華，早有志尚，間關夷險之際，終遇英雄之主，雖禮秩未弘，亦為佐命之一也。

translations.literal: Wenwei's standing was weighty and his land splendid; he had early resolve; through straits of hardship he at last met a heroic lord—though rank was not grand, he was still one who aided the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei's standing was weighty with early resolve; through hardship he met a heroic lord—rank not grand, yet one who aided the mandate.

sentences.zh: 詢祖辭情豔發，早著聲名，負其才地，肆情矜矯，位遇未聞，弱年夭逝。

translations.literal: Xunzu's words were brilliant and he gained fame early; trusting his talent and station, he indulged pride—office never heard of him, and he died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzu's words were brilliant and fame early; trusting talent he indulged pride—no office heard, young death.

sentences.zh: 若得終介眉壽，通塞未可量焉。

translations.literal: Had he lived to full years, whether blocked or open could not be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Had he lived full years, blocked or open could not be measured.

sentences.zh: 叔倫質器洪厚，卷舒兼濟。

translations.literal: Shulun's substance was vast and thick, bending and extending together.
translations.idiomatic: Shulun's substance was vast, bending and extending together.

sentences.zh: 子章殘忍為志，咎之徒也。

translations.literal: Zizhang's cruelty was his aim—the kind that brings blame.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang aimed at cruelty—the blameworthy kind.

sentences.zh: 景裕兄弟，雅業可宗，雖擇木異邦，而立名俱劭。

translations.literal: Jingyu's brothers had elegant work worth honoring; though they chose different trees in different states, they both made strong names.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu's brothers had elegant work worth honor; though in different states, both made strong names.

sentences.zh: 辯捐益成務，其殆優乎。

translations.literal: Bian's additions and reductions completed the task—perhaps he was superior.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's additions completed the task—perhaps superior.

sentences.zh: 勇雖文武異趣，各其美也。

translations.literal: Yong, though civil and martial differed in bent, each had its beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, civil and martial differing, each had beauty.

sentences.zh: 賁二三其德，雖取悅於報己，而移之在我，亦安能其罵人。

translations.literal: Ben's fickleness, though pleasing those who repaid him, when shifted to himself—how could he still revile others?
translations.idiomatic: Ben's fickleness pleased those who repaid him, yet shifted to himself—how revile others?

sentences.zh: 見遣末路，尚何足怪？

translations.literal: Driven off at the end of the road—what wonder?
translations.idiomatic: Driven off at the end—what wonder?

sentences.zh: 誕不殞儒業，亦足稱云。

translations.literal: Dan did not ruin Confucian work—that too is praise enough.
translations.idiomatic: Dan did not ruin Confucian work—that is praise enough.
